title: Warehouse Automation Strategies and Supply Chain Performance of Oil Servicing Firms in Port Harcourt
source: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF SOCIAL SCIENCES AND MANAGEMENT RESEARCH
summary: As technological advancements reshape business operations around the world, warehouse automation strategies have redefined supply chain performance. The study examined the relationship between warehouse automation strategies and the supply
content: As technological advancements reshape business operations around the world, warehouse automation strategies have redefined supply chain performance. The study examined the relationship between warehouse automation strategies and the supply chain performance of oil servicing firms in Port Harcourt. The inability of firms in developing economies to modernize their warehouse activities threatens the sustainability and overall performance. Addressing this gap, the study adopted the resource-based view (RBV) and diffusion of innovation (DOI) theory to extrapolate how warehouse automation strategies relate to the supply chain performance of oil servicing firms in Port Harcourt. And how technology moderates the relationship. Empirical data were gathered through copies of the questionnaire distributed among warehouse managers, production managers, operations managers, and logistics managers of the firms under review. And the results revealed that all dimensions of warehouse automation strategies relate positively with measures of supply chain performance; however, technology does not moderate the relationship between warehouse automation strategies and supply chain performance of oil servicing firms in Port Harcourt. Hence, the study concludes that the adoption of warehouse automation strategies improves the supply chain performance of oil servicing firms in Port Harcourt. Therefore, the study recommends that oil servicing firms in Port Harcourt should invest in modern automation technologies to ensure adequate inventory tracking, automated storage and retrieval systems to improve supply chain visibility, and responsiveness.

title: Process Evaluation of Ironmaking Using In-Flight Hydrogen Plasma Reduction of Partially Pre-reduced Iron Ore
summary: This work evaluates a hybrid ironmaking process that combines hydrogen direct reduction with in-flight hydrogen plasma reduction of iron ore powder using a new reactor, Swin $${\text {H}_2^+}$$ . The reactor uses a non-transferred DC arc pl
content: This work evaluates a hybrid ironmaking process that combines hydrogen direct reduction with in-flight hydrogen plasma reduction of iron ore powder using a new reactor, Swin $${\text {H}_2^+}$$ . The reactor uses a non-transferred DC arc plasma torch with continuous powder injection and was tested with up to 41 kW of electrical power and 9% $$\text {H}_\text {2}$$ -Ar plasma gas. The results suggest that controlling particle residence time is a major challenge for co-current in-flight plasma reactors. As a result, the optimal level of pre-reduction for in-flight systems differs from that for molten-bath reactors. Plasma-reduced iron was found to be less susceptible to reoxidation than direct-reduced iron. However, the current reactor design experienced product losses (>90%), limited metallization (<10%), and high specific energy consumption ( $$\approx$$ 67 kWh/kg of ore, before heat recovery).

title: Livelihood-led Environmental Degradation and its Consequences for Habitability of the Area Around Lake Chivero, Zimbabwe: A Systematic Review
source: Kuveza neKuumba The Zimbabwe Ezekiel Guti University Journal of Design Innovative Thinking and Practice
summary: This systematic review examines how livelihood activities relate to environmental degradation in the Lake Chivero Catchment Area, Zimbabwe, and evaluates the impacts on the area‘s longterm habitability. Motivated by the lake‘s serious ecolo
content: This systematic review examines how livelihood activities relate to environmental degradation in the Lake Chivero Catchment Area, Zimbabwe, and evaluates the impacts on the area‘s longterm habitability. Motivated by the lake‘s serious ecological decline over the past 30 years, despite being a vital water source for over 2.4 million people, a population 10 times its original capacity, the study employs the Social-Ecological Systems (SES) Framework and Institutional Analysis and Development (IAD) Framework. It synthesizes evidence from 67 peer-reviewed studies found through a systematic search of the Scopus, Google Scholar and Web of Science databases, following PRISMA guidelines. Results show that livelihood activities, such as sand mining, brick moulding, urban farming and informal waste disposal, although providing short-term survival benefits, have collectively caused significant environmental harm. Indicators reveal a reduction in lake depth from 28 to 18 metres, an elevenfold increase in nutrient inflows between 2000 and 2012 and sedimentation filling 18% of the lake‘s capacity. Institutional failures, including weak enforcement of environmental laws, underfunded sewage systems and poor governance, have worsened these ecological stresses. The review advocates a comprehensive intervention plan that includes infrastructure upgrades, enforcement of the polluter-pays principle, alternative livelihoods and ecological restoration to prevent a predicted ―2050 Doomsday Scenario‖ in which the lake may become unusable. Without such integrated efforts, the study warns that the lake‘s habitability will remain critically endangered, risking human health and ecological stability.

title: Biological production of synthetic aviation fuels (SAFs) from biomass
summary: Abstract Synthetic aviation fuels (SAFs) produced from biological routes are emerging as a practical way to decarbonize the aviation sector. This review summarizes progress in producing jet-range molecules from renewable carbon and benchmar
content: Abstract Synthetic aviation fuels (SAFs) produced from biological routes are emerging as a practical way to decarbonize the aviation sector. This review summarizes progress in producing jet-range molecules from renewable carbon and benchmarks them against the Jet A and Jet A-1 property window defined by the standard specification for aviation turbine fuels (ASTM D1655). We group candidates into three families, fatty acid-derived streams, alcohol-based precursors, and isoprenoid-derived hydrocarbons, and map their properties and upgrading chemistry to the standard specification for aviation turbine fuel containing synthesized hydrocarbons (ASTM D7566) certification framework. We survey diverse microbial hosts on renewable feedstocks and highlight advances in pathway and chassis engineering and bioprocess intensification that raise titers, productivities, and carbon efficiency. Together, these advances chart a practical route to certified, scalable, and cost-competitive SAF supply.

title: Organic fluorescent metal ion probes for understanding design rules photophysical mechanisms and bioimaging applications
summary: Organic fluorescent probes are widely used for metal-ion detection, yet many reviews remain descriptive and do not explain why different metal ions produce different fluorescence responses. This review addresses that gap by connecting metal
content: Organic fluorescent probes are widely used for metal-ion detection, yet many reviews remain descriptive and do not explain why different metal ions produce different fluorescence responses. This review addresses that gap by connecting metal-ion electronic structure, coordination behavior, and photophysical signal generation for Cu 2+ , Zn 2+ , Fe 3+ , Hg 2+ and Pb 2+ . The central argument is that probe performance depends not only on fluorophore design, but on the compatibility between the target ion and the sensing mechanism. Paramagnetic ions such as Cu 2+ and Fe 3+ usually promote fluorescence quenching through non-radiative decay, intersystem crossing, and charge-transfer pathways, whereas diamagnetic Zn 2+ more readily supports turn-on emission through PET suppression and chelation-induced rigidification. Soft heavy metals such as Hg 2+ and Pb 2+ require carefully selected donor atoms and receptor geometries to balance strong binding, selectivity, and signal reliability. This review compares PET, ICT/TICT, CHEF/CHEQ, ESIPT, energy-transfer, and aggregation-based mechanisms in terms of sensitivity, selectivity, reversibility, water compatibility, and bioimaging utility. The role of DFT and TD-DFT is also discussed as a supporting tool for validating binding modes and excited-state behavior. Overall, this review provides mechanism-guided design principles for developing more selective, photostable, water-compatible, and biologically useful fluorescent metal-ion probes.

title: Optimal control models with random switches and applications to economics and management
summary: Abstract This survey examines the role of stochastic switching times in optimal control theory with a particular emphasis on applications in economics and management. We start with a review of the problem’s formulation and early foundationa
content: Abstract This survey examines the role of stochastic switching times in optimal control theory with a particular emphasis on applications in economics and management. We start with a review of the problem’s formulation and early foundational contributions, followed by an outline of the general model framework. We highlight the structural key components and illustrate the sequence of decision stages. Two main methodological approaches are explored: a backward solution technique and an age-structured (vintage) optimal control formulation. We analyze how both approaches inform the determination and characterization of switching times in the dynamic optimization nexus. The survey further illustrates the relevance of random switching dynamics by applications in environmental economics, health economics and other related domains. Finally, we discuss current challenges and avenues for future research, including the incorporation of multiple switching events, agent heterogeneity, and the consideration of smaller shocks that occur frequently, almost continuously. This synthesis aims to provide both a rigorous theoretical perspective and a practical applied viewpoint on switching times–as critical components of decision-making in economics, finance, management and the broader social sciences–by leveraging mathematical modelling, analytical methods and computational techniques.

title: Mesostigmata mite assemblages in stands developed on former agricultural land
summary: Afforestation of post-agricultural land plays a crucial role in restoring forest soil properties and initiating secondary succession processes driven by soil biota. In this study, we compared Mesostigmata communities in even-aged (21 y./o.)
content: Afforestation of post-agricultural land plays a crucial role in restoring forest soil properties and initiating secondary succession processes driven by soil biota. In this study, we compared Mesostigmata communities in even-aged (21 y./o.) stands of Alnus glutinosa, Betula pendula, Picea abies, Pinus sylvestris, and Tilia cordata established on a former agricultural lands, and adjacent fallow field as a reference habitat, located near the Żelazny Most tailings storage facility (Lubin Forest District, Poland). Soil sampling was conducted on 18 study sites (5 tree species and fallow field × 3 plots) using steel corer (0-15 cm depth), consisting of 90 samples (5 samples from each plot). In total, 592 mesostigmatid mites representing 39 taxa and 15 families were recorded. Community structure differed among habitats, with Alnus glutinosa supporting the highest abundance and diversity, while Tilia cordata exhibited the lowest values. Deciduous stands generally hosted richer and more abundant assemblages than coniferous stands and the fallow field. The occurrence of both widespread generalists and highly specialized species highlights clear habitat differentiation and varying degrees of ecological specialization, reflecting differences in soil restoration processes among tree species.

title: High-Resolution Boundary-Layer Detection Lidar for Spaceborne Applications: Parameter Design, Theoretical Simulation, and Airborne Validation
summary: Abstract. The planetary boundary layer height (PBLH) is a key parameter for studying global land-atmosphere interactions, weather forecasting, and climate change. However, owing to the limited adaptability of existing detection techniques o
content: Abstract. The planetary boundary layer height (PBLH) is a key parameter for studying global land-atmosphere interactions, weather forecasting, and climate change. However, owing to the limited adaptability of existing detection techniques over complex terrain and the lack of observational consistency across different environments, unified and refined boundary layer observations on a global scale remain a major challenge. To support future spaceborne lidar missions for global boundary layer monitoring, this study establishes a closed-loop framework integrating spaceborne parameter design, theoretical simulation, and airborne experimental validation. As a core technical advance, a scaled airborne prototype was developed, and a synergistic terrain-atmosphere detection regime was introduced. By synchronously acquiring surface elevation and atmospheric backscatter signals, the system can directly retrieve the boundary layer height relative to the actual ground surface, namely above ground level (AGL), thereby fundamentally mitigating the terrain-matching bias of conventional approaches. System performance was primarily validated through the Yulin nighttime flight experiment, where the retrieved BLH showed a median difference of 10 m and a maximum RMSE of 45 m relative to the ground-based reference. The additional Hainan daytime flight experiment indicated the system's detection potential under strong background illumination and complex cloud conditions. This study validates the performance of the airborne prototype and provides empirical evidence for the parameter design of future spaceborne detection systems, supporting the construction of a globally consistent and high-precision boundary layer observation network.

title: Multi-Model Analysis for Policy in Agricultural Economics: A Conceptual Framework
summary: The complexity of the issues that practitioners in the field of agricultural economics encounter is increasing, with agriculture intersecting with most of the challenges that society faces.Policies related to agriculture need to address an
content: The complexity of the issues that practitioners in the field of agricultural economics encounter is increasing, with agriculture intersecting with most of the challenges that society faces.Policies related to agriculture need to address an increasing number of objectives, while at the same time it is necessary to understand their related trade-offs.How can policy analysts make use of the available quantitative tools to support an evidence-based policymaking process?In this context, collaborative approaches are increasingly recognised as a vital solution.This paper provides a framework for conducting multi-model analysis for policy and encourages its use in the field of agricultural economics.The following elements are crucial to the success of this method: (i) the development of clear conceptual frameworks identifying the core elements of the problem at hand; (ii) the cooperation between researchers in different fields (or modelling teams); (iii) the identification of synergies and overlaps between models; and (iv) the development of linkages between modelling tools in a largely structured manner.Overall, such an approach ensures that modelling outcomes satisfy policymakers' needs while keeping the modelling tools manageable.The synergistic use of models that are already well-tested in their respective fields enhances the credibility of the results.

title: Multifunctional applications of algae in environmental sustainability, food, agriculture, and biotechnology: current advances and future perspectives
source: World Journal of Biology Pharmacy and Health Sciences
summary: Algae represent a diverse and versatile group of photosynthetic organisms with considerable potential for addressing environmental, agricultural, nutritional, and industrial challenges. This review provides an overview of recent advances in
content: Algae represent a diverse and versatile group of photosynthetic organisms with considerable potential for addressing environmental, agricultural, nutritional, and industrial challenges. This review provides an overview of recent advances in algal biotechnology, with particular emphasis on the multifunctional applications of microalgae, macroalgae, and cyanobacteria in environmental sustainability, food and nutrition, agriculture, and health. In environmental applications, algae can serve as bioindicators of pollution and contribute to the removal of heavy metals, nutrients, and organic contaminants from wastewater and other contaminated environments. Their roles in nitrogen fixation, soil improvement, carbon sequestration, and the development of sustainable agricultural practices are also discussed. From a nutritional perspective, algae provide proteins, essential amino acids, polyunsaturated fatty acids, vitamins, minerals, dietary fiber, polysaccharides, and other bioactive compounds, supporting their incorporation into functional foods, fermented products, meat and dairy formulations, and cereal-based foods. Algal-derived compounds, including carotenoids, phycobiliproteins, polyphenols, polysaccharides, sterols, and bioactive peptides, have demonstrated antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, antidiabetic, and potential anticancer activities, although further clinical evidence is required to establish their therapeutic efficacy. The review also considers the potential of algae as sustainable sources of protein, biofuels, bioplastics, and other value-added bioproducts. Despite these advantages, challenges related to cultivation costs, harvesting, biomass processing, environmental variability, food safety, scalability, regulatory requirements, and economic feasibility continue to limit widespread commercialization. Future advances in strain improvement, integrated cultivation systems, algal–microbial interactions, resource recovery, and algal biorefineries may help overcome these limitations. Overall, algae represent promising biological platforms for developing circular and sustainable solutions across food production, agriculture, environmental management, and biotechnology.

title: Litter quality controls early decomposition rates and thus 14C cycling in old peat
summary: Additional 14 C input in ecosystems is often a concern in radiological assessments, and a secondary pathway exists through litter production and decomposition following atmospheric or belowground uptake of 14 C. To examine how litter qualit
content: Additional 14 C input in ecosystems is often a concern in radiological assessments, and a secondary pathway exists through litter production and decomposition following atmospheric or belowground uptake of 14 C. To examine how litter quality influences this process, a 90-day laboratory incubation was conducted using peat soil amended with labile litter, recalcitrant litter, or an equal mixed-litter treatment. Peat soils contain strongly 14 C-depleted carbon stocks, whereas fresh plant litter introduces modern carbon that enters biologically active pools during decomposition. Litter mass loss was used as an index of early decomposition and microbial processing. Litter treatment significantly affected mass loss (one-way ANOVA, p < 0.001). Labile litter showed the greatest decomposition (35%), whereas recalcitrant litter decomposed least (10%), with the mixed treatment intermediate (22%). Observed mass loss in the mixed treatment did not differ from the value expected from the two single-litter treatments, indicating an additive mixture effect. To interpret these results in a radiocarbon context, a conceptual framework of carbon pools was developed using previously determined percent modern carbon (pMC) values from the same peat system. Bulk peat represented an old carbon endmember, whereas dissolved organic carbon, microbial biomass, and dissolved inorganic carbon formed intermediate pools enriched relative to peat. The results indicate that fresh litter quality can rapidly regulate early decomposition rates and the transfer of modern carbon into active soil pools, even in 14 C-depleted peat. These findings highlight the need to consider fresh organic inputs, alongside peat age, when evaluating carbon cycling and 14 C transfer in peatland systems.

title: Advances in Biodegradation of petroleum hydrocarbons based pollutants by Microbes
source: Journal of Ethnobiology and Environmental Research
summary: Petroleum hydrocarbons are the organic contaminants that accumulate in different ecosystems due to their hydrophobic nature and limited bioavailability, which have raised concerns about their release into the environment. Due to their carci
content: Petroleum hydrocarbons are the organic contaminants that accumulate in different ecosystems due to their hydrophobic nature and limited bioavailability, which have raised concerns about their release into the environment. Due to their carcinogenic and neurotoxic nature a serious threat has been posed to human and environmental health. But the removal of these pollutants from the environment is a challenging task. Conventional treatment techniques like mechanical and chemical approaches are expensive and inefficient for eliminating hydrocarbons from contaminated areas. Bioremediation is a significant approach for the remediation of petroleum hydrocarbon-contaminated environments, using the natural biodegradation activity of microorganisms. Microorganisms that utilize petroleum hydrocarbons are prevalent in the environment. They naturally degrade pollutants and remove them from the environment. Biosurfactants lower surface tension, encourage emulsification, micelle formation, and make hydrocarbons bioavailable for microbial breakdown. So, utilising biosurfactant-producing bacteria can increase the effectiveness of bioremediation (Zhuang et al., 2022). This article provides an overview of bioremediation of petroleum hydrocarbon pollutants. Some crucial, but often overlooked factors which play a key role in the bioremediation are also elucidated. It also provides information about hydrocarbon metabolism in microorganisms with emphasis on new insights gained during the past couple of years. The main aim of this review is to provide a thorough understanding of the distinctive features of hydrocarbon microbiology that could be helpful in organizing further biodegradation studies. It also serves as a springboard for a broader discussion about the shortcomings and potential enhancements of the bioremediation techniques now in use.

title: Engineering Equitable Data Platforms: A Governance Framework for Algorithmic Fairness, Transparency, and Sustainable Decision-Making Infrastructure
source: East African Journal of Information Technology
summary: Data analytics platforms have evolved from internal business tools into critical infrastructure mediating access to economic opportunity across financial services, employment, retail, and civic life. While organisations typically evaluate t
content: Data analytics platforms have evolved from internal business tools into critical infrastructure mediating access to economic opportunity across financial services, employment, retail, and civic life. While organisations typically evaluate these platforms on narrow performance metrics revenue impact, operational efficiency, and decision velocity the platforms simultaneously encode assumptions about populations, replicate historical inequities, and amplify those inequities at the scale and speed of algorithmic decision-making. This article develops a multi-layer governance framework for engineering equitable data platforms, addressing algorithmic fairness, transparency and accountability, environmental sustainability, and the particular governance requirements of vulnerable and underrepresented populations. The article introduces a dual-gatekeeping model that distinguishes between restrictive gatekeeping in which data platforms entrench historical bias through biased training data and historical optimisation criteria and expansive gatekeeping in which platforms are intentionally designed to extend economic opportunity to previously excluded populations. The proposed governance framework integrates six operational dimensions: fairness metric definition and continuous monitoring, representative training data governance, pre-deployment bias testing, continuous post-deployment fairness auditing, data collection governance, and transparency and accountability mechanisms. The article further examines the environmental footprint of data platform infrastructure, arguing that sustainable platform governance must encompass energy accountability and lifecycle stewardship alongside fairness commitments. Finally, the article demonstrates convergence between fairness governance and strategic advantage, repositioning ethical platform design as an organisational imperative rather than a compliance burden. The framework is intended to be operationalizable by data architects, platform engineers, and organisational leaders responsible for consequential algorithmic decision systems.

title: Heavy Metal Determination and Risk Assessment of Selected Mushroom Species and their Substrates in South-eastern Nigeria
source: IIARD INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF GEOGRAPHY AND ENVIRONMENTAL MANAGEMENT
summary: Heavy metals (HMs) contaminate the environment and pose significant health risks to humans through accumulation in ecosystems, leading to toxicity and various diseases. This study assessed heavy metal contamination and associated risks in s
content: Heavy metals (HMs) contaminate the environment and pose significant health risks to humans through accumulation in ecosystems, leading to toxicity and various diseases. This study assessed heavy metal contamination and associated risks in selected mushroom species and their substrates across southeastern Nigeria. Using a stratified random sampling approach, representative mushroom and substrate samples were collected from five states: Abia, Anambra, Ebonyi, Enugu, and Imo. Soil chemical properties were analyzed using standard methods, while heavy metals were determined using an Atomic Absorption Spectrophotometer (Varian Spectra AA 200). Data were subjected to analysis of variance (ANOVA), and significant means were separated using Duncan’s Multiple Range Test (DMRT) at a 5% probability level. Results showed significant variations in heavy metal concentrations (Pb, Ni, Cr, Fe, and Cd) in both mushrooms and substrates, as well as in soil chemical properties (pH, organic carbon, organic matter, total nitrogen, total phosphorus, electrical conductivity, and cation exchange capacity) across species and sampling locations. The distribution of heavy metals followed the order Fe > Pb > Ni > Cr > Cd in oyster mushrooms and Fe > Pb > Ni > Cd > Cr in Agaricus species. Ebonyi State recorded the highest contamination levels for most heavy metals (Pb, Ni, Cd) in oyster mushrooms, followed by Anambra (Fe) and Abia (Cr). Similarly, Agaricus mushrooms from Ebonyi showed the highest contamination for Pb, Ni, Cr, and Cd, while Anambra recorded higher levels of Fe. For substrates, Agaricus samples from Enugu exhibited the highest pollution levels, whereas oyster mushroom substrates showed higher contamination in Abia (Pb and Cd) and Ebonyi (Ni), followed by Anambra (Fe). Although most risk assessment results indicated non-contaminated to low contamination levels suggesting that the studied locations are relatively safe continuous monitoring of heavy metal concentrations in biological tissues is recommended to prevent long-term bioaccumulation.

title: Green waste-to-biogas in Ghana’s urban markets: A comprehensive review of energy potential, opportunities, challenges, and policy frameworks
summary: Ghana, a developing nation, faces the dual crises of a persistent energy deficit and rapidly escalating municipal solid waste (MSW) generation. The country's energy supply is heavily dependent on traditional biomass, which contributes to de
content: Ghana, a developing nation, faces the dual crises of a persistent energy deficit and rapidly escalating municipal solid waste (MSW) generation. The country's energy supply is heavily dependent on traditional biomass, which contributes to deforestation and public health issues, while its waste management infrastructure struggles to keep pace with urbanization and economic growth. This literature review evaluates the technical, economic, and socio-political feasibility of converting green waste from Ghana's urban markets into a renewable energy source via anaerobic digestion (AD). Findings reveal that Ghana possesses an immense, largely untapped resource potential, with market waste exhibiting a composition and characteristics highly suitable for biochemical conversion. However, this potential is significantly hindered by a range of systemic barriers. These include the fundamental lack of source segregation, which compromises feedstock quality; a robust but weakly implemented policy and regulatory framework that fails to attract consistent private investment; and critical sociocultural and technical hurdles, such as low public awareness and a deficit of local technical expertise. This review argues that addressing these interconnected, non-technical barriers is crucial for unlocking the full potential of a waste-to-energy paradigm in Ghana. By synthesizing existing research and identifying key implementation and research gaps, this review provides a strategic roadmap for policymakers, investors, and civil society to transition from theoretical possibility to practical reality, fostering a circular economy that simultaneously enhances energy security, improves sanitation, and mitigates climate change.

title: Beyond Sustainability Narratives: A Forensic Algorithm for Verifying Governance and Environmental Data Integrity under IFRS S1 and IFRS S2
source: East African Journal of Business and Economics
summary: The regulatory enforcement of the International Sustainability Standards Board (ISSB) frameworks is forcing a mandatory transition in emerging-market corporate disclosure, moving reporting away from qualitative, public-relations-oriented na
content: The regulatory enforcement of the International Sustainability Standards Board (ISSB) frameworks is forcing a mandatory transition in emerging-market corporate disclosure, moving reporting away from qualitative, public-relations-oriented narratives and toward auditable, transaction-backed evidence. Under IFRS S1, entities must transparently disclose governance body composition and progress against stated targets, while IFRS S2 requires precise, financially material climate-related disclosures covering greenhouse gas emissions. Despite these mandates, no standardised, automated mechanism currently exists for verifying the transaction-level evidence that underlies such disclosures, leaving a persistent gap between what companies report and what can actually be audited in real time. This paper addresses that gap by developing and empirically demonstrating a unified Forensic Assurance Algorithm built from two original quantitative instruments: an adjusted Herfindahl-Hirschman Index, recalibrated from competition economics to a strict fifty-percent gender-parity baseline, used to evaluate governance concentration risk; and a multi-weighted, five-tier Data Quality Score that scores the systemic maturity of environmental data pipelines rather than the completeness of their narrative description. Working from a positivist research paradigm, the algorithm is applied to the public sustainability disclosures of Kakuzi PLC, a market-leading, transparently reporting agricultural enterprise selected specifically as an illustrative diagnostic anchor rather than as a representative of poor practice. The resulting diagnostic identifies a governance concentration index of 0.6250, a twenty-five percent variance above the parity benchmark that also breaches Kenya's own constitutional two-thirds gender rule, and an environmental data quality score of zero, reflecting complete reliance on retrospective, manually compiled spreadsheets. The paper concludes with a proposed automated data-engineering architecture intended to move corporate sustainability reporting toward continuous, audit-ready assurance in emerging markets.

title: Evaluate Operational Effectiveness of Waste Water Treatment Facility (WWTF) of a Petro - Chemical Plant in Port Harcourt
source: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF ENGINEERING AND MODERN TECHNOLOGY
summary: The aim of this study is to evaluate operational effectiveness of waste water treatment facility (WWTF) of a petro - chemical plant in Port Harcourt. In this study, the analysis is done in order to estimate waste water treatment facility op
content: The aim of this study is to evaluate operational effectiveness of waste water treatment facility (WWTF) of a petro - chemical plant in Port Harcourt. In this study, the analysis is done in order to estimate waste water treatment facility operational effectiveness and reliability using operational and experimental data from the petro chemical plant. The volumetric efficiency, energy efficiency, sludge production rate, performance indices and removal efficiency of BOD, COD, TSS and TDS is gotten using effective and reliability model. Thus, the data regarding the WWTF operated in Eleme petro chemical plant was collected from the works/maintenance department in (6) months period, before they will be further analyzed. Based on the explanatory results the operational effectiveness and reliability of the WWTF are determined. The research showed that the volumetric efficiency of the WWTF falls between 20%-59%, also, the energy consumption falls between 0.48kwh/m3-0.71kwh/m3, the energy consumption BOD5 removal falls between 2.9 kwh /kg -13.1kwh/kg, the highest sludge production is at the sixth month (F) which is 1.83kg/m3. Also, the removal efficiency of BOD for the 6 months is above 70%, for COD is between 50%-74%, for TSS is above 90% and for TDS is between 43% - 72%. This research work recommends Turn around maintenance (TAM) should be carried out in the waste water treatment facility to ensure the equipment is not damage.

title: The spillover effect of intelligent supply chain construction on green governance performance: based on the perspective of supply chain relationship
summary: We examine whether and how the Pilot Programme of Supply Chain Innovation and Application affects green governance of pilot firms’ suppliers. We find that intelligent supply chain construction generates positive green spillovers, improving
content: We examine whether and how the Pilot Programme of Supply Chain Innovation and Application affects green governance of pilot firms’ suppliers. We find that intelligent supply chain construction generates positive green spillovers, improving suppliers‘ green governance performance. The mechanisms operate through pressure, learning, and synergy effects along the supply chain. The effect is heterogeneous across supplier characteristics, industry, location, regional conditions, and supply chain structure. We also find that intelligent supply chain construction enhances suppliers’ future performance. This study provides a theoretical foundation and policy implications for strengthening intelligent supply chain systems and promoting the industry’s transformation towards high-end and green development.

title: Influence of rotor blade rotational speed on the spectrum and emission level of noise in the rotating system of the dual-use small Wabik helicopter
source: Eksploatacja i Niezawodnosc - Maintenance and Reliability
summary: The article analyzes how the rotational speed of the Wabik helicopter rotor affects both the overall noise level and its spectral characteristics. Measurements were performed in one third octave bands for two configurations: the rotor hub a
content: The article analyzes how the rotational speed of the Wabik helicopter rotor affects both the overall noise level and its spectral characteristics. Measurements were performed in one third octave bands for two configurations: the rotor hub alone and the complete rotor system with blades installed. This allowed clear separation of the hub noise from the aerodynamic noise generated by the blades and showed how both components depend on rotational speed. The results confirm that rotor speed strongly influences total noise emission and the spectral structure of the emitted sound, while at higher speeds the blades become a major noise source under piston engine operating conditions. The findings provide a basis for improving blade geometry, selecting optimal engine and rotor operating ranges, and reducing noise in the most critical frequency bands. The novelty of the work is the detailed one third octave analysis of a prototype custom designed Wabik rotor system at three rotational speeds.

title: Are the Benefits of Electrification Realized Only in the Long Run? Evidence from Rural India
summary: Experimental studies find smaller benefits of electrification than observational studies. Is this because the latter typically observe benefits after a longer period of time? Using three waves of data from the Human Development Profile of I
content: Experimental studies find smaller benefits of electrification than observational studies. Is this because the latter typically observe benefits after a longer period of time? Using three waves of data from the Human Development Profile of India and the Indian Household Development Survey of Indian rural households, we quantify the impacts of short-term (0-7 years) and long-term (7-17 years) electricity access on household well-being. We use a propensity-score-weighted-difference-in-differences design that controls for spillover effects and find that electricity access increases consumption and education in the long term, and reduces the time spent by women on fuel collection, although we do not find significant effects on agricultural income, agricultural land holding, and kerosene consumption. Per capita consumption grows by 18 percentage points more over seven years in the long-term connected group than in the control group. Short-term effects are smaller and not statistically significant for any outcome variable.

title: Three Decades of Energy Efficiency in Chile: Institutional Path Dependence and the Systemic Limits of Decoupling
summary: Energy efficiency (EE) is widely promoted as a climate-mitigation strategy, yet improvements in energy intensity emerge from interactions among institutions, technologies, economic structures, and environmental conditions and cannot be attr
content: Energy efficiency (EE) is widely promoted as a climate-mitigation strategy, yet improvements in energy intensity emerge from interactions among institutions, technologies, economic structures, and environmental conditions and cannot be attributed to efficiency policies alone. This study examines the evolution of EE governance in Chile between 1992 and 2022, treating national energy intensity as an emergent property of a path-dependent sociotechnical system. A two-component mixed-methods approach combines a historical-institutional reconstruction of governance with a parsimonious econometric analysis of short-run changes in energy intensity, integrated through a causal loop diagram. The historical analysis shows EE governance evolving through path dependence, critical junctures, layering, and policy feedback, strengthening state coordination without transforming the underlying market-oriented regime. Across four specifications, only carbon intensity is robustly associated with short-run changes in energy intensity; structural, extractive, and sociotechnical variables show no robust association. A comparison of the two strands reveals an asymmetry: the institutional trajectory coincided with aggregate change in the carbon–energy dimension, while no comparable short-run signature was detected along the direct demand-side routes examined. These findings reframe energy intensity as a system-level property and indicate that efficiency policies should be complemented by demand-side governance, structural change, and sufficiency to support sustainability transitions.

title: The Economics and Finance of the Green Transition
summary: The green transition is no longer simply a question of better technologies or stronger carbon prices. It is a question of whether decarbonisation can remain feasible, investable, and socially durable under volatility, geopolitical rivalry,
content: The green transition is no longer simply a question of better technologies or stronger carbon prices. It is a question of whether decarbonisation can remain feasible, investable, and socially durable under volatility, geopolitical rivalry, ecological limits, and distributional conflict. This book examines the transition as a systemic process shaped by bottlenecks, institutional capacity, and the interactionof policy, finance, and social legitimacy. Bringing together political economy, governance, and green finance, this book analyses how policy instruments, metrics, resilience, and risk architectures condition the pace and durability of transformation. It explores the design of policy mixes, the role of indicators as governance devices, and the architecture of de‑risking, market‑making, coordination, disclosure, and supervisory frameworks. The discussionalso addresses digital innovation, greenwashing risks, and the ways in which climate and regulatory uncertainty reshape capital allocation. Comparative evidence from the European Union, the United States, and China, together with analysis of European electricity markets, shows how transitionstrategies succeed or fail as constraints shift. Written for academics, policymakers, regulators, practitioners, and graduate students in economics, finance, and sustainability, this book offers a framework for understanding how the transition can be governed under turbulence. It provides tools for identifying binding constraints, evaluating resilience, and understanding how credibility, sequencing, and uncertainty affect investment. Rather than offeringa blueprint, it shows how transitions depend on managing sequences of constraints over time. Its central message is that a sustainable transition depends not on ambition alone, but on institutions capable of making long‑term commitment credible under structural uncertainty.

title: Industrial enzymatic hydrolysis of chicken viscera and bone materials: effect on protein recovery and product properties
summary: Enzymatic hydrolysis is an efficient strategy for valorizing chicken rest raw materials, yet the influence of industrially relevant process design on protein recovery and product functionality remains insufficiently described, especially fo
content: Enzymatic hydrolysis is an efficient strategy for valorizing chicken rest raw materials, yet the influence of industrially relevant process design on protein recovery and product functionality remains insufficiently described, especially for sediment fractions. This paper evaluates how key hydrolysis parameters affect protein recovery, degree of hydrolysis (DH), amino acid composition, and quality properties of hydrolysates and sediments from chicken viscera and bone materials. Eleven hydrolyses were performed using endogenous and commercial enzymes under varying pre-treatments, water additions, and hydrolysis times. Protein recovery in hydrolysates increased during the first 60 min, while DH continued to rise up to 120 min. For viscera, heating raw material to hydrolysis temperature accounted for 45–66% of total hydrolysate protein recovery, compared with 18%−30% for bone materials. Both viscera and bone hydrolysates achieved high protein contents. A substantial share of bone material proteins was recovered in sediments, characterized by lower DH and higher ash content. Thermal pre-inactivation of endogenous enzymes shifted protein recovery from hydrolysates to sediments, and reduced water addition decreased hydrolysate protein recovery and DH while increasing these parameters in sediments. The amino acid composition of hydrolysates and sediments reflected raw material composition. Viscera hydrolysates exhibited higher DH and superior emulsifying properties, whereas bone hydrolysates showed higher water-holding and oil-absorption capacities. These results demonstrate that targeted control of processing parameters is essential for influencing the distribution of protein between fractions and their properties. Both hydrolysates and sediments represent valuable protein products, emphasizing the need to consider the entire process when optimizing industrial enzymatic hydrolysis.

title: Identifying Green Bond Greenwashing Behavior Using Large Language Models: Evidence from China
summary: Green bonds, as an important financing tool for promoting the transition to a low-carbon economy, warrant attention to their actual environmental benefits. The existence of greenwashing behavior not only harms the interests of investors but
content: Green bonds, as an important financing tool for promoting the transition to a low-carbon economy, warrant attention to their actual environmental benefits. The existence of greenwashing behavior not only harms the interests of investors but may also undermine the credibility of the green financial market. This study takes the Chinese green bond market from 2016 to 2024 as the research object, introduces the BERT artificial intelligence model into the field of greenwashing behavior identification, and constructs a greenwashing identification framework covering two dimensions of selective disclosure and expressive manipulation with six sub-indicators. The study finds: (1) Compared with traditional bag-of-words methods and machine learning methods, the BERT artificial intelligence model has significant advantages in identifying greenwashing behavior; (2) With the improvement of regulatory policies, the greenwashing strategies of bond issuers show dynamic evolution characteristics, the space for selective disclosure is compressed, and expressive manipulation becomes the more dominant form of greenwashing; (3) Bond issuers with greenwashing behavior are more likely to engage in strategic green innovation in the future, and their future financial performance and sustainability are significantly weaker than non-greenwashing entities, and this situation exists in both bond issuers with selective disclosure and expressive manipulation. This study provides a new technical path for the automatic identification of greenwashing behavior in green bonds and provides empirical evidence for regulatory agencies to improve the information disclosure system.

title: Fresh food consumers and e-marketplaces for smallholders: an analysis of perceptions and attitudes
summary: Abstract Disintermediation has been proposed as a possible strategy to enhance the competitiveness of small farmers. This paper examines consumers’ interest in using e-marketplaces to purchase fresh food directly from smallholders, employin
content: Abstract Disintermediation has been proposed as a possible strategy to enhance the competitiveness of small farmers. This paper examines consumers’ interest in using e-marketplaces to purchase fresh food directly from smallholders, employing a focus groups methodology. Unlike previous studies that have focused on current users of e-marketplace platforms, this research explores the views of potential consumers responsible for food purchases in their households, specifically regarding their willingness to participate in such e-marketplaces. 41 consumers participated, grouped into 6 different groups. Focus group discussions were transcribed and analyzed using content analysis, keywords-in-context, and discourse analysis to obtain the main results. Although there is a widespread understanding of the challenges faced by smallholders, a shift towards direct purchasing and e-marketplace usage is not yet widely embraced by consumers. Cultural changes appear necessary before consumers fully accept e-markets as a direct sales channel for fresh produce. Nevertheless, based on participant opinions and observations of several e-marketplaces, the study offers specific recommendations to improve consumers’ perception of these platforms.

title: The ontological dimensions of coastal mangrove reserve conflicts——insights from China
summary: In the context of escalating anthropogenic pressures on coastal ecosystems, this article employs a case study of one of China’s southeastern coastal mangrove reserves to interrogate the interplay between local communities and state authorit
content: In the context of escalating anthropogenic pressures on coastal ecosystems, this article employs a case study of one of China’s southeastern coastal mangrove reserves to interrogate the interplay between local communities and state authorities in natural resource governance from an ontological perspective. Through qualitative research involving 30 semi-structured interviews conducted between 2019 and 2023, we reveal how state, market, and community actors operate from fundamentally different – and often incompatible – understandings of mangroves. We trace a historical shift from a community ontology, where mangroves were perceived as socio-ecological commons buffering against flooding, to a market ontology through which mangroves were seen as barriers to marketized aquaculture development. While state intervention later curtailed market overexploitation, its regulatory, ecological ontology clashed with both the eroded community framework and the persistent market logic. Consequently, state governance, though justified by ecologically necessity, proved ontologically irreconcilable with the community’s original, relational approach. This study demonstrates that environmental governance conflicts are not merely about resource distribution but are rooted in conflicting ontologies and clashes between divergent world-making practices. It thus contributes a novel analytical lens for understanding governance conflicts in socio-ecological systems under competing state and market pressures, revealing that effective and just governance requires recognizing and navigating deep ontological divides, not just negotiating resource claims.

title: Comparative governance of coffee value chains in Oaxaca and Latin American cases
summary: This paper addresses the topic of the current comparative governance of coffee value chains in the state of Oaxaca, Mexico, as well as a comparison with a selection of Latin American case studies, to identify how institutional arrangements
content: This paper addresses the topic of the current comparative governance of coffee value chains in the state of Oaxaca, Mexico, as well as a comparison with a selection of Latin American case studies, to identify how institutional arrangements can influence producer inclusion, the improvement of local and export-oriented markets, and resilience to the climate crisis and price fluctuations. Through a comparative analysis of policies and value chains, this study examines the role of public agencies, producer organizations, intermediaries, certification systems, and territorial coordination mechanisms in the distribution of benefits and decision-making power throughout the chain. Governance models with greater public-private coordination and producer participation tend to improve market access, value capture, and adaptability. At the same time, fragmented or market-dominated arrangements reinforce dependence on intermediaries and reduce opportunities for improvement at the local level. Governance in the coffee sector should be understood as a multilevel institutional issue that encompasses more than just the agro industrial component. The findings contribute to comparative research on governance by linking rural development outcomes to institutional design, collective action, and policy coordination in a strategic export crop sector.

title: Unlocking SME Financing for BRICS Economies: Insights from Case Studies
summary: For BRICS economies, SMEs are essential as a domestic supplier base, growth multiplier, livelihood safety net, and channels for the absorption of innovation. These enterprises account for anywhere between 20-60 percent of their country’s GD
content: For BRICS economies, SMEs are essential as a domestic supplier base, growth multiplier, livelihood safety net, and channels for the absorption of innovation. These enterprises account for anywhere between 20-60 percent of their country’s GDP, with those in China and South Africa in the lead

title: Valorisation of Market Food Waste for Sustainable Polyhydroxyalkanoate Production: A Critical Review of Feedstock Variability, Bioprocess Integration and Scale-Up
summary: Market food waste is a concentrated, spatially identifiable stream of discarded fruits, vegetables and other perishables generated at wholesale and retail food markets. Its high moisture content, rapid degradability and variable carbohydrat
content: Market food waste is a concentrated, spatially identifiable stream of discarded fruits, vegetables and other perishables generated at wholesale and retail food markets. Its high moisture content, rapid degradability and variable carbohydrate composition create disposal problems but also provide a renewable carbon source for polyhydroxyalkanoate (PHA) production. This critical narrative review evaluates the evidence for converting market food waste to PHA, with particular attention to the acidogenic fermentation-volatilised fatty acid (VFA) route, microbial selection, polymer recovery, scale-up and sustainability. The literature shows that direct, fully integrated demonstrations using genuine market waste remain scarce. Stronger evidence exists for individual links in the chain: market vegetable and fruit wastes rapidly generate VFA-rich leachates; mixed food waste, organic municipal waste and food-industry residues can support PHA accumulation; and feast-famine mixed microbial cultures can operate without sterilised substrates. Pure cultures, especially Cupriavidus necator, can achieve high intracellular storage when waste-derived carbon is sufficiently clarified and appropriately dosed, whereas mixed microbial cultures reduce sterility requirements but introduce ecological and product-composition variability. The critical interface is not PHA biosynthesis alone but upstream control of hydrolysis and acidogenesis, because VFA concentration and acid spectrum govern inhibition, carbon conversion and the 3-hydroxybutyrate/3-hydroxyvalerate balance. Downstream stabilisation and extraction can also erase upstream gains by lowering molecular weight or increasing solvent, energy and chemical demand. Market-waste valorisation therefore cannot be assumed to be sustainable merely because the feedstock is discarded. The strongest deployment case is a source-segregated, short-haul biorefinery that prioritises prevention and edible redistribution, converts unavoidable residues to VFAs, directs selected carbon to PHA, and valorises residual solids and process liquors. Future work should prioritise market-specific seasonal campaigns, continuous pilot validation, contaminant tracking, harmonised mass balances, polymer-quality endpoints, and integrated techno-economic and life-cycle assessment.

title: Bamboo-based agroforestry systems: a nature-based solution for degraded land restoration
summary: Land degradation is a pressing global challenge that undermines ecosystem health, biodiversity, agricultural productivity, and human well-being. Nature-based Solutions (NbS), particularly bamboo-based agroforestry systems, are increasingly
content: Land degradation is a pressing global challenge that undermines ecosystem health, biodiversity, agricultural productivity, and human well-being. Nature-based Solutions (NbS), particularly bamboo-based agroforestry systems, are increasingly recognized for their potential to restore degraded landscapes while enhancing climate resilience and supporting sustainable development. Owing to its rapid growth, high biomass production, extensive root system, and wide ecological adaptability, bamboo plays a vital role in improving soil fertility, increasing organic carbon, reducing erosion, conserving soil moisture, and supporting biodiversity conservation. Its integration into agricultural systems further enhances land productivity, diversifies rural income sources, and strengthens livelihood resilience. Bamboo-based systems also deliver multiple ecosystem services, including carbon sequestration, watershed protection, bioenergy production, and provision of sustainable raw materials, thereby contributing to several Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Despite these benefits, wider adoption remains constrained by limited empirical synthesis, inadequate availability of quality planting material, weak market linkages, and policy gaps. This review critically synthesizes existing knowledge on bamboo-based agroforestry systems, focusing on their ecological, economic, and social contributions to degraded land restoration, climate change mitigation, biodiversity enhancement, livelihood improvement, and sustainable development. The findings highlight bamboo-based agroforestry as a promising, climate-resilient, and multifunctional strategy for sustainable land restoration.

title: Formulation of a Protective Non-Edible Coating Incorporating Dawul Kurudu (Neolitsea cassia) Leaf Extract and Flaxseed (Linum usitatissimum) Gel for Extending the Postharvest Shelf Life of Bananas
source: Sri Lankan Journal of Applied Sciences
summary: Bananas are one of the most popular fruits in the world due to their delicious flavour, smooth texture, and high nutritional content. However, they are extremely susceptible to microbial contamination and post-harvest degradation during sto
content: Bananas are one of the most popular fruits in the world due to their delicious flavour, smooth texture, and high nutritional content. However, they are extremely susceptible to microbial contamination and post-harvest degradation during storage and transit, leading to large post-harvest losses. This study aimed to develop a non-edible protective coating using Dawul Kurudu (DK) leaf extract and flax (FX) seed gel to extend the shelf life of bananas. Cavendish bananas were harvested at 15 days after flowering and coated with formulations with varying FX gel-to-DK leaf extract ratios of 4:1, 3:2, 2:3, and 1:4. Changes in weight loss, pH, titratable acidity (TA), total soluble solids (TSS), and microbial colony counts were evaluated over a 15-day storage period in both coated and uncoated bananas. All treatments were performed in triplicate. When compared to the uncoated control, the coated bananas had significantly (p< 0.05) less weight loss, TA, and TSS over the storage time. The coating with an FX gel-to-DK leaf extract ratio of 2:3 exhibited the most effective efficacy among the tested formulations. Overall, the coatings made of FX seed gel and DK leaf extract effectively extended the shelf life of bananas. The best preservation effectiveness was observed with the FX gel-to-DK leaf extract ratio of 2:3, maintaining acceptable fruit quality for more than 12 days. These findings suggest that this natural, non-edible coating has the potential to serve as an effective and environmentally friendly method for extending the post-harvest shelf life of bananas.

title: Does rainfall affect inflation? Evidence from Indonesia’s regional heterogeneity
summary: This study analyzes the impact of seasonal rainfall variations on inflation in Indonesia, using panel data from 82 cities between 2014 and 2019. While prior research links weather conditions, particularly rainfall, to inflation through effe
content: This study analyzes the impact of seasonal rainfall variations on inflation in Indonesia, using panel data from 82 cities between 2014 and 2019. While prior research links weather conditions, particularly rainfall, to inflation through effects on agricultural production, our findings challenge this view. Using fixed effects regression models, we observe a statistically significant negative relationship between rainfall and inflation at the district level; however, the effect sizes are economically negligible. When time fixed effects are added, capturing national-level factors like monetary policy and global conditions, rainfall’s impact becomes statistically insignificant. Robustness checks, including weighted two-way fixed effects models, placebo tests, and extending the observational period to 2023, confirm the consistency of these results. The findings suggest that national-level policies overshadow minor local effects of rainfall on inflation. Policymakers should prioritize macroeconomic strategies over local environmental factors when addressing inflation, highlighting the limited role of weather variability.

title: Injectable biodegradable hydrogels for in situ tissue engineering
summary: Biodegradable hydrogels are injected in situ to create scaffolds in complex tissue defects with a minimally invasive approach. The current narrative review critically discusses their design principles such as polymer type (natural, syntheti
content: Biodegradable hydrogels are injected in situ to create scaffolds in complex tissue defects with a minimally invasive approach. The current narrative review critically discusses their design principles such as polymer type (natural, synthetic and hybrid systems), crosslinking processes (physical, chemical, and self-crosslinking strategies), and optimization of their rheological properties for clinical injectability. Various advanced biofunctionalization strategies such as cell encapsulation, spatiotemporal delivery of growth factors, extracellular matrix mimicry via fiber-reinforced composites, and active immunomodulation are assessed for their application in tissue-specific regeneration in cartilage, bone, cardiac, neural, skin, and dental applications. While there has been significant progress in preclinical work, there are significant translational challenges that remain: mechanical mismatch with load-bearing native tissues, natural polymer batch-to-batch variability, unpredictable degradation rates, and a complex regulatory pathway for combination products. We explore under-explored areas such as 4D bioprinting for dynamic shape morphing, the design of materials through artificial intelligence, and closed-loop theranostic platforms that combine real-time biosensing with on-demand therapeutic release. This review suggests that the interdisciplinary convergence of materials science, bioengineering, and regulatory science is necessary to tackle these challenges and make injectable hydrogels a standard-of-care regenerative therapeutic.

title: Microalgae as a Promising Platform for the Production of Eco-Friendly Biodiesel: Recent Advances, Bottlenecks, and Solutions
summary: Biodiesel made from microalgae is now being mass-produced and sold as a viable alternative to petroleum-based feedstock due to advances in industrial production. Microalgae have a high growth rate and high carbon sequestration, and they can
content: Biodiesel made from microalgae is now being mass-produced and sold as a viable alternative to petroleum-based feedstock due to advances in industrial production. Microalgae have a high growth rate and high carbon sequestration, and they can be grown without the need for arable 146 soil in both fresh and salt water. Recent improvements in the cultivation, harvesting, pretreatment, lipid extraction, and transesterification subsystems are bringing microalgal biodiesel closer to being able to be used as a fuel. Although promising, microalgal platforms have yet to be adopted for bioenergy production on an industrial scale due to a number of obstacles in the form of technical and economic hurdles. Challenges in microalgae production processes for bioenergy purposes are outlined in this review, along with techno-economic assessments of the cultivation, harvesting, and downstream processes necessary to produce biodiesel. Microalgae cultivation, lipid accumulation, microalgae harvesting, and lipid extraction have all been summed up in the section on influencing parameters for biodiesel production. The goal of this analysis is to improve the economics and technology of making biodiesel from microalgae and to help come up with efficient and marketable technology to do this.

title: Del Extractivismo al Metabolismo Regenerativo: Análisis Crítico-Propositivo de la Estrategia Forestal Sostenible del Ecuador (EFSE) 2026–2050 desde un Enfoque de Biosfera, Tecnosfera y Sociosfera para una Bioeconomía Circular y Bioética
summary: La EFSE 2026–2050, elaborada con asistencia técnica de la Organización de las Naciones Unidas para la Alimentación y la Agricultura (FAO) y financiamiento del Programa REM-Ecuador, organiza la política forestal nacional en cuatro ejes estra
content: La EFSE 2026–2050, elaborada con asistencia técnica de la Organización de las Naciones Unidas para la Alimentación y la Agricultura (FAO) y financiamiento del Programa REM-Ecuador, organiza la política forestal nacional en cuatro ejes estratégicos: gestión sostenible de los recursos forestales, negocios sostenibles e incentivos, investigación y cultura forestal, y gobernanza forestal (Ministerio de Ambiente y Energía [MAE] et al., 2026). Este trabajo reordena el análisis de esos ejes bajo una matriz ontológica de biosfera–tecnosfera–sociosfera, inspirada en la noción de tecnosfera como subsistema planetario cuasi-autónomo (Haff, 2014) y en la perspectiva de resiliencia socioecológica (Folke, 2006), y la contrasta con los principios ecológicos de la bioeconomía circular (Muscat et al., 2021), el marco del desarrollo regenerativo (Mang & Reed, 2012) y la bioética como puente entre el conocimiento biológico y los sistemas de valores humanos (Potter, 1971). Se demuestra, con datos oficiales reproducidos en tablas y figuras propias, que la deforestación neta ecuatoriana convergió con la deforestación bruta entre 2018 y 2022 (de 58 429 ha año⁻¹ neta a 93 023 ha año⁻¹, frente a una bruta de 91 692 y 95 570 ha año⁻¹, respectivamente) (MAE et al., 2026), que el 75,3 % del volumen maderero legal proviene ya de plantaciones (MAE et al., 2026), que el crédito forestal apenas alcanza el 1,2 % del financiamiento productivo agropecuario-forestal (MAE et al., 2026), y que los sistemas agroforestales indígenas Chakra y Aja almacenan hasta 105,6 Mg C ha⁻¹ en sus parcelas mejor manejadas, casi 25 veces más que un pastizal ganadero extensivo (Álava-Núñez et al., 2025). Se examinan además los efectos de fuga del programa Socio Bosque (Gordillo et al., 2021), el desafío de trazabilidad que impone el Reglamento (UE) 2023/1115 sobre productos libres de deforestación (EUDR) (Unión Europea [UE], 2023), y un modelo participativo de gestión regenerativa del fuego validado en los Andes ecuatorianos (Carvajal-Benavides et al., 2025b). El artículo cierra con una matriz propositiva que traduce el marco teórico en recomendaciones concretas para la implementación de la EFSE.

title: Chili Pepper Flavourants in 'Heat" Oral Nicotine Pouches Marketed as Unflavoured in United States Jurisdictions Restricting Flavoured Tobacco Products
summary: Background: In the United States, several states have restricted sales of flavoured tobacco products, including popular menthol- and mint-flavored Oral Nicotine Pouches (ONP). In response, tobacco companies introduced "unflavoured" ONP cont
content: Background: In the United States, several states have restricted sales of flavoured tobacco products, including popular menthol- and mint-flavored Oral Nicotine Pouches (ONP). In response, tobacco companies introduced "unflavoured" ONP containing odorless synthetic cooling agents. Since these, in turn, have become targets of legislative bans, the tobacco industry may seek out flavourants with other sensory effects to increase the appeal of "unflavored" ONP. Methods: Online merchants were searched for "unflavored" ONP marketed to consumers in jurisdictions with flavour bans. Sensory effects of aqueous extracts from identified "heat / unflavored" and "spicy" ONP were analyzed by Ca2+ microfluorimetry in HEK293 cells expressing the human heat/chili pepper flavourant (capsaicinoid) receptor, hTRPV1. ONP were analyzed for capsaicinoids by Ultra Performance Liquid Chromatography/Mass Spectrometry (UPLC/MS). Results: A new category of "heat" or "spicy" ONP was identified, including products marketed as "unflavored". Extracts from all these ONP robustly activated TRPV1, with "unflavored" Lucy Heat the most potent. Chemical analysis demonstrated that Lucy Heat contained the synthetic capsaicinoid nonivamide at high levels (~650 microgram/pouch), while others contained mixtures of capsaicinoids (5-25 microgram/pouch) combined with other characterizing flavors (tropical, fruit). Conclusions: The tobacco industry continues to probe regulatory loopholes by claiming that newly introduced "heat" flavourants in ONP do not represent characterizing flavours, justifying sales in US jurisdictions with flavour bans. This is contradicted by industry documentation assigning flavour descriptors to these additives. The toxicological oral health risks of repeated capsaicinoid exposures due to ONP use, in combination with nicotine and other constituents, need to be assessed.

title: From AI resources to sustainable competitive advantage: Building AI-enabled sustainable gastronomy capabilities in restaurants
source: Journal of Tourism Theory and Research
summary: This study examines the relationships among AI capability, organizational readiness for AI, AI-enabled sustainable gastronomy capability, sustainable food innovation orientation, and sustainable competitive advantage. Data were collected fr
content: This study examines the relationships among AI capability, organizational readiness for AI, AI-enabled sustainable gastronomy capability, sustainable food innovation orientation, and sustainable competitive advantage. Data were collected from 400 restaurant decision-makers in Brazil and analyzed using SPSS, AMOS, and the PROCESS Macro. The findings indicate that AI capability and organizational readiness for AI are positively associated with AI-driven operational sustainability and AI-driven customer sustainability experience. Bootstrapped indirect effects further show that these capability dimensions constitute significant pathways linking AI-related resources to sustainable competitive advantage. In addition, sustainable food innovation orientation strengthens the conditional indirect relationships, supporting its role as a boundary condition in AI-enabled capability development. The study extends dynamic capability theory by specifying a contingent capability-building mechanism through which AI-related resources are associated with sustainable competitiveness in restaurant contexts.

title: The Role of Government in Housing Development: A Multi Dimensional Analysis of Policy Transitions, Market Failures, and Institutional Reform in Nigeria
source: IIARD INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF GEOGRAPHY AND ENVIRONMENTAL MANAGEMENT
summary: This research paper examined the multifaceted role of government intervention in housing development, focusing on the critical tension between housing as a private market commodity and a fundamental social right. It was observed that this d
content: This research paper examined the multifaceted role of government intervention in housing development, focusing on the critical tension between housing as a private market commodity and a fundamental social right. It was observed that this dual character necessitated state involvement to mitigate systematic market failures such as spatial fixity, information asymmetry, and speculative volatility. The study traced the global evolution of housing strategies from post-1945 direct public provision to the neoliberal enabling state paradigm and the contemporary rise of public-private partnerships. A detailed case study of the Nigerian housing sector was conducted, revealing a staggering housing deficit newly validated in 2026 at 14.925 million units, with an additional 15.2 million units classified as structurally inadequate. It was reported that while the Nigerian government established a comprehensive institutional architecture involving the Federal Mortgage Bank of Nigeria and the Federal Housing Authority, implementation was chronically hampered by land administration bottlenecks, weak finance systems, and macroeconomic shocks. The study identified a critical research gap in the lack of evidence-based policy alignment between formal housing delivery and the realities of the informal self-build sector, which accounted for approximately 80% of urban residents. The analysis further integrated contemporary data on the impact of hyperinflation and currency devaluation, which saw cement prices surge to ₦15,000 per bag in 2026, thereby stalling many affordable housing initiatives. It was concluded that the enabling state model required active administrative capacity and transparent accountability to be effective. The findings suggested that addressing the housing crisis requires a fundamental reset of land governance, the scaling of incremental housing models, and the adoption of climate resilient construction technologies to ensure sustainable urban growth.
