title: Nanobiotechnological enhancement of bioethanol production from potato peel waste using green-synthesized ZnO nanoparticles
summary: The growing demand for sustainable energy and effective waste management has intensified interest in bioethanol production from agro-industrial residues. This study investigates the potential of potato peel waste (PPs) as an economical subs
content: The growing demand for sustainable energy and effective waste management has intensified interest in bioethanol production from agro-industrial residues. This study investigates the potential of potato peel waste (PPs) as an economical substrate for enhanced bioethanol production using a nanobiotechnological approach. Zinc oxide nanoparticles (ZnONPs) were green-synthesized using potato peel extract and characterized through SEM, EDX, and zeta analysis, confirming their nanoscale size, stability, and elemental composition. An alkali-thermophilic bacterial strain, Bacillus licheniformis (OQ740163), exhibiting both amylolytic and cellulolytic activities, was employed for biomass hydrolysis. The incorporation of ZnONPs significantly enhanced saccharification efficiency, yielding a maximum reducing sugar concentration of 9.58 g/L compared to 5.91 g/L without nanoparticles, representing a 61.96% increase. Subsequent fermentation using Saccharomyces cerevisiae K7 further demonstrated improved ethanol production, achieving a yield of 0.460 g/g glucose compared to 0.399 g/g in the control. The findings highlight the catalytic role of ZnONPs in enhancing both hydrolysis and fermentation processes. Overall, this study presents a sustainable and cost-effective strategy for converting potato peel waste into bioethanol, contributing to renewable energy production and circular bioeconomy development.

title: Knowledge Accuracy and Response Characteristics of an On-Device Large Language Model in Building Environmental Engineering: a Preliminary Case Study of EXAONE 4.0 1.2B Using ChatGPT-4o as a Cloud Reference
summary: This preliminary case study examines EXAONE 4.0 1.2B, an on-device large language model (LLM), in building environmental engineering, using ChatGPT-4o as a high-capability cloud reference rather than a size-matched competitor. Ten Korean-la
content: This preliminary case study examines EXAONE 4.0 1.2B, an on-device large language model (LLM), in building environmental engineering, using ChatGPT-4o as a high-capability cloud reference rather than a size-matched competitor. Ten Korean-language items were evaluated: four multiple-choice, three single-step calculations, and three short-answer questions covering indoor environmental quality, energy, and post-occupancy evaluation. The same simple prompt condition was applied to both models, with no model-specific prompt optimization; therefore, the results represent one standardized condition rather than each model’s maximum performance. Both models answered all seven objective items correctly, although EXAONE showed terminology confusion in its reasoning on a thermal-environment item. Five doctoral-level experts rated the short-answer responses for accuracy, completeness, and logical consistency. Mean scores were 4.18 for ChatGPT-4o and 2.98 for EXAONE. Fleiss’ kappa was 0.020 and 0.044, while free-marginal kappa was 0.333 and 0.222, respectively; the latter values indicate fair, not moderate, agreement, so absolute expert scores require cautious interpretation. Qualitatively, ChatGPT-4o more consistently organized responses around concepts and scope, whereas EXAONE tended to provide specific technical, operational, and Korean-regulatory content but occasionally omitted canonical elements or added unsupported detail. Because the item pool is small and only one on-device model was tested, the findings are exploratory and cannot be generalized to building environmental engineering as a whole or to on-device LLMs as a class. The results support further investigation of on-device LLMs as supervised offline assistants where connectivity or external data transmission is constrained, but not as unsupervised tools for engineering calculation or compliance decisions.

title: Resilience Waterfront Housing Models For Sustainable Community Development in The Niger Delta
source: IIARD INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF GEOGRAPHY AND ENVIRONMENTAL MANAGEMENT
summary: The Niger Delta region of Nigeria confronts a critical housing deficit compounded by annual flooding, sea level rise, and rapid urbanisation. This paper examined resilient waterfront housing models as strategic interventions for sustainable
content: The Niger Delta region of Nigeria confronts a critical housing deficit compounded by annual flooding, sea level rise, and rapid urbanisation. This paper examined resilient waterfront housing models as strategic interventions for sustainable community development in this ecologically vulnerable region. Through a qualitative multi-case study design incorporating document analysis, secondary data synthesis, and observational assessment of existing housing typologies, this research evaluates the structural integrity, environmental compatibility, and socio-economic viability of three resilient housing approaches: amphibious architecture, elevated pile dwellings adapted with modern materials, and integrated solar-powered estate models. The study draws empirical insights from recent NDDC emergency shelter projects, the Brooks Haven solar estate in Port Harcourt, and comparative vernacular adaptations from the Tempe Lake floating settlements. Findings reveal that the hybridisation of indigenous building knowledge with modern engineering offers the most viable path toward flood resilience and energy autonomy. The analysis further demonstrates that inter-agency collaboration between the Federal Ministry of Housing and the Niger Delta Development Commission creates institutional frameworks capable of scaling these models from pilot projects to community wide implementation. The paper contributes a resilience assessment framework for evaluating waterfront housing interventions and provides policy recommendations for integrating resilient design into Nigeria's national housing agenda.

title: STUDY AND OPTIMIZATION OF THE EFFICIENCY OF A VERTICAL-JUNCTION SILICON SOLAR CELL IN SERIES UNDER A MAGNETIC FIELD IN STEADY STATE
source: World Journal of Advanced Research and Reviews
summary: This article presents a theoretical study of a vertical-junction silicon solar cell in steady state under polychromatic illumination and subjected to an external magnetic field. After solving the magnetotransport equation for minority charg
content: This article presents a theoretical study of a vertical-junction silicon solar cell in steady state under polychromatic illumination and subjected to an external magnetic field. After solving the magnetotransport equation for minority charge carriers in the base using the boundary conditions applied at the junctions and in the rear region, the expressions for the photovoltage, electrical power, and conversion efficiency of the photovoltaic cell are determined as functions of the magnetic field and the optimal thickness of the base. The current-voltage and power-voltage characteristics are studied for several values of the applied magnetic field. Finally, the photovoltaic cell’s efficiency is studied as a function of the optimal base thickness obtained based on the applied magnetic field. This study shows a linear correlation between these two parameters.

title: Fuzzy Analytical Hierarchy Process Model for Malaria Control Strategies Prioritization in North-East, Nigeria
source: Mikailalsys Journal of Mathematics and Statistics
summary: Although the Fuzzy Analytic Hierarchy Process (F-AHP) is widely used to address complex multi-criteria decision-making problems under uncertainty, its application to malaria intervention prioritization in resource-constrained settings, part
content: Although the Fuzzy Analytic Hierarchy Process (F-AHP) is widely used to address complex multi-criteria decision-making problems under uncertainty, its application to malaria intervention prioritization in resource-constrained settings, particularly North-East Nigeria, remains limited. This study developed and applied an F-AHP decision-support framework to prioritize malaria control interventions based on epidemiological, economic, operational, and social considerations. A mixed-methods approach involved 18 purposively selected experts, including epidemiologists, medical doctors, and health educators from the six states of North-East Nigeria. Primary data were collected through structured questionnaires, while secondary evidence was drawn from peer-reviewed literature, national malaria control guidelines, and relevant health reports. Five evaluation criteria and five intervention alternatives were assessed using fuzzy pairwise comparison matrices. Expert judgments were represented by triangular fuzzy numbers and defuzzified using the centroid method to generate normalized priority weights and global intervention rankings. All judgment matrices met the recommended consistency threshold (CR ≤ 0.10), supporting the internal consistency of the evaluations. Acceptability emerged as the most influential criterion (0.387), followed by cost-effectiveness (0.283) and health impact (0.200). Among the intervention alternatives, insecticide-treated nets/long-lasting insecticidal nets ranked first, with a global priority weight of 0.346, followed by indoor residual spraying at 0.278. These findings demonstrate that social acceptability, economic efficiency, and health impact are central determinants of malaria intervention priorities in the region. The study contributes to fuzzy multi-criteria decision-making in public health by providing a transparent and systematic framework for incorporating uncertainty into expert judgments. Practically, the framework can support policymakers, malaria control programmes, and public health stakeholders in allocating limited resources and selecting contextually appropriate interventions in North-East Nigeria. It also provides a foundation for integrating stochastic and adaptive approaches into future malaria intervention prioritization under temporal and epidemiological uncertainty.

title: Power Sector Reform and Industrial Development in Nigeria: A Study of Transmission Company of Nigeria (TCN) Port Harcourt Region
source: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF SOCIAL SCIENCES AND MANAGEMENT RESEARCH
summary: This study investigated the impact of power sector reforms on industrial development in Nigeria, with specific focus on the Transmission Company of Nigeria (TCN) power transmission operations in Rivers State. The study aimed to identify app
content: This study investigated the impact of power sector reforms on industrial development in Nigeria, with specific focus on the Transmission Company of Nigeria (TCN) power transmission operations in Rivers State. The study aimed to identify approaches adopted by TCN in enhancing power transmission to industries and analyze the impacts of TCN power transmission on industrial development. The research adopted a descriptive survey design, utilizing both primary and secondary data sources. From a population of 592 TCN employees, 239 questionnaires were administered using stratified random sampling technique, with 212 usable questionnaires retrieved representing 88.7% response rate from the Port Harcourt Regional Transmission Company. Data analysis utilized descriptive and inferential statistics through SPSS version 25.0. Key findings revealed that direct wheeling of power emerged as the most effective approach adopted by TCN (mean = 3.38), with transmission operations demonstrating significant positive impacts on industrial development, particularly in boosting Rivers State's IGR through industrial profits (mean = 3.05). An extremely strong correlation (r = 0.986) was established between TCN's impacts and industrial development. The study recommends strengthening direct wheeling capability of TCN and implementing climate-resilient infrastructure measures to optimize TCN's contribution to Rivers State's industrial development.

title: High-Efficiency Novel Cu₃InSnS₅ Quantum Dot Photovoltaics: From Quantum Confinement Modeling to Tandem Cell Optimization for Dual Indoor/Outdoor Energy Harvesting
source: ECS Journal of Solid State Science and Technology
summary: Abstract This study presents a comprehensive numerical optimization of single and tandem photovoltaic cells utilizing novel Cu₃InSnS₅ colloidal quantum dots (CQDs) as absorbers. These quaternary CQDs have emerged as a compelling class of lo
content: Abstract This study presents a comprehensive numerical optimization of single and tandem photovoltaic cells utilizing novel Cu₃InSnS₅ colloidal quantum dots (CQDs) as absorbers. These quaternary CQDs have emerged as a compelling class of low-dimensional materials due to their tunable optoelectronic properties and compliance with the Restriction of Hazardous Substances (RoHS) directive. A multi-scale simulation framework is employed, combining the envelope function approximation to predict size-dependent quantum confinement effects, Rigorous Coupled-Wave Analysis (RCWA) for optical modeling, and the Solar Cell Capacitance Simulator (SCAPS-1D) for device-level electrical optimization. By systematically tuning the CQD radius, buffer layer, and absorber thickness, the optimized single-junction cell achieves a power conversion efficiency of 11.53% under standard AM1.5G illumination, significantly surpassing the current experimental benchmark of <0.1%. Furthermore, a tandem architecture is designed to minimize thermalization losses, yielding an impressive efficiency of 31.97% under AM1.5G. Under indoor LED illumination (1250 lx), the single and tandem cells attain efficiencies of 12.13% and 22.21%, respectively. These findings underscore the immense potential of Cu₃InSnS₅ CQDs for dual indoor/outdoor energy harvesting, particularly for powering low-light Internet of Things (IoT) devices.

title: An Overview of Liberal Ideology and Democracy in Nigeria’s Fourth Republic, 1999-2023
source: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF SOCIAL SCIENCES AND MANAGEMENT RESEARCH
summary: The crux of this paper is an overview of liberal ideology and democracy within the context of the Nigerian Fourth Republic, spanning from 1999 to 2023. The Nigerian Fourth Republic, established in 1999, is characterized by a complex relatio
content: The crux of this paper is an overview of liberal ideology and democracy within the context of the Nigerian Fourth Republic, spanning from 1999 to 2023. The Nigerian Fourth Republic, established in 1999, is characterized by a complex relationship between liberal ideology and democratic practice. The amended 1999 Constitution lays out a federal framework that includes the separation of powers, fundamental human rights, and guarantees for free and fair elections. Nigeria functions under a multi-party system, with regular elections designed to promote popular participation and representation. The constitution underscores the importance of the rule of law, striving to ensure equality before the law and accountability for all citizens and institutions. The primary aim of this study is to explore liberal ideology and democracy in the Nigerian Fourth Republic from 1999 to 2023. The research employs liberal theory as its theoretical framework and utilizes qualitative research analysis methods. The methodology incorporates secondary data sources, such as online materials, articles, journals, and textbooks. The data collected were qualitatively analyzed through content analysis techniques. The findings indicate that although the constitution and political framework are intended to embody liberal democratic principles, the actual situation often falls short. Challenges such as weak institutions, corruption, military influence, ethnic and regional divisions, limited public engagement, and a lack of robust ideological foundations within political parties impede the full realization of liberal democratic ideals. Based on these findings, the study concludes that Nigeria requires purposeful leadership with a vision that prioritizes its citizens in the administrative agenda, moving beyond limited public participation. The study advocates for strengthening institutions, tackling corruption, and fostering a more inclusive and participatory democracy.

title: From brewery waste to bioactive nanomaterials: Eco-friendly biosynthesis of silver nanoparticles with antimicrobial and anticancer activities using brewery waste-cultivated Parachlorella kessleri
summary: Green algae have emerged as promising platform for the eco-friendly biosynthesis of nanoparticles owing to their abundance in proteins, pigments, polysaccharides, phenolic compounds, and other bioactive metabolites. The present study aimed
content: Green algae have emerged as promising platform for the eco-friendly biosynthesis of nanoparticles owing to their abundance in proteins, pigments, polysaccharides, phenolic compounds, and other bioactive metabolites. The present study aimed to synthesize silver nanoparticles (Pk-AgNPs) using the biomass of the green alga Parachlorella kessleri MDC6524 cultivated on brewery production waste and to evaluate their antimicrobial and antiproliferative activities. The algal biomass served as a natural reducing and stabilizing agent during Pk-AgNPs synthesis under illumination. UV-Vis spectroscopy revealed a characteristic surface plasmon resonance peak at 440 nm, confirming Pk-AgNPs formation. Transmission electron microscopy showed predominantly ellipsoidal Pk-AgNPs with an average size of 46 nm, while X-ray diffraction analysis confirmed their crystalline structure and purity. Fourier-Transform Infrared spectroscopy indicated the involvement of functional groups from P. kessleri biomass in AgNPs formation. Pk-AgNPs exhibited significant antibacterial activity against Staphylococcus aureus, Enterococcus hirae , Salmonella typhimurium, and Pseudomonas aeruginosa , with minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) values ranging from 10 to 20 μg mL −1 , and greater activity against Gram-negative bacteria. Their antifungal activity against Aspergillus flavus, Penicillium aurantioviolaceum, and Trichoderma viride was species-dependent, with MIC values ranging from 200 to 500 μg mL −1 . Furthermore, Pk-AgNPs exhibited dose- and time-dependent cytotoxicity against lung adenocarcinoma A549 cells at low concentrations (0.6–10 μg mL −1 ). These findings demonstrate the potential of brewery waste-derived algal biomass as a renewable platform for nanoparticles biosynthesis and suggest that the resulting Pk-AgNPs possess promising antimicrobial and anticancer properties.

title: A unified multimodal learning framework for stress detection using IoT biomarkers and NLP with return-aligned decision transformers
summary: Early mental stress detection is important for timely intervention and proactive mental healthcare. However, unimodal stress detection methods often fail to capture the complexity of human stress responses, since physiological and linguisti
content: Early mental stress detection is important for timely intervention and proactive mental healthcare. However, unimodal stress detection methods often fail to capture the complexity of human stress responses, since physiological and linguistic signals represent complementary yet heterogeneous manifestations of affective state. To address this limitation, this study proposes UML-RADT-WOA, a unified multimodal framework for binary stress detection using wearable physiological signals from WESAD and stress-related textual posts from Dreaddit. The framework integrates MMADN-based preprocessing for physiology, DistilBERT-based textual representation, and class-conditioned Unified Multimodal Learning pairing for controlled multimodal fusion. A Modality-Token Return-Aligned Decision Transformer projects both modalities into a shared latent space, while Gated Multimodal Fusion suppresses modality-specific noise before final classification. Hyperparameters are optimized using the Wombat Optimization Algorithm. Under 15-fold Leave-One-Subject-Out cross-validation, the framework achieves 84.52% accuracy, 84.11% macro-F1, 89.52% ROC-AUC, and 85.88% AUPRC. The results indicate that the proposed framework offers an effective and reproducible IoT-enabled solution for multimodal stress detection.

title: NEXT-GENERATION 5G BAND DEPLOYMENT STRATEGIES FOR HIGH-SPEED WIRELESS COMMUNICATION IN SAUDI ARABIA
source: Veredas do Direito Direito Ambiental e Desenvolvimento Sustentável
summary: In response to the fast-paced development of information technologies in Saudi Arabia, there is a high need for high-speed and future-proof wireless communication infrastructure. This paper considers potential approaches for deploying 5G ba
content: In response to the fast-paced development of information technologies in Saudi Arabia, there is a high need for high-speed and future-proof wireless communication infrastructure. This paper considers potential approaches for deploying 5G bands capable of meeting national requirements in terms of connecting smart cities, implementing industry automation, supporting Internet of Things solutions, and preparing for 6G development according to the vision of Saudi Arabia 2030. The use of low-band, medium-band, and high-band frequency ranges in the millimeter wavelength spectrum for ensuring efficient coverage and adequate capacity is the focus of this report. The significance of spectrum management, radio access network optimization, small cell dense placement, fiber backhaul, network slicing, massive MIMO, carrier aggregation, and energy-efficient deployment of 5G infrastructure would be discussed in detail. Some of the key challenges of implementing 5G include problems of propagation loss, site acquisition, interferences, indoor coverage, efficiency, and regulation. Thus, an effective approach to planning of wireless networks requires careful assessment of the current telecommunications market, existing problems, and future demands for digital infrastructure.

title: Enhancing Internally Generated Revenue for Sustainable Financing of Tertiary Institutions in Nigeria: Global Perspectives and Strategic Options
source: Gamification Fatigue and Continuance Intention in Technology‑Enhanced Learning Platforms A Post‑Adoption Extension of TAM
summary: This paper reviewed practical and sustainable approaches for improving internally generated revenue in tertiary institutions, drawing lessons from international experiences and examining their applicability to the Nigerian higher education
content: This paper reviewed practical and sustainable approaches for improving internally generated revenue in tertiary institutions, drawing lessons from international experiences and examining their applicability to the Nigerian higher education system. The stud y specifically reviewed ten strategic areas including commercialization of research outputs, consultancy services, entrepreneurial ventures, public -private partnerships, commercial agriculture, continuing education programmes, alumni fundraising, commercialization of institutional assets, internationalization, and establishment of dedicated investment units. The review revealed that institutions that successfully diversify their revenue sources tend to achieve greater financial sustainability, improved infr astructure, enhanced research productivity, and stronger institutional competitiveness. The paper further observed that many Nigerian tertiary institutions possess significant untapped opportunities for generating additional income but are constrained by w eak entrepreneurial culture, inadequate policy frameworks, poor management structures, and limited commercialization capacity. The study concludes that internally generated revenue should serve as a strategic complement rather than a substitute for governm ent funding. It recommends the adoption of innovative financing mechanisms, strengthened institutional autonomy, enhanced industry collaboration, and professional management of revenue -generating ventures to improve the financial sustainability of tertiary institutions in Nigeria.

title: A compressor fault probability prediction and early warning method based on OCSSA–VMD–CNN–GRU-attention and chi-square residual mapping
summary: This study proposes a fault probability prediction and early-warning method based on the Osprey–Cauchy–Sparrow Search Algorithm (OCSSA), Variational Mode Decomposition (VMD), CNN–GRU-Attention, and chi-square residual mapping for compressor
content: This study proposes a fault probability prediction and early-warning method based on the Osprey–Cauchy–Sparrow Search Algorithm (OCSSA), Variational Mode Decomposition (VMD), CNN–GRU-Attention, and chi-square residual mapping for compressor monitoring signals characterized by strong noise, non-stationarity, multiscale behavior, and limited labeled fault samples. Compressor pressure and motor current are used as input signals to characterize pressure-response dynamics and load-state variation. OCSSA–VMD is employed to adaptively decompose the raw sequences, thereby improving multiscale feature separability and suppressing noise. A one-step CNN-GRU-Attention predictor is then constructed, in which CNN extracts local time-varying patterns, GRU captures temporal dependencies, and temporal attention emphasizes the historical moments that contribute most to the current prediction. Based on prediction residuals in the healthy stage, a statistical baseline is established. The current deviation is quantified by the squared standardized residual and mapped to the instantaneous fault probability through the cumulative distribution function of a chi-square distribution with one degree of freedom. A moving average is further applied to obtain a smoothed fault probability curve, and online warning is achieved by combining a dynamic threshold with a consecutive exceedance criterion. In the final validation run, the proposed method achieves RMSE, MAE, R², and MAPE values of 0.4746, 0.2147, 0.9879, and 6.54%, respectively. All four reported fault events in the April–May and June–August validation periods are successfully detected at the event level, with an average warning lead time of 21.25 h.

title: Reliability analysis of an off-grid fire safety system
summary: In this 21st century, demand for electricity is growing every day. The transformation from the traditional fossil fuel-based electricity production to a sustainable and renewable energy-based consumption is at its peak. A steady supply of e
content: In this 21st century, demand for electricity is growing every day. The transformation from the traditional fossil fuel-based electricity production to a sustainable and renewable energy-based consumption is at its peak. A steady supply of electricity is necessary in today’s modern life because sensitive configurations are susceptible to interruptions that might compromise both occupant safety and operational continuity in an emergency. This chapter uses reliability modelling and mathematical methods to improve the reliability of an integrated system comprising a solar energy and a fire safety system that provides vital services and protection. This chapter emphasizes improving system stability, reducing reliance on the utility grid, and promoting clean energy by the use of autonomous off-grid renewable systems based on solar energy. The proposed Markov approach highlights reliability, availability, mean time to failure (MTTF), and expected cost as performance estimation of the proposed system.

title: A High-Gain Single-Input Dual-Output DC-DC Converter for Fuel Cell Electric Vehicle Applications with Reduced Input Current Ripple
summary: Abstract This paper presents a high-gain non-isolated single-input dual-output (SIDO) DC–DC converter based on a quadratic boost architecture for fuel cell electric vehicle (FCEV) applications. The converter is designed to interface a low-v
content: Abstract This paper presents a high-gain non-isolated single-input dual-output (SIDO) DC–DC converter based on a quadratic boost architecture for fuel cell electric vehicle (FCEV) applications. The converter is designed to interface a low-voltage proton exchange membrane fuel cell (PEMFC) with two simultaneous loads: a high-voltage traction bus and a low-voltage auxiliary rail. Unlike conventional multi-output topologies that rely on transformers or coupled inductors, the proposed structure achieves significant voltage gain at moderate duty ratios using only two switches, four diodes, and three inductors in a common-ground configuration. Magnetic coupling is eliminated while continuous input current with reduced ripple is maintained, which is a critical requirement for PEMFC longevity. Comprehensive steady-state analysis, parasitic evaluation, component stress derivation, and dual-loop proportional–integral (PI) control design are presented to characterize and regulate both output ports independently. The converter is validated through MATLAB/Simulink simulation and a 120 W experimental prototype operating at 12 V input, 48 V and 6 V dual outputs, and 50 kHz switching frequency. Results confirm stable closed-loop regulation, strong inter-port decoupling, fast dynamic recovery under step load and input voltage disturbances, and a peak efficiency of 94%, demonstrating the practical suitability of the proposed converter for high-gain multi-output DC–DC conversion in FCEV powertrains.

title: Ortaokul Öğrencilerinin Sürdürülebilir Yaşama Yönelik Farkındalık Düzeylerinin Çeşitli Değişkenler Açısından İncelenmesi
summary: Sürdürülebilirlik kavramı; çevresel, ekonomik ve sosyal boyutları içeren zengin bir alana sahiptir. Çevresel boyut, doğal çevreyi korumayı; ekonomik boyut, kaynakları etkin kullanmayı; sosyal boyut ise toplumun ihtiyaçlarını adil bir şekild
content: Sürdürülebilirlik kavramı; çevresel, ekonomik ve sosyal boyutları içeren zengin bir alana sahiptir. Çevresel boyut, doğal çevreyi korumayı; ekonomik boyut, kaynakları etkin kullanmayı; sosyal boyut ise toplumun ihtiyaçlarını adil bir şekilde karşılamayı amaçlar. Sürdürülebilir yaşam farkındalığı ise, bireylerin doğal kaynakları koruyup çevre dostu uygulamaları benimsemesi ve atığı azaltmasıdır. Bu araştırmada, Sakarya ilindeki 2 farklı okuldan katılım sağlayan 304 ortaokul öğrencisinin sürdürülebilir yaşama yönelik farkındalık düzeyi incelenmiştir. Kolay ulaşılabilir örnekleme yöntemiyle seçilen öğrencilere Akgül ve Aydoğdu (2020)'nun geliştirdiği "Sürdürülebilir Yaşama Yönelik Farkındalık Ölçeği" uygulanmıştır. Analizler sonucunda, öğrencilerin yaş, cinsiyet ve sınıf düzeyleri ile sürdürülebilirlik farkındalıkları arasında anlamlı bir fark bulunamamıştır. Ancak, okul, sürdürülebilirlik ve sürdürülebilir yaşam kavramını daha önce duymuş olma durumları, yaşadıkları yer, kardeş sayısı, anne mesleği, baba mesleği, en son gelen elektrik faturası miktarı ve yenilenebilir enerji kaynakları hakkında bilgi sahibi olma değişkenleri açısından ise anlamlı farklar tespit edilmiştir. Bu bulgular, ortaokul öğrencilerinin sürdürülebilirlik farkındalığını etkileyen birçok faktörün olduğunu ortaya koymaktadır.

title: From critical temperature to engineering reality: A quantitative framework for assessing the translation gap in superconducting materials
summary: Purpose This review proposes and applies a quantitative measure—the Superconductor Translation Gap Index (STGI)—that expresses how far a given superconducting material sits from engineering viability in a defined application. The motivation
content: Purpose This review proposes and applies a quantitative measure—the Superconductor Translation Gap Index (STGI)—that expresses how far a given superconducting material sits from engineering viability in a defined application. The motivation is straightforward: record critical temperatures have risen dramatically over four decades, yet the set of superconducting technologies that achieve commercial deployment has expanded only slowly. No standard tool currently exists to quantify this translation gap in a transparent, reproducible way. Methods The STGI is a weighted composite score that maps laboratory performance onto application-specific requirements along four axes: temperature margin evaluated at the target magnetic field, in-field engineering current density, cryogenic accessibility including any pressure requirement, and mechanical and manufacturing robustness. Each axis is normalised against published benchmarks for three application classes—high-field magnets, power-grid components, and electric aircraft propulsion—and combined on a 0–100 scale. A viability gate is imposed: materials that cannot carry useful transport current in the target operating envelope receive a composite score of zero regardless of their performance on other axes. Results Seven material systems are scored. Under the assumptions defined here, no material exceeds an STGI of 76 in any application class, and in the demanding high-field class the best score is 64, belonging to REBCO coated conductors at 20 K. That score is constrained by conductor cost and transverse mechanical robustness rather than by electromagnetic performance. Hydride superconductors, despite critical temperatures above 200 K, score zero because no conductor form exists. Five structural barriers are ranked through a weighted impact matrix, and a milestone-based roadmap to 2045 identifies conductor cost reduction and helium-free cryocooler development as the highest-leverage near-term goals. Conclusions The translation gap between laboratory superconductor performance and engineering deployment remains wide, and the critical temperature alone is a weak predictor of technological impact. The value of the STGI framework lies in the discipline of simultaneous, application-referenced evaluation, and in the fact that every score can be recomputed from the tabulated inputs by any reader who prefers different assumptions.

title: A System-Level Power Behavior Model for Bluetooth and Wi-Fi Coexistence in Dual-Mode Wireless Devices
source: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF COMPUTER SCIENCE AND MATHEMATICAL THEORY E-ISSN
summary: Dual-mode wireless devices that implement Bluetooth and Wi-Fi in the same physical layer platform and share a single 2.4 GHz antenna must manage the mutual interference and power consumption that arise from concurrent operation of two radio
content: Dual-mode wireless devices that implement Bluetooth and Wi-Fi in the same physical layer platform and share a single 2.4 GHz antenna must manage the mutual interference and power consumption that arise from concurrent operation of two radio systems in overlapping spectrum. The coexistence challenge encompasses both the RF interference dimension, where simultaneous Bluetooth and Wi-Fi transmissions in the 2.4 GHz ISM band produce adjacent-channel and cochannel collisions that degrade throughput and packet error rate for both protocols, and the power consumption dimension, where the activation states of the Bluetooth and Wi-Fi transceivers, power amplifiers, and baseband processors interact to produce aggregate device power profiles that determine battery life in portable IoT and wearable applications. This paper presents a system-level power behavior model for Bluetooth and Wi-Fi coexistence in dual-mode wireless devices, developed from current profiling measurements of the transmit, receive, and idle current states of the Bluetooth 5.3 and Wi-Fi 6 radio subsystems under a range of coexistence configurations including time-division multiplexing, adaptive frequency hopping, and packet traffic arbitration. The model characterizes the power contribution of each protocol as a function of its duty cycle, packet size, data rate, and coexistence mode, and aggregates the per-protocol contributions into a system-level power model that predicts the average current consumption of the dual-mode device under mixed Bluetooth and Wi-Fi traffic loads. The model is assessed through measured current profiles from a commercial Bluetooth 5.3 and Wi-Fi 6 combo module under controlled traffic conditions and demonstrates a mean prediction error of 3.2 percent across the evaluated operating scenarios. Applications of the model to battery life estimation for IoT wearable devices and to coexistence mode selection for optimal power efficiency are presented.

title: Ageing in Unani medicine: Conceptual framework and modulatory approaches
source: Journal of Ayurveda and Integrative Medicine
summary: In Unani medicine, the sustenance of life and the ageing process are largely attributed to the gradual depletion of Ruṭūbat Gharīziyya (innate moisture), which weakens Ḥarārat Gharīziyya (innate heat), impairs Quwā (all faculties) of the bo
content: In Unani medicine, the sustenance of life and the ageing process are largely attributed to the gradual depletion of Ruṭūbat Gharīziyya (innate moisture), which weakens Ḥarārat Gharīziyya (innate heat), impairs Quwā (all faculties) of the body, and shifts Mizāj (temperament) towards coldness and dryness. These changes lead to impaired digestion, defective Akhlāṭ (humour) formation, increased Taḥallul (wear and tear), and accelerated senescence. This literature review examines how the balance of these principles, together with Aab Sitta Ḍaruriyya (six essential factors), influences vitality and healthy ageing. It employs a qualitative review of classical Unani texts alongside modern biomedical literature, integrating traditional metabolic concepts with contemporary perspectives on oxidative balance and degeneration. The findings indicate that Unani medicine advocates a comprehensive, holistic approach, encompassing regimental therapies, dietary modifications, and pharmacological interventions with antioxidant properties, to maintain internal homeostasis and promote healthy ageing and health span. However, the evidence remains largely theoretical, underscoring the need for rigorous mechanistic and clinical studies to facilitate integration into modern geriatric care.

title: Do wine prices reflect the environmental and social engagement of winemakers? An analysis of online prices of the Montepulciano d’Abruzzo wine
summary: This study aims to estimate a hedonic price model to assess whether environmental and social responsibility practices are associated with a price premium. Utilizing a sample of online retail prices for Montepulciano d’Abruzzo wine, we lever
content: This study aims to estimate a hedonic price model to assess whether environmental and social responsibility practices are associated with a price premium. Utilizing a sample of online retail prices for Montepulciano d’Abruzzo wine, we leverage the fact that winery websites and online stores provide more detailed and comprehensive information about producers than wine labels, allowing consumers to make more informed and ethically motivated purchasing decisions. The results confirm that consumers are willing to pay a premium price for wines certified as organic or biodynamic. However, we find no significant evidence that other social responsibility practices influence the price. Nevertheless, this result should not be directly interpreted as a lack of consumer interest in socially responsible practices, but rather as a potential consequence of imperfect information.

title: Recent Trends and Industrial Applications of Microbially Fabricated 2,3-Butanediol
summary: The non-oxidative metabolism of microorganisms produces 2,3-butanediol (BD), which has a wide range of industrial applications and a high market value. A particular focus has been placed on its microbial production as 218 a substitute for p
content: The non-oxidative metabolism of microorganisms produces 2,3-butanediol (BD), which has a wide range of industrial applications and a high market value. A particular focus has been placed on its microbial production as 218 a substitute for petroleum-based production. Many 2,3-BD-producing microorganisms, including yeast and bacteria, have been segregated and their metabolisms extensively changed in order to technically manufacture 2,3-BD. In comparison to chemical-based processes, microbial production of 2,3-BD is thought to be more environmentally sustainable. The viability of the microbial production process on a commercial scale is constrained by this high energy consumption. The selection of the top strains and methodical optimization of the fermentation conditions are necessary for increased 2,3-BD production. Additionally, metabolic pathway engineering is necessary to optimize outcomes and reduce production costs by making the strains adept at utilizing inexpensive substrates. Currently, renewable energy sources, whose greatest benefit is their environmental friendliness, are used as raw materials in microbial fermentation, which is how most 2,3-BD is produced. A number of fermentation techniques have been put to the test using raw materials like lignocellulose, starch, sugar, and glycerol as feed-stocks. This chapter will present current details on the parameters and strategies for increased microbial 2,3-BD production.

title: Pooled prevalence and associated factors of overweight/obesity among under-five children in 46 low- and middle-income countries: A cross-sectional analysis of Demographic and Health Surveys data (2015–2024)
summary: Overweight and obesity remain major global public health challenges, particularly among children under five years of age in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). This study aimed to assess the pooled prevalence of overweight/obesity and
content: Overweight and obesity remain major global public health challenges, particularly among children under five years of age in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). This study aimed to assess the pooled prevalence of overweight/obesity and its associated factors among children aged 6-59 months in 46 LMICs. We used the most recent nationally representative demographic and health surveys (2015-2024) from forty-six LMICs. A total of 393,638 weighted samples of children aged 6-59 months were included. Childhood overweight and obesity were defined as weight-for-height greater than two and three standard deviations above the WHO reference population median, respectively. Multilevel log-binomial regression models were employed. An adjusted risk ratio (RR) with a 95% confidence interval (CI) was used to select variables that had a significant association with childhood overweight/obesity. A p value < 0.05 was used to declare statistical significance. The data were analyzed with R software (version 4.5.1). The pooled prevalence of overweight/obesity was 3% (95% CI: 2.44, 3.58), with significant regional variation ranging from 1.62% in West Africa to 10% in the Europe and Central Asia (95% CI: 5.26, 17.84). Male sex (RR = 1.07, 95% CI: 1.03, 1.11), larger-than-average birth size (RR = 1.66, 95% CI: 1.54, 1.78), facility delivery (RR = 1.20, 95% CI: 1.13, 1.27), maternal smoking (RR = 1.61, 95% CI: 1.38, 1.87), maternal overweighed/obesity (RR = 2.37, 95% CI: 2.19-2.56), media exposure (RR = 1.05, 95% CI: 1.01, 1.10), and rich (RR = 1.10, 95% CI: 1.04, 1.16) household wealth were factors associated with increased risk. Children aged 24-59 months had lower risk compared to those aged 6-23 months. Protective factors included current breastfeeding (RR = 0.91, 95% CI: 0.87, 0.95), interpregnancy intervals 18-23 months (RR = 0.77, 95% CI: 0.71, 0.83), and ≥ 24 months (RR = 0.87 95% CI: 0.83, 0.91), and multiple births (RR = 0.67, 95% CI: 0.57, 0.79). Contextually, children in medium-human development index (HDI) (RR = 1.80, 95% CI: 1.62, 2.00) and higher-HDI countries (RR = 3.57, 95% CI: 3.00, 4.24) had elevated risk. Compared to West Africa, all other regions showed significantly higher risk, with Europe & Central Asia demonstrated the strongest association (RR = 3.37, 95% CI: 2.90, 3.91). The pooled prevalence of overweight/obesity among under-five children in LMICs is relatively low compared to high-income nations, yet substantial regional variation exists. Male sex, larger size at birth, maternal smoking, maternal overweight/obesity, higher household wealth quantiles and higher-HDI were associated with increased risk of childhood overweight/obesity, whereas current breastfeeding and longer interpregnancy intervals were protective. These findings highlight the importance of close monitoring of the problem and region-specific interventions targeting modifiable risk factors.

title: Microalgal Biohydrogen an Insight into Recent Advances Glitches and Solutions
summary: Microalgae are a renewable resource that can be used to manufacture biohydrogen ( https://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"> bio-H 2 ). As a result, this contributes to both the energy problem and global warming. The discovery o
content: Microalgae are a renewable resource that can be used to manufacture biohydrogen ( https://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"> bio-H 2 ). As a result, this contributes to both the energy problem and global warming. The discovery of various valuable metabolites as byproducts of the https://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"> bio-H 2 generation process has received a lot of attention in recent years. The use of microalgae for https://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"> bio-H 2 production is exceptional because 46 of their carbon-mitigating effects and their use of solar energy. https://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"> bio-H 2 production can be achieved through microbial methods. In this chapter, the authors discussed the enzymes and influencing parameters necessary for bio-H₂ production, as well as the state-of-the-art techniques currently employed to produce bio-H₂ from microalgal feedstock. Commercial certification of processes based on microalgal bio-H₂ production is still lacking. There are significant obstacles to implementing https://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"> bio-H 2 production on a commercial scale, including low https://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"> bio-H 2 yield and high production costs. This chapter proposes a method for commercializing https://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"> bio-H 2 production using microalgae that involves an integrated production process. Further, we discuss the importance of process integration to boost efficiency, as well as the application of cutting-edge strategies to increase https://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"> bio-H 2 production and economic viability, and the demand for further study.

title: Monokristal, polikristal ve ince film fotovoltaik hücrelerin karşılaştırmalı analizi: Verim, sıcaklık ve ışınım etkileri
source: Ömer Halisdemir Üniversitesi Mühendislik Bilimleri Dergisi
summary: Bu çalışmada, monokristal, polikristal ve ince film fotovoltaik (FV) hücrelerin verim, sıcaklık ve güneş ışınımı etkileri açısından karşılaştırmalı olarak incelenmesi amaçlanmıştır. Bu kapsamda, seçilen ticari modüllere ait teknik parametre
content: Bu çalışmada, monokristal, polikristal ve ince film fotovoltaik (FV) hücrelerin verim, sıcaklık ve güneş ışınımı etkileri açısından karşılaştırmalı olarak incelenmesi amaçlanmıştır. Bu kapsamda, seçilen ticari modüllere ait teknik parametreler kullanılarak MATLAB ortamında sıcaklık ve güneş ışınımının hücre verimi üzerindeki etkilerine yönelik sayısal hesaplamalar gerçekleştirilmiştir. Elde edilen bulgular, monokristal hücrelerin sınırlı alanlarda yüksek verim sunduğunu, polikristal hücrelerin maliyet-performans açısından büyük ölçekli uygulamalar için uygun olduğunu ve ince film hücrelerin ise yüksek sıcaklık ve düşük ışınım koşullarında daha kararlı bir performans sergilediğini göstermektedir. Sonuç olarak, FV hücre seçiminde yalnızca nominal verim değerlerinin değil, iklim koşulları, çevresel etkiler ve uygulama gereksinimlerinin de birlikte değerlendirilmesi gerektiği ortaya konulmuştur.

title: Study and Characterization of Heat Storage Materials Composed of Clay, Laterite, and Slag from the Maradi Region of Niger
summary: In this study, raw materials composed of clay, laterite, and clinker were characterized in order to analyse their thermal and thermogravimetric behaviour and validate their use as heat storage materials in thermodynamic power plants. The ra
content: In this study, raw materials composed of clay, laterite, and clinker were characterized in order to analyse their thermal and thermogravimetric behaviour and validate their use as heat storage materials in thermodynamic power plants. The raw materials were first ground (to a particle size of 100µm) and characterized using various methods (X-ray fluorescence spectrometry, X-ray diffraction, differential scanning calorimetry, thermogravimetric analysis) to better understand their different properties. This characterization made it possible to determine the various physicochemical properties of these raw materials. The aim is to make use of local materials such as clay, laterite from the Maradi region, and ash from the SONICHAR thermal power plant in order to develop new ceramic composite materials with good mechanical and thermal properties for use in thermodynamic power plants:

title: ECOLOGICAL AND ECONOMIC MECHANISMS FOR STIMULATING THE IMPLEMENTATION OF GREEN PROJECTS AT THE TERRITORIAL LEVEL UNDER CLIMATE CHANGE CONDITIONS
summary: The article discusses the ecological and economic mechanisms for stimulating the implementation of "green" projects at the territorial level in the context of climate change. The relevance of the transition to a "green" economy as a tool fo
content: The article discusses the ecological and economic mechanisms for stimulating the implementation of "green" projects at the territorial level in the context of climate change. The relevance of the transition to a "green" economy as a tool for reducing environmental risks and increasing the sustainability of socio-economic development is substantiated. The existing economic, institutional and investment mechanisms for supporting "green" projects are analyzed. The main problems of their implementation in the Russian Federation have been identified. A system of ecological and economic incentive mechanisms is proposed, taking into account the interaction of government authorities, business and society.

title: Reliability of multi-criteria decision making methods in stock selection: evidence from Istanbul Stock Exchange
summary: This study offers a practical framework for investors and financial decision-makers who must evaluate multiple criteria when selecting stocks. Traditional approaches often rely on subjective judgments, while this research applies two struct
content: This study offers a practical framework for investors and financial decision-makers who must evaluate multiple criteria when selecting stocks. Traditional approaches often rely on subjective judgments, while this research applies two structured multi-criteria decision-making methods: the Preference Selection Index (PSI) and the Evaluation Based on Distance from Average Solution (EDAS). PSI provides a simple and objective way to rank stocks because it does not require assigning weights to criteria. EDAS helps practitioners identify stocks that perform better than the market average by measuring their distance from the mean. Both methods are easy to implement, transparent, and suitable for environments with many alternatives. The results show how these techniques can support more consistent, data-driven stock selection and examine whether the rankings are related to future returns. The framework can be used by individual investors, portfolio managers, and financial institutions seeking a systematic and replicable selection process.

title: Synergistic Color Retention of Charcoal Pigment in Triticum aestivum subsp. Flour Mediated by Plant Polyphenols and Mineral Salts
source: International Journal of Scientific Research in Science and Technology
summary: Natural food colors are in high demand owing to their benefits to human health, but they also have disadvantages. Natural food coloring frequently has poor stability, which restricts its industrial use. The goal of this study was to create
content: Natural food colors are in high demand owing to their benefits to human health, but they also have disadvantages. Natural food coloring frequently has poor stability, which restricts its industrial use. The goal of this study was to create a stable natural black food color. The stabilization of black color is described in this paper by using mordants such as Pure Starch, Corn starch, rice flour, Guar Gum, Tannin, NaCl, and Sodium Bicarbonate, Citrus sinensis (L.) Osbeck. In the food industry, this composition has potential as a substitute for artificial black food coloring. Starting with the stabilization of black charcoal dye by Guar Gum, Citrus sinensis (L.) Osbeck., and NaHCO3, their binding and stabilizing abilities are mentioned. Followed by Rice Flour, Corn Starch, Pure Starch, and tannin, which gave better results and imparted an even black color, NaCl enhanced the black color and binding capacity.

title: Material Degradation of Heat-Resistant Steels during Long-Term Creep Exposure
summary: Creep strength and material degradation of heat-resistant steel were discussed, focusing on microstructural changes during long-term creep exposure. The materials and creep rupture data were obtained from Creep Data Sheet Project by Nationa
content: Creep strength and material degradation of heat-resistant steel were discussed, focusing on microstructural changes during long-term creep exposure. The materials and creep rupture data were obtained from Creep Data Sheet Project by National Institute for Materials Science. For determining the allowable stress, the 100,000 h creep rupture strength should be evaluated based on creep rupture data. The selection of TTP and dividing the creep rupture data set are important to evaluate long-term creep strength when creep strength degradation occurs in the long term. In order to establish the allowable stress, minimum creep strength must also be evaluated. The minimum creep strength depends on the standard error of estimate (SEE) for creep rupture data. If the heat-to-heat variation of creep strength is large even for the same material specification, the value of SEE is estimated to be large. Therefore, it is important to clarify the reason for the heat-to-heat variation of creep strength in terms of microstructural changes and chemical compositions. Microstructural degradations were reported for carbon steels, low alloy steels, 9–12%Cr ferritic steels and austenitic heat-resistant steels, focusing on precipitates and dislocation structures. The reason for the heat-to-heat variation of creep rupture strength was discussed in term of the difference of solute atoms, segregation and grain size.

title: Natural Polymers and Bio-Based Additives as Pour Point Depressants for Flow Assurance of Waxy Crude Oil Pipelines: A Review
source: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF ENGINEERING AND MODERN TECHNOLOGY
summary: Waxy crude oils create persistent flow assurance challenges in petroleum pipelines because paraffinic waxes precipitate, crystallize and deposit when temperature falls below wax appearance conditions. These processes increase viscosity, pro
content: Waxy crude oils create persistent flow assurance challenges in petroleum pipelines because paraffinic waxes precipitate, crystallize and deposit when temperature falls below wax appearance conditions. These processes increase viscosity, promote gel formation, raise pumping and restart pressure, reduce pipeline capacity and may eventually cause blockage. Conventional synthetic pour point depressants, including ethylene-vinyl acetate copolymers, polyacrylates, polymethacrylates and related comb polymers, remain important chemical-control options because they can modify wax crystal growth and reduce crystal-network strength. However, their petroleum-derived origin, crude-specific performance, environmental concerns and cost have encouraged increasing interest in natural polymers and bio-based additives. This review evaluates the prospects of natural polymers and bio-based materials as greener pour point depressants for waxy crude oil pipelines. It synthesizes literature on wax deposition, mechanisms of pour point depression, conventional chemical additives, bio-derived flow improvers, performance indicators and practical limitations. The review concludes that natural polymers and bio-based additives are promising, but they should not yet be presented as universal substitutes for commercial synthetic depressants. Their industrial value depends on reproducible composition, crude-specific testing, rheological validation, compatibility assessment, economic analysis and field-scale confirmation.

title: Cyber security risk assessment methods for energy systems: A systematic literature review
source: Journal of Information Security and Applications
summary: In recent decades, energy control networks have turned from ‘isolated islands’ into a large-scale, digitalized smart grid with ecosystem-like interdependencies. This shift opens the way for various cyber risks that were impossible beforehan
content: In recent decades, energy control networks have turned from ‘isolated islands’ into a large-scale, digitalized smart grid with ecosystem-like interdependencies. This shift opens the way for various cyber risks that were impossible beforehand. These cyber risks must be carefully assessed and treated to ensure the smooth operation of one of the most vital industries for society and the economy. The review examines the Cybersecurity Risk Assessment (CRA) approaches designed with a particular focus on energy systems. Despite the critical importance of the topic, there is no comprehensive study examining achievements in CRA for the energy sector. This article identifies the key peculiarities of the energy sector and establishes the criteria for CRA methodologies within the energy domain. We identify the existing CRA approaches designed for the energy sector, examine their core aspects, and analyse them against our energy-specific criteria. The review considers the problem from different angles, including the evaluation of mature CRA frameworks, comprehensive CRA approaches, and those CRA methods which focus on assessing a specific threat or system type. Our analysis reveals key gaps and outlines research directions for enhancing energy-specific CRA frameworks. This review is particularly valuable for cybersecurity IT specialists applying and designing CRA frameworks for the energy sector.

title: Applying social acceptance theory to urban logistics: Insights and research priorities
summary: Planning for urban logistics innovations is increasingly considered as part of broader transport and urban planning, amplifying the complexity of these planning processes. In this research note, we apply social acceptance (SA) theory, tradi
content: Planning for urban logistics innovations is increasingly considered as part of broader transport and urban planning, amplifying the complexity of these planning processes. In this research note, we apply social acceptance (SA) theory, traditionally applied to energy technologies, to understand the complexity surrounding adoption of urban logistics innovations by different segments of society. The theory encompasses three dimensions: socio-political acceptance, community acceptance and market acceptance, which are essential for the successful adoption of new technologies by providing insights on stakeholder interests. We illustrate this application through Seamless, a structured process which supports sustainable logistics innovation while addressing social acceptance. Seamless employs stakeholder mapping, qualitative governance analysis, stakeholder needs identification and survey data methods. Employed in four Living Labs, Seamless illustrates the value of SA, while also confronting the reality that logistics stakeholders tend to focus on market and socio-political acceptance and engaging community stakeholders directly can be challenging. We see SA as a promising approach for urban logistics innovations worthy of further exploration.

title: Thermal Analysis of POP Ceiling Boards Produced with Palm Petiole Fibres
source: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF ENGINEERING AND MODERN TECHNOLOGY
summary: The high demand for sustainable and energy-efficient building materials has encouraged the incorporation of natural fibres into construction products. This study presents the thermal analysis of a plaster of Paris (POP) ceiling board reinfo
content: The high demand for sustainable and energy-efficient building materials has encouraged the incorporation of natural fibres into construction products. This study presents the thermal analysis of a plaster of Paris (POP) ceiling board reinforced with palm petiole fibres. Palm petiole fibres, an abundant agricultural waste, were extracted using water retting process, treated with sodium hydroxide, and incorporated into the POP matrix at varying fibre contents to evaluate their influence on thermal performance. The fabricated ceiling boards were subjected to thermal conductivity, thermal resistivity, and specific heat capacity tests using standard experimental procedures. The best sample produced is 0.55% higher than the standard value range of POP thermal conductivity, 0.54% lower than the standard value range of POP thermal resistivity, and 17.8% lower than the standard value range of POP specific heat capacity. The results indicate that the inclusion of palm petiole fibres significantly reduces the thermal conductivity of the POP ceiling board compared to conventional POP boards, thereby improving its thermal insulation capability. This reduction is attributed to the low thermal conductivity and porous structure of the natural fibres, which hinder heat flow within the composite material. The study demonstrates that palm petiole fibre–reinforced POP ceiling boards have strong potential as a cost-effective, eco-friendly, and thermally efficient alternative for ceiling applications in residential and commercial buildings.
