title: Perbandingan Penggunaan Pupuk NPK dan KCl Sebagai Sumber Nutrisi Optimal Saccharomyces cerevisiae Untuk Produksi Bioetanol dari Tandan Kosong Kelapa Sawit (TKKS)
summary: Tandan kosong kelapa sawit (TKKS) merupakan limbah lignoselulosa yang berpotensi sebagai bahan baku bioetanol, namun hidrolisatnya miskin unsur hara (N, P, K) sehingga menghambat pertumbuhan dan aktivitas fermentatif Saccharomyces cerevisia
content: Tandan kosong kelapa sawit (TKKS) merupakan limbah lignoselulosa yang berpotensi sebagai bahan baku bioetanol, namun hidrolisatnya miskin unsur hara (N, P, K) sehingga menghambat pertumbuhan dan aktivitas fermentatif Saccharomyces cerevisiae . Penelitian ini bertujuan mengetahui pengaruh pupuk NPK dan KCl terhadap pertumbuhan S. cerevisiae , perbedaan signifikan antara keduanya sebagai sumber nutrisi terhadap kadar bioetanol, serta rasio nutrisi paling optimal dalam produksi bioetanol dari TKKS. Penelitian menggunakan Rancangan Acak Lengkap (RAL) dengan enam perlakuan, yaitu kontrol (P0) serta rasio KCl:NPK 4:0 (P1), 3:1 (P2), 2:2 (P3), 1:3 (P4), dan 0:4 (P5), masing-masing empat ulangan. Fermentasi dilakukan selama 7 hari pada pH 4 dan suhu ruang. Pertumbuhan khamir diukur dengan OD600, sedangkan kadar bioetanol diukur dengan refraktometer. Data dianalisis menggunakan uji One-Way ANOVA dan uji lanjut Tukey HSD pada taraf kepercayaan 95%. Hasil menunjukkan nilai OD meningkat pada seluruh perlakuan, tertinggi pada rasio 2:2 (0,789) dan terendah pada kontrol (0,331). Uji ANOVA menunjukkan variasi rasio KCl dan NPK berpengaruh sangat nyata terhadap kadar bioetanol (F(5,18) = 41,830; p < 0,001). Uji Tukey HSD mengelompokkan perlakuan menjadi tiga subset: kontrol (11,6%) berbeda nyata dari seluruh perlakuan bernutrisi; rasio 4:0 (13,3%) membentuk subset tersendiri; sementara rasio 0:4, 3:1, 1:3, dan 2:2 (14,4–15,3%) tidak berbeda nyata satu sama lain namun berbeda nyata dari kontrol dan rasio 4:0. Kadar bioetanol tertinggi diperoleh pada rasio 2:2 (15,3%). Disimpulkan bahwa nutrisi KCl dan NPK berpengaruh terhadap pertumbuhan S. cerevisiae dan kadar bioetanol dari TKKS, dengan rasio KCl:NPK 2:2 sebagai rasio paling optimal.

title: GIS-based scalable rooftop solar mapping in Bangkok using multi-resolution segmentation, adaptive footprint regularization, and climate-aware generation modeling
summary: Rapid expansion of rooftop photovoltaic (PV) systems requires scalable methods for estimating capacity and generation for grid planning. This paper presents an end-to-end workflow integrating multi-resolution satellite image segmentation, G
content: Rapid expansion of rooftop photovoltaic (PV) systems requires scalable methods for estimating capacity and generation for grid planning. This paper presents an end-to-end workflow integrating multi-resolution satellite image segmentation, GIS-ready footprint regularization, and climate-aware solar generation modeling. Using a Bangkok case study, we evaluate U-Net and U-Net++ architectures across 10-cm, 30-cm, and 50-cm resolutions. Results show that 30-cm imagery largely preserves the 10-cm segmentation fidelity, whereas 50-cm imagery degrades substantially. To support spatial analysis and capacity estimation, we introduce an adaptive regularization framework optimizing area similarity, orthogonality, and node parsimony. The method reduces mean node-count error by 94%, and improves footprint orthogonality from 0.28 to 0.99. Furthermore, coupling footprints with meteorological data captures seasonal irradiance variability and temperature derating, revealing monthly generation deviations ranging from −7.5% to +11.4%. Ultimately, robust operational PV inventories require coordinating imagery resolution, vector usability, and dynamic climate forcing to effectively support grid planning in tropical urban environments.

title: A Solar Power Forecasting Model Using the Whale Optimization Algorithm
summary: This paper presents a Whale Optimization Algorithm (WOA)-based solar power forecasting framework targeting improved prediction accuracy due to the inherent irregularity and nonlinearity of photovoltaic power generation. A comprehensive lite
content: This paper presents a Whale Optimization Algorithm (WOA)-based solar power forecasting framework targeting improved prediction accuracy due to the inherent irregularity and nonlinearity of photovoltaic power generation. A comprehensive literature review highlighted the limitations of conventional statistical methods and the dependency of machine learning and deep learning models on appropriate parameter tuning. To overcome these challenges, WOA was integrated with a forecasting model to ideally tune model parameters and improve the generalization capability. Data collection, preprocessing, model development, WOA-based parameter optimization, and rigorous performance evaluation were some of the steps efficiently used in this method. Methodological clarity and reproducibility were ensured through mathematical modeling of WOA, algorithmic implementation, and a detailed flowchart provided. Results demonstrated that the proposed WOA-based model consistently outperformed the baseline models and other optimization techniques, such as Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), in terms of performance efficiency. Performance evaluation using standard metrics, including Root Mean Square Error (RMSE), Mean Absolute Error (MAE), and Mean Squared Error (MSE), demonstrated a significant reduction in forecasting errors with the proposed approach. Comparative and convergence analysis showcased that the given method achieves an RMSE of 577.320, an MAE of 459.563, and an MSE of 333298.025, indicating reduced forecasting errors compared to Artificial Neural Networks (ANN), GA-ANN, and PSO-ANN.

title: Oil and Gas Supply Chains in Africa: Structure, Actors, and Flow of Materials
source: International Journal of Supply Chain and Logistics
summary: Purpose: This paper evaluates the oil and gas sector in Africa through a supply chain approach, arguing that developmental performance is shaped not by resource endowment alone but by the interaction between chain structure, actor power, an
content: Purpose: This paper evaluates the oil and gas sector in Africa through a supply chain approach, arguing that developmental performance is shaped not by resource endowment alone but by the interaction between chain structure, actor power, and material flows. Methodology: The article deploys the qualitative study of secondary data based on the synthesis approaches to trace the transnational material flows using the upstream, midstream and downstream segments and firmly imprints a comparative case study of Nigeria, Mozambique and Algeria. These illustrations depict how different formations of the actors and infrastructure constructions produce different flow effects such as extensive leakage and reliance on imports and more centralized but stringent control. Findings: The findings show that the partial governance and underperforming midstream integration bring about a massive loss of value in form of flaring, theft, bottlenecks, and circular trade structures. Formation of enclaves and export-oriented economical organization diminishes national inter-relatedness, and lack of undercapacity in the downstream will guarantee dependence on imported refined products. More unified systems achieve a tradeoff between sovereignty and efficiency. Overall, there is no correspondence between the formal possession of the resources and their efficient management in terms of development Unique Contribution to Theory, Practice, and Policy: The article also contributes to the scholarship on extractive industry by creating an interdisciplinary flow of flow, which relates the aspects of governance and political economy to the embodied realities of logistics and infrastructure. The policy implications are based on the fact that the country should not just leave on fiscal policies but should go to the extent of integrating supply chain, governing infrastructure and having institutional capability. To the companies, the research indicates hazards of failing to analyze risks in ecosystem-based analysis which extends beyond a project to a whole supply chain.

title: A Stepwise Parameter Identification Method for an Electrochemical–Thermal Coupled Model of Lithium-Ion Batteries Based on Global Sensitivity Analysis
summary: Abstract The pseudo-two-dimensional (P2D) model provides a physics-based description of lithium-ion battery behavior, but its numerous strongly coupled electrochemical and thermal parameters make simultaneous voltage and temperature predict
content: Abstract The pseudo-two-dimensional (P2D) model provides a physics-based description of lithium-ion battery behavior, but its numerous strongly coupled electrochemical and thermal parameters make simultaneous voltage and temperature prediction challenging. This study proposes a multi-stage parameter identification method for an electrochemical–thermal coupled P2D model. Sobol global sensitivity analysis with Saltelli sampling is first used to quantify the effects of model parameters on voltage and temperature responses under different operating conditions. Based on the sensitivity results, a stage-wise multi-objective identification strategy is developed, with adaptive weights determined from normalized sensitivity indices. A hybrid Whale Optimization Algorithm–Differential Evolution (WOA–DE) method is then employed for parameter optimization. Compared with the original model, voltage prediction errors are reduced by 25.68%, 42.13%, and 47.48% under 0.5 C, HPPC, and DST conditions, respectively, while temperature errors decrease by 37.97%, 45.16%, and 30.96%. Under dynamic conditions, the model achieves RMSEs of 10.21 mV for voltage and 0.115 °C for temperature. The results demonstrate improved prediction accuracy and robustness for coupled voltage–temperature responses.

title: Acoustic Microbots: Linking Fabrication Techniques to Acoustic Actuation Mechanisms—A Systematic Review
summary: ABSTRACT Acoustic fields are emerging as a promising wireless and tissue‐penetrant power source for micro‐ and nanorobots, with propulsion efficiency, steering precision, and biocompatibility all critically linked to fabrication strategy. T
content: ABSTRACT Acoustic fields are emerging as a promising wireless and tissue‐penetrant power source for micro‐ and nanorobots, with propulsion efficiency, steering precision, and biocompatibility all critically linked to fabrication strategy. To clarify these interdependencies, we conducted a Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta‐Analyses (PRISMA)‐guided systematic review of literature from Scopus, Web of Science, PubMed, and IEEE Xplore (January 1, 2010–May 31 2025). Of 144 records, 63 primary studies and 22 secondary/background sources met predefined criteria and were synthesized. The evidence reveals five dominant actuation modes: boundary‐driven streaming (~40%), bubble oscillation (~25%), acoustic radiation forces (~12%), whole‐body resonance (~13%), and hybrid magneto‐/chemo‐acoustic mechanisms (~9%), each shaped by distinct fabrication approaches. Photolithography produces sharp fins for high‐Re streaming; soft lithography forms gas‐tight cavities for cavitation; two‐photon and micro‐DLP printing achieve nanometer‐scale smoothness for radiation‐pressure traps; and emerging multimaterial printers combine rigid acoustic chambers with magnetic or catalytic components. Three themes recur: (i) geometry–material–control co‐design consistently outperforms sequential prototyping; (ii) scalability and biocompatibility remain major barriers, with ad hoc quality metrics; and (iii) inverse‐design algorithms and closed‐loop acoustic imaging are accelerating optimization. This review maps fabrication techniques to actuation demands and application contexts, offering a consolidated roadmap toward clinically and industrially viable acoustic microrobots.

title: Counselling Nigerian Youth in the Fourth Industrial Revolution: Implications for National Development
source: Journal of Counseling and Educational Research
summary: This conceptual paper examines how technological innovation, particularly the Fourth Industrial Revolution (4IR), artificial intelligence, and automation, is reshaping the world of work and the career-adjustment demands facing Nigerian yout
content: This conceptual paper examines how technological innovation, particularly the Fourth Industrial Revolution (4IR), artificial intelligence, and automation, is reshaping the world of work and the career-adjustment demands facing Nigerian youth. Drawing on a structured synthesis of peer-reviewed literature, national policy documents, and international labour-market reports published between 2015 and 2026, the paper analyses three interlocking shifts: the restructuring of global and Nigerian labour markets, the transformation of work values and occupational identity, and the counselling responses required to support youth adjustment. The World Economic Forum's Future of Jobs Report 2025 projects that 92 million jobs will be displaced and 170 million created by 2030, with 39% of existing skill sets requiring transformation. Nigeria's ICT sector contributed approximately 19.8% of real GDP in the second quarter of 2024, while youth unemployment estimates range from 6.5% under the National Bureau of Statistics' revised methodology to over 50% under civil-society assessments, underscoring the scale of adjustment required. The paper argues that professional counsellors occupy a strategic position for translating these macro-level shifts into individual career resilience, and concludes with prioritised, actor-specific recommendations for counsellor education, professional bodies, curriculum policy, and government agencies to strengthen Nigeria's national human-capital response.

title: Silica Nanoparticles from Sustainable Sources: Fundamentals of Processing and Emerging Strategies
summary: The transition from conventional silica nanoparticle (SiNP) production based on purified alkoxysilanes and high-temperature flame hydrolysis of silicon tetrachloride to renewable and waste-derived silicon resources requires more than precur
content: The transition from conventional silica nanoparticle (SiNP) production based on purified alkoxysilanes and high-temperature flame hydrolysis of silicon tetrachloride to renewable and waste-derived silicon resources requires more than precursor substitution. It requires a mechanistic understanding of how feedstock mineralogy, silicon speciation, impurity chemistry, and processing history propagate through dissolution, nucleation, condensation, gelation, aging, drying, and pore evolution to determine material performance, environmental burden, and manufacturing feasibility. Although previous reviews have established the technical feasibility of producing silica from secondary resources, their predominant organization by feedstock, synthesis route, or application provides limited ability to explain why nominally similar processes generate materials with markedly different structural and functional properties. This review addresses these through a resource-pull, feedstock-to-function framework that links resource chemistry and process design to critical material attributes, application-specific specifications, sustainability, and scale-up requirements. Agricultural residues, industrial by-products, geothermal resources, waste glass, and fluorosilicate streams are critically compared according to silicon form and phase, reactivity, impurity profile, compositional variability, purification demand, and attainable product quality. Particular attention is given to waste-derived alkaline silicate systems, in which molecular, oligomeric, and colloidal silica coexist and therefore require characterization beyond bulk SiO2 concentration. Established and emerging processing strategies, including controlled combustion and alkaline extraction, alkali fusion, ambient-pressure drying, microwave and mechanochemical activation, biogenic and biomimetic templating, and continuous processing, are evaluated according to their mechanistic effects, technological maturity, structural control, and demands for energy, reagents, water, solvents, effluent treatment, and capital. Across these routes, gelation and aging emerge as critical transfer stages through which feedstock composition is translated into network connectivity, pore architecture, shrinkage behavior, and ultimately functional performance. Evidence from secondary-source aerogels further shows that properly controlled waste-derived systems can attain BET surface areas of approximately 350–500 m2 g−1, within the textural range of many alkoxide-derived materials, indicating that feedstock variability, impurity management, and process control are more important constraints than an inherently lower performance ceiling. On this basis, this review proposes a minimum evidence framework comprising feedstock traceability, intermediate-speciation and colloidal characterization, silicon mass balance, gelation and aging metrics, application-specific qualification criteria, performance-normalized life cycle and techno-economi

title: A-CPES: A Reference Framework for Agentic AI in Cyber-Physical Energy Systems
summary: Energy system operation contains a loop of work that automation has never taken over: posing the optimization problem the current cycle should solve, disposing of infeasibility, sequencing a solution into interlocked switching orders, assem
content: Energy system operation contains a loop of work that automation has never taken over: posing the optimization problem the current cycle should solve, disposing of infeasibility, sequencing a solution into interlocked switching orders, assembling evidence no single model holds, negotiating adjustable capacity with many parties, and settling experience into practice. Licensed dispatchers carry all of it in person, and the rising share of variable renewable generation is making that loop turn faster than their number can grow. Agentic AI supplies the abilities it requires, but enters as the outer loop of control: it calls SCED and the other decision models rather than being called by them. We propose A-CPES, three nested rings, an authorization and accountability frame around an agentic control outer loop around a six-layer CPES core. We argue the loop is indivisible, tune where and how tightly it may close, state eight structural failure modes as falsifiable predictions, and specify six governance modules that rebuild the authorization frame until it covers the loop, before the loop starts turning.

title: High‐Output Moisture‐Electric Generator Based on High‐Conductive Anti‐Freezing Poly(Acrylamide)/NaCl Ionic Hydrogel
summary: ABSTRACT Moisture‐electric generators (MEGs) have emerged as a promising strategy for harvesting energy from omnipresent atmospheric moisture, which is still compromised by restricted electrical output and harsh working temperatures. Herein
content: ABSTRACT Moisture‐electric generators (MEGs) have emerged as a promising strategy for harvesting energy from omnipresent atmospheric moisture, which is still compromised by restricted electrical output and harsh working temperatures. Herein, a high‐output MEG based on high‐conductive anti‐freezing poly(acrylamide)/NaCl ionic hydrogel (PNIH) is developed to convert ambient chemical potential energy into electricity. The PNIH‐based MEG (PNIH‐MEG) can achieve excellent electrical outputs with a continuous output voltage of 1.6 V for 16 days, a current density of 1.2 mA/cm 2 , and a power density of 129 µW/cm 2 , which is attributed to synergistic effects of moisture‐induced ion migration, interfacial electrical double layer, interfacial reactions, and high conductivity of PNIH. Especially, the persistent voltage output (1.6 V) of the PNIH‐MEG is still maintained even under harsh working conditions of low temperature (−20°C) and low relative humidity (20% RH), which indicates a fascinating all‐weather operational capability. Furthermore, an integrated array composed of 72 MEGs in series or 6 MEGs in parallel generates a voltage of 120 V or a current of 5.0 mA, respectively, which can further charge commercial capacitors and directly power ten thermohydrometers. Consequently, this work demonstrates new insights for designing renewable, clean, and sustainable power generation with high‐output performance and environmental adaptability.

title: Transmission Loss Prediction Using Neural Networks With Correlation‐Derived Input Features
summary: ABSTRACT Accurate prediction of transmission losses is essential for efficient operation and planning of modern power systems under increasingly dynamic operating conditions driven by renewable energy integration and weather‐dependent varia
content: ABSTRACT Accurate prediction of transmission losses is essential for efficient operation and planning of modern power systems under increasingly dynamic operating conditions driven by renewable energy integration and weather‐dependent variability. This paper proposes a neural network–based framework for transmission loss prediction that improves predictive performance through correlation‐derived input features. The methodology integrates operational power system measurements, meteorological variables, and analytically derived input features designed to capture temporal patterns and nonlinear dependencies in system behavior. Two derived input features are introduced: a 24‐h loss‐pattern forecast and a pattern‐matched loss feature, to capture historical pattern similarity directly in the model inputs. The framework is validated using 4 years of hourly operational and meteorological data from the transmission system of Bosnia and Herzegovina. The baseline MLP achieves a mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) of 14.40% on the test dataset. Incorporating the 24‐h loss‐pattern forecast feature reduces the prediction error to 13.29%, while the pattern‐matched loss feature provides a modest improvement relative to the baseline configuration. The results demonstrate that correlation‐derived inputs enhance prediction accuracy while maintaining model simplicity and computational efficiency.

title: Gamma-irradiated PVA/chitosan/moringa extract edible coatings for postharvest quality and insect control in Siwi dates
source: Journal of Bioactive and Compatible Polymers
summary: Siwi dates are highly nutritious, versatile, and naturally energy-rich. However, prolonged storage often results in quality deterioration due to pests and microbial contamination, leading to texture changes, insect infestation, and loss of
content: Siwi dates are highly nutritious, versatile, and naturally energy-rich. However, prolonged storage often results in quality deterioration due to pests and microbial contamination, leading to texture changes, insect infestation, and loss of flavor and nutrients. To address these challenges, environmentally friendly preservation strategies have been explored to safeguard this valuable crop. In this study, we report the synthesis of a sustainable edible coating formulated from moringa extract (ME) incorporated into polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) and chitosan (CS) matrices, prepared via γ-irradiation. Different ratios of moringa extract (ME) (3, 5, 10, and 15%) were successfully incorporated into PVA/CS matrix to synthesize four distinct PVA/CS/ME coating solutions. For efficient characterization, PVA/CS/ME films containing 10% ME were fabricated using the casting method, and their properties were examined by FTIR, XRD, and tensile testing. FTIR and XRD analyses confirmed the effective interaction between ME and the PVA/CS matrix. Increasing the ME concentration within the PVA/CS matrix imparted significant antibacterial activity against Staphylococcus aureus and Escherichia coli , attributed to ME phytochemicals, thereby highlighting the films’ potential as active food packaging materials that enhance safety and extend shelf life. Furthermore, four PVA/CS/ME coating solutions were applied as edible coatings to extend the shelf life and maintain the quality of Siwi dates during 6 months of storage at room temperature (65–70% RH). Quality parameters, including insect infestation (%), weight loss (%), moisture content (%), browning index, total soluble solids, and pH, were monitored throughout the storage period. The coating solution containing 15% ME demonstrated the most pronounced effect, effectively reducing insect infestation and preserving fruit quality. These findings highlight a promising eco-friendly approach for the long-term preservation and marketing of Siwi dates.

title: DECARBONIZING INDIA’S CONSTRUCTION MATERIALS SYSTEM HISTORICAL CONSUMPTION, INDUSTRIAL EMISSIONS AND AN INTEGRATED PATHWAY TO 2070
summary: India's development since independence has been accompanied by a sustained increase in the use of cement, concrete and steel.These materials have enabled housing, transport, irrigation, energy and industrial development, but they have also
content: India's development since independence has been accompanied by a sustained increase in the use of cement, concrete and steel.These materials have enabled housing, transport, irrigation, energy and industrial development, but they have also embedded a substantial carbon burden within the built environment.Cement is particularly difficult to decarbonize because its emissions arise from both thermal energy and the chemical decomposition of limestone.Steel presents a parallel challenge through coal intensive production routes, while concrete transfers the embodied emissions of cement, reinforcement and other constituents into buildings and infrastructure.This study reconstructs the long term evolution of construction material consumption in India from the early post-independence period to the present.Cement and finished steel consumption per capita were calculated from apparent consumption and corresponding population.Concrete consumption was derived from cement use through a period specific estimate of the share of cement consumed in concrete and The analysis indicates that plant efficiency alone cannot offset sustained material demand growth.A credible transition requires clinker substitution, calcined clay, alternative fuels, cleaner electricity, carbon capture, low carbon steelmaking, structural optimization, precast construction, recycled materials, and improved curing and robust quality management.Construction materials are not the sole determinant of India's national net zero outcome, but their transformation is essential because they represent one of the largest and most persistent industrial emissions domains.

title: Building Global resilience through Sustainable Innovation: A Case study approach
source: International Journal of Computer Information Systems and Industrial Management Applications
summary: The most prominent engineering issues of the twenty-first century are climate change, rapid urbanization, water shortages, and growing energy consumption. The paper argues that a sustainable future necessitates a deliberate integration of e
content: The most prominent engineering issues of the twenty-first century are climate change, rapid urbanization, water shortages, and growing energy consumption. The paper argues that a sustainable future necessitates a deliberate integration of energy innovation, infrastructure development, and climate research into a single engineering framework rather than isolated technical solutions. Global data is collected from the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC), the International Energy Agency (IEA) and the International Renewable Energy Agency (IRENA). The paper first quantifies the scale and urgency of the challenge before examining how climate change threatens existing infrastructure through sea-level rise, extreme heat, flooding, wildfire, storms, and water stress. It then reviews the state of the global energy transition and the emerging discipline of smart, sustainable urban engineering. The core of the paper is a case study analysis spanning five Indian projects alongside five international benchmarks. These cases illustrate recurring engineering principles: systems thinking that couples energy, water and the built environment; the commercial viability of renewable energy at scale; and the outsized leverage of urban and agricultural engineering interventions. The paper concludes with a synthesis of the engineering imperatives required through 2030, including a tripling of renewable capacity, the scaling of green hydrogen, zero-carbon building codes, transport electrification, and nature-based infrastructure.

title: LANTHANUM (LaCl3) ADDITION DIVERSIFIES ORGANIC ACID PRODUCTION AND SIGNIFICANTLY ENHANCES METHANE PRODUCTION IN A METHANOGENIC CONSORTIUM
summary: Trace elements, such as iron, nickel, and cobalt are known to regulate methanogenic activity in anaerobic digestors used for waste valorisation, but the potential role of rare earth elements remains poorly understood. This study investigate
content: Trace elements, such as iron, nickel, and cobalt are known to regulate methanogenic activity in anaerobic digestors used for waste valorisation, but the potential role of rare earth elements remains poorly understood. This study investigated the effects of lanthanum (La) supplementation on biogas production, methane generation, volatile fatty acid (VFA) formation, and carbohydrate utilisation in anaerobic digestion (AD). Biomethane potential (BMP) assays conducted under mesophilic conditions (37C) using methanogenic sludge granules, and glucose as substrate, were supplemented with 0.1, 1, 10, and 100 mg/L lanthanum chloride (LaCl3). Biogas production and composition was monitored over a 96-h incubation, while sacrificial, batch bioreactors were used to evaluate temporal VFA and carbohydrate profiles. La supplementation significantly enhanced biogas and methane production in a concentration-dependent manner. The highest cumulative biogas yield (478.9 mL, corresponding to 179.5 mL biogas/g COD) and methane production (285.7 mL, corresponding to 107.1 mL CH4/g COD) were observed with 100 mg/L LaCl3, corresponding to increases of 88.7% and 186%, respectively, compared with La-free controls. CO2 production also increased with La concentration, whereas hydrogen production remained comparatively low. Acetic and butyric acids represented the dominant fermentation products (80-88% of total VFAs), but profiles of accumulated VFA in the bioreactors diversified with La addition, including showing caproate production, indicating changed biodegradation dynamics in the methanogenic microbiome. These findings demonstrate that lanthanum can stimulate anaerobic digestion performance and methane generation, highlighting the potential as a novel trace element additive to enhance biogas production. Research is now required to elucidate the underlying microbial and biochemical mechanisms, and establish optimal dosing strategies for large-scale applications.

title: Effects of 3-nitrooxypropanol on productivity and carcass traits in feedlot cattle fed a steam-flaked wheat diet in a commercial setting
summary: Context As the livestock sector faces mounting expectations to curb greenhouse gas emissions alongside evolving public attitudes toward feed additives, rigorous evaluation of emission-mitigation additives within commercial feedlot operation
content: Context As the livestock sector faces mounting expectations to curb greenhouse gas emissions alongside evolving public attitudes toward feed additives, rigorous evaluation of emission-mitigation additives within commercial feedlot operations is warranted. Aims The present study evaluated the impact of 3-nitrooxypropanol (3-NOP) supplementation on growth performance and carcass outcomes of feedlot cattle fed a steam-flaked wheat diet in a large-scale commercial setting. Methods In total, 9492 crossbred steers and heifers (bodyweight 362.8 ± 30.4 kg, mean ± s.d. ) were randomly assigned to one of two treatments, namely, control (no 3-NOP) or 3-NOP (100 mg/kg DM dose of 3-NOP). Cattle were transitioned to a finisher ration over 11 days and then fed for 95 days, during which each treatment remained on its respective diet for the 106 day finishing period. All statistical procedures were performed using SAS software, where the pen was considered the experimental unit and block as random. Key results The 3-NOP cattle had significantly lower dry-matter intake than did the control (8.78 vs 8.91 kg/day respectively). Moreover, average daily gain, feed:gain, morbidity, carcass weight, and dressing percentage were unaffected. The 3-NOP cattle had a reduced P8 fat depth and Meat Standards Australia (MSA) marbling score, and tended to have lower Ausmeat marbling scores; however, these differences were practically small, and overall MSA index was not affected. Conclusion The study indicated that 3-NOP can be confidently supplemented to feedlot cattle finished on steam-flaked wheat diets without negatively influencing key feedlot performance and carcass characteristics. Implications Feeding 3-NOP to finishing cattle reduced dry-matter intake, resulting in diminished marbling and fat depth, without negatively influencing cattle performance or health.

title: Do energy savings really save? Uncovering the residential electricity rebound effect in Indonesia
summary: Energy efficiency is widely recognized as one of the most cost-effective strategies for reducing electricity consumption and mitigating greenhouse gas emissions. However, improvements in energy efficiency do not always translate into propor
content: Energy efficiency is widely recognized as one of the most cost-effective strategies for reducing electricity consumption and mitigating greenhouse gas emissions. However, improvements in energy efficiency do not always translate into proportional reductions in electricity use because households may adjust their consumption behavior, giving rise to the residential electricity rebound effect. This study estimates household electricity efficiency and examines the residential electricity rebound effect in Indonesia using provincial panel data covering 33 provinces during 2010–2024. Energy efficiency is measured using Stochastic Frontier Analysis (SFA) within an energy demand frontier framework, while the rebound effect is estimated using a dynamic panel model based on the System Generalized Method of Moments (System GMM). The results show that the average household electricity efficiency is approximately 83%, suggesting substantial room for improving residential electricity efficiency across provinces. The estimated short-run rebound effect is 51%, indicating a partial rebound in which part of the expected electricity savings is offset by increased household electricity consumption. In contrast, the estimated long-run rebound effect is −13%, indicating a super-conservation effect, whereby improvements in electricity efficiency eventually lead to more-than-proportional reductions in residential electricity consumption. These findings suggest that residential electricity efficiency policies remain effective in reducing household electricity demand over the long term, although complementary demand-side and behavioral policies are needed to limit short-run rebound effects and maximize electricity savings.

title: Anisotropic evolution of mechanical and seepage properties in coal under mining-induced stress paths: experiments and modeling for enhanced gas extraction
summary: As mining depth increases, the in-situ stress in coal bodies rises significantly, leading to an increased risk of dynamic disasters such as rock burst, coal and gas outburst. Deeply understanding the influence of stress paths on the anisotr
content: As mining depth increases, the in-situ stress in coal bodies rises significantly, leading to an increased risk of dynamic disasters such as rock burst, coal and gas outburst. Deeply understanding the influence of stress paths on the anisotropic evolution of coal mechanics and seepage characteristics during mining is crucial for improving gas drainage efficiency and disaster prevention. In this study, self‑developed true‑triaxial compression‑seepage test system was adopted, and two groups of typical stress‑path tests were carried out on anthracite specimens, including triaxial proportional loading (Path 1) and simulated excavation unloading (Path 2). Test results show that the peak strength in the perpendicular-to-bedding direction is 3.48%‑6.94% higher than that in the parallel-to-bedding, and the failure mode is transformed from X‑type conjugate shear failure to combined shear‑splitting failure along weak structural planes. Permeability exhibits a four‑stage evolutionary characteristic under both stress paths, whereas the post‑peak permeability amplification in the parallel-to-bedding direction (16.5‑52.3 times) is considerably larger than that in the perpendicular-to-bedding direction (14.7‑22.7 times). Theoretically, an anisotropic damage‑permeability coupling model is established in this work. The relationship between the differential development of fracture networks and the amplification effect of the cubic law for permeability anisotropy is investigated, and the intrinsic mechanism accounting for the above‑mentioned direction‑dependent behaviours is interpreted. From an engineering perspective, it is demonstrated that gas drainage boreholes should be approximately arranged along the bedding direction to connect highly conductive shear‑tensile fracture channels. Meanwhile, targeted support is utilised to maintain confining pressure, by which the outburst risk induced by the sharp permeability increment during unloading can be mitigated. This research provides a theoretical foundation and implementable engineering countermeasures for safe and efficient gas drainage in deep coal mines.

title: Adsorptive recovery of NF 3 and CF 4 using a scalable stacked coordination polymer
summary: Abstract Recovering nitrogen trifluoride (NF 3 ) and carbon tetrafluoride (CF 4 ) from semiconductor‐related streams is a process challenge for electronic‐gas reuse and greenhouse‐gas mitigation. Here, we report the efficient NF 3 /CF 4 sie
content: Abstract Recovering nitrogen trifluoride (NF 3 ) and carbon tetrafluoride (CF 4 ) from semiconductor‐related streams is a process challenge for electronic‐gas reuse and greenhouse‐gas mitigation. Here, we report the efficient NF 3 /CF 4 sieving separation through a flexible one‐dimensional MOF, Mn‐dhbq, that exhibits a temperature‐responsive “gate‐opening” effect. At 298 K and 1 bar, Mn‐dhbq adsorbs 1.24 mmol·g −1 of NF 3 while showing negligible uptake of CF 4 (0.14 mmol·g −1 ), leading to an ideal adsorbed solution theory (IAST) selectivity of 10.6 for an equimolar mixture. Dynamic breakthrough experiments confirm that high‐purity CF 4 (≥ 99.5%) and NF 3 (≥ 99.5%) can be recovered during the adsorption and desorption process, respectively. And the separation performance could maintain for at least 5 cycles without degradation. Moreover, Mn‐dhbq can be synthesized on a hundred‐gram scale in water at room temperature and shaped into pellets with a hydroxyethyl cellulose binder. These combined properties make Mn‐dhbq a promising adsorbent for practical NF 3 /CF 4 separation.

title: Defining climate change acceptance in undergraduate science student populations: A Delphi study
summary: Acceptance of climate change often promotes pro-environmental behavior and encourages greater support of climate change policy and mitigation strategies. Despite its important role, no standardized definition of climate change acceptance ex
content: Acceptance of climate change often promotes pro-environmental behavior and encourages greater support of climate change policy and mitigation strategies. Despite its important role, no standardized definition of climate change acceptance exists in the published literature, leading to significant variability in how it is measured by researchers. Additionally, climate change is included in many educational frameworks as a vital curricular topic for establishing scientific literacy; however, student acceptance is neglected as a key factor. This ambiguity makes it difficult to compare research findings from studies measuring acceptance and further complicates educational efforts aimed at fostering climate literacy. The goal of the present study was to establish a consensus definition of climate change acceptance for undergraduate science student populations using a mixed-methods Delphi methodology. Our process integrated data from three sources: a preliminary framework of 14 constructs derived from a scoping review of 523 articles, a pilot survey of undergraduate students, and four iterative rounds of interviews and surveys with 210 experts and stakeholders in biology, chemistry, and geosciences. After multiple rounds of data collection and revision, expert consensus and stability of responses resulted in two definitions for climate change acceptance: the Anthropogenic Definition , which focuses on climate change occurrence and human causality, and the Anthropogenic + Mechanistic Definition , which also incorporates mechanisms of temperature and greenhouse gases. This bipolarity of opinion amongst participants suggests that the appropriate definition for an undergraduate student may depend on educational context or academic level. These rigorously researched definitions provide needed context for existing research instruments, a clearer target for future instruments, and guidance for post-secondary science educators on what constitutes acceptance at different levels.

title: Reducing methane and nitrous oxide emissions from rainfed paddy fields using corn cob-derived biochar at Central Java, Indonesia
summary: ABSTRACT Rainfed paddy fields constitute approximately one-third of Indonesia’s total rice (Oryza sativa L.) field area, including those distributed in Central Java Province. Rainfed lowlands are susceptible to the effects of climate change
content: ABSTRACT Rainfed paddy fields constitute approximately one-third of Indonesia’s total rice (Oryza sativa L.) field area, including those distributed in Central Java Province. Rainfed lowlands are susceptible to the effects of climate change. Furthermore, there are several challenges in managing rainfed paddy fields, such as low crop productivity, poor soil fertility, and drought stress. Utilizing agricultural waste as biochar is expected to enhance soil quality, increase crop productivity and reduce greenhouse gas emissions responsible for global warming. The research aimed to determine the emissions of methane (CH4) and nitrous oxide (N2O) from rainfed paddy fields by using the corncob (Zea mays L.) biochar as urea coating (BCU), and biochar combined with compost. The research was conducted in rainfed paddy fields using a randomized block design with three treatments and four replicates. Plant growth, grain yield, CH4 flux, and N2O flux were among the parameters measured. The result showed that biochar utilization, both as a urea coating (BCU) and in combination with compost, significantly improved plant growth, increased grain yields of ‘Ciherang’ rice, and reduced more CH4 and N2O emissions in rainfed paddy fields. Grain yield increased by 29.2% with biochar-coated urea (BCU), and 11.9% with the biochar-compost combination. Furthermore, the application of biochar-compost and BCU reduced daily CH4 flux by 93.2% and 97.7%, respectively. Compared to conventional farmer practices, biochar-compost resulted in a greater reduction in N2O flux than BCU. Thus, utilizing agricultural waste biochar in lowland rice cultivation can increase productivity while mitigating climate change impacts.

title: Contributing to Climate Change: A Contractualist Response to the Sceptic
summary: ABSTRACT As a consumer, am I morally obligated to reduce my personal greenhouse gas emissions footprint? As a citizen, do I have an obligation to support political measures that mitigate climate change? These important questions remain cont
content: ABSTRACT As a consumer, am I morally obligated to reduce my personal greenhouse gas emissions footprint? As a citizen, do I have an obligation to support political measures that mitigate climate change? These important questions remain contentious. A central obstacle to affirmative answers lies in two familiar moral scepticisms: that any individual contribution seems too inconsequential to be morally significant and that the harms of climate change seem to occur regardless of one's share. I argue that T. M. Scanlon's moral contractualism should be brought in to enable a response. Contractualism holds that the justifiability of action matters in its own right. On this basis, principles that leave individuals free to ignore climate change could reasonably be rejected by its victims. In advancing this argument, contractualism still faces at least two major challenges: the problem of probability and the so‐called aggregation problem. But there is no reason to think these cannot be overcome. The effort is worthwhile, for contractualism would then counter the scepticisms much more convincingly than either act consequentialism or unguarded moral intuition ever could.

title: India's historical contribution to present-day warming is recent and multi-gas
summary: Abstract Quantifying national contributions to present-day warming helps clarify how historical emissions from different countries have shaped global temperature change. This is particularly relevant for India, where rising energy demand an
content: Abstract Quantifying national contributions to present-day warming helps clarify how historical emissions from different countries have shaped global temperature change. This is particularly relevant for India, where rising energy demand and emissions make the country’s future mitigation pathway increasingly important for global efforts to limit warming. Understanding India’s contribution to warming to date, and how it varies across greenhouse gases and emitting sectors, can therefore provide useful context for its future mitigation priorities. Here, we quantify India’s contribution to the 2024 global mean surface temperature change from historical territorial emissions of CO₂, CH₄ and N₂O over 1750–2024 using PRIMAP-hist emissions and the FaIR climate model. India contributes approximately 0.047–0.05 °C to 2024 warming, less than the United States, China, the EU27 and Russia among the major emitters considered, but more than several other industrial and emerging economies. Much of India’s contribution has accumulated in recent decades, with the strongest increase occurring after 1990. This rise is driven primarily by CO₂ emissions from the energy sector, while agriculture remains the main source of non-CO₂ warming through CH₄ and N₂O. Overall, CH₄ and N₂O account for roughly one-third to two-fifths of India’s total contribution, giving India a more multi-gas profile than many early industrialised emitters. Although India’s cumulative contribution to present-day warming remains comparatively modest, its rapid recent growth highlights the increasing importance of energy system decarbonisation. Reducing fossil fuel dependence in the energy sector will therefore be central to limiting further growth in India’s warming contribution and supporting progress towards its long-term net-zero target for 2070.

title: Enhancing Operational Efficiency in Wastewater Treatment: STOAT Modelling and Optimization of the Kurunegala WWTP
source: Sri Lankan Journal of Applied Sciences
summary: This study evaluates the energy optimization potential of the Kurunegala Wastewater Treatment Plant (WWTP) using STOAT, a freely available wastewater process simulation tool. The plant’s treatment process, based on an anoxic-oxic (AO) confi
content: This study evaluates the energy optimization potential of the Kurunegala Wastewater Treatment Plant (WWTP) using STOAT, a freely available wastewater process simulation tool. The plant’s treatment process, based on an anoxic-oxic (AO) configuration, was modelled and calibrated using measured influent and effluent quality parameters. The validated model accurately predicted key performance indicators such as BOD, TSS, ammonia, and nitrate, confirming STOAT’s reliability. Sensitivity analysis identified influent flow rate and return activated sludge (RAS) ratio as the most critical parameters influencing effluent quality. Simulation-based optimization was conducted to assess the impact of dissolved oxygen (DO) and RAS variations on treatment efficiency and energy consumption. Results demonstrated that reducing DO from 2.0 to 1.0 mg/L and RAS from 0.667 to 0.4 achieved a 46.4% reduction in energy consumption without compromising effluent quality. The study also identified operational thresholds for BOD and NH₄⁺-N in influent to maintain compliance with Sri Lankan discharge standards. These findings highlight the practical value of STOAT in supporting data-driven decision-making for energy-efficient and sustainable wastewater treatment, especially in resource-constrained contexts.

title: Predicting hyperopic reserve in children based on school-based vision programs with ensemble learning
summary: Purpose To develop a predictive model based on school-based vision screening programs for evaluating hyperopic reserve status in children aged 5–10 years. Methods This cross-sectional study included 8,035 students aged 5–10 years from senio
content: Purpose To develop a predictive model based on school-based vision screening programs for evaluating hyperopic reserve status in children aged 5–10 years. Methods This cross-sectional study included 8,035 students aged 5–10 years from senior kindergarten and primary school in Guangdong Province, China. Participants underwent ocular biometric measurements, autorefraction, and questionnaire assessment before cycloplegia, after which autorefraction was repeated. An ensemble learning model was constructed to predict low hyperopic reserve (LHR), a refractive status below age-appropriate norms but not yet myopic, using NCR ocular parameters and questionnaire data. Model performance was evaluated and compared through nested 5-fold cross-validation. Sensitivity and robustness analyses were conducted to verify the comprehensive model performance. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) was utilized to interpret feature contributions and model logic. Results On the test set, the ensemble learning model achieved an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.807, an accuracy of 0.737, and a precision of 0.747, outperforming all the single machine learning models. Compared to the direct NCR-based assessment and the +0.50 D / +0.75 D fixed-offset benchmarks (accuracy = 0.614–0.669, precision = 0.593–0.683), the ensemble learning model improved accuracy by 0.068–0.123 and precision by 0.064–0.154. SHAP analysis identified axial length to corneal radius ratio (SHAP value = 0.652), spherical equivalent (SHAP value = 0.514), and school type (SHAP value = 0.312) as the most three important predictors. Conclusions and Relevance The proposed ensemble learning model offers a noncycloplegic, convenient approach for school-based vision programs to predict LHR in children aged 5–10 years. This model and its risk-assessment tool may support existing school-based vision programs in preserving children's hyperopic reserve.

title: Effect of metal oxide nanoparticles on nutritional quality of chickpea: A focus on protein and mineral content
source: Journal of King Saud University - Science
summary: Chickpea is a nutritious leguminous crop mostly cultivated for its leaves and grains offering a reliable and cost-effective source of protein. Its production and nutritional quality are hindered by soil degradation in many regions worldwide
content: Chickpea is a nutritious leguminous crop mostly cultivated for its leaves and grains offering a reliable and cost-effective source of protein. Its production and nutritional quality are hindered by soil degradation in many regions worldwide. However, studies have shown that the use of nanoparticles for plant fertilization can enhance plant nutritional quality and growth. Thus, this study aimed to evaluate the effects of ZnO, Fe 2 O 3 and CuO nanoparticles on chickpea mineral composition and total protein content. Total protein content was evaluated using a LECO TruMac Carbon (C) and Nitrogen (N) analyser (TRUMAC CN) analyzer. Chickpea seeds and grains’ mineral composition was evaluated through ICP-EOS. Data was subjected to a two-way analysis of variance (ANOVA). The findings revealed that foliar application of 5 ppm of ZnO NPs increased Zn concentrations by 70% for Desi and 30% for Kabuli grains, also increasing the uptake of other minerals such as Ca, Cu, K, and Na, as compared to the control treatment. Both genotypes reacted differently to foliar application of Fe 2 O 3 and CuO nanoparticles, although the favorable effect on nutrient accumulation in both leaves and grains was significant. The protein content of chickpea grains was enhanced by the application of all nanoparticles at lower concentrations.

title: Modulating red: Far-red ratios accelerates speed breeding efficiency by coordinating photosynthesis and flowering in winter wheat (Triticum aestivum L.) under controlled environments
summary: The ratio of red to far-red light (R/FR) is well known to regulate plant photosynthesis and flowering. However, the molecular and physiological mechanisms underlying these coordinated responses in winter wheat remain largely unclear. In a c
content: The ratio of red to far-red light (R/FR) is well known to regulate plant photosynthesis and flowering. However, the molecular and physiological mechanisms underlying these coordinated responses in winter wheat remain largely unclear. In a controlled-environment growth chamber, we investigated flowering behavior, photosynthetic performance, genome-wide transcriptional responses, and breeding efficiency in winter wheat under four R/FR light treatments: 10:1, 2:1, 1:1, and 1:2. Compared with an R/FR ratio of 10:1, an R/FR ratio of 2:1 significantly enhanced breeding efficiency, enabling up to 4.7 generations annually, via enhancing photosynthetic capacity, accelerating floral transition and progeny seed early maturation, albeit causing a decrease in production. Transcriptomic profiling further demonstrated that low R/FR ratios extensively remodel the expression of core genes associated with gibberellin (GA) biosynthesis, photosynthesis, and the flowering regulatory pathway. Far-red light supplementation upregulated key gibberellin biosynthesis genes (e.g., TaGA20 ox1 , TaGA20 ox2 -like ), increasing the accumulation of biologically active gibberellins (GA 3 and GA 4 ). This subsequently upregulated flowering promoters (e.g., TaFT and TaFT-like ) and downregulated flowering inhibitors (e.g., CO-L9 and CO-L10 ), thereby accelerating flowering. Taken together, these findings provide a mechanistic framework showing that far-red light accelerates reproductive development in winter wheat by enhancing GA-mediated signaling pathways, while maintaining higher photosynthetic performance. This regulatory effect highlights the potential of R/FR manipulation to shorten generation cycles and improve breeding efficiency in controlled-environment agriculture systems for winter wheat.

title: Integrated food safety indicator for proactive evaluation of foods - application to plant-based protein foods
summary: Current food safety assessments lack a proactive approach informing decision-makers about the general safety status of foods. Using a semi-quantitative framework, this study developed an integrated food safety indicator to evaluate the over
content: Current food safety assessments lack a proactive approach informing decision-makers about the general safety status of foods. Using a semi-quantitative framework, this study developed an integrated food safety indicator to evaluate the overall safety of a single food a priori, by combining evidence on the presence of chemical contaminants, microbial hazards, and allergenic potential. Each component is computed by specific indicators and sub-indicators. The methodology was applied to a case study where we compared plant-based and animal-based protein foods. Results showed that alternative protein foods have lower food safety implications than traditional ones. Having a single measure of food safety enables a better understanding of the safety status of a food and supports structured comparisons among foods. This provides actionable results to decision-makers to set priorities towards foods. Eventually, this also fosters the integration of food safety considerations into broader decision-making settings.

title: Endophytic fungi: Nature's hidden vault of biomolecules
summary: The alarming rise of antibiotic-resistant bacteria has emerged as a major global health concern, intensifying the urgent need for novel bioactive compounds from natural sources. In recent years, scientific interest in endophytic fungi, whic
tags: Plant use of endophytic fungi in defense
content: The alarming rise of antibiotic-resistant bacteria has emerged as a major global health concern, intensifying the urgent need for novel bioactive compounds from natural sources. In recent years, scientific interest in endophytic fungi, which reside asymptomatically within plant tissues, has grown substantially. These microorganisms have demonstrated the capacity to produce a diverse range of bioactive secondary metabolites, exhibiting anticancer, antimicrobial, antiviral and anti-inflammatory properties. The metabolites exhibit antibacterial activity by disrupting membranes and interfering with essential cellular processes like protein and nucleic acid synthesis. Such compounds hold immense promise for both drug discovery and the development of agricultural biocontrol agents. The role of fungal endophytes in pharmaceutical innovation is becoming increasingly apparent. The unique microenvironment within plant hosts, coupled with the genetic diversity of endophytic fungi, fosters the biosynthesis of structurally novel and biologically potent molecules. However, harnessing this potential is not without challenges. Difficulties in isolating, culturing and characterising endophytic fungi and their metabolites continue to impede progress. Artificial intelligence, omics technologies, and metabolic engineering could be integrated into future research to improve the sustainable production and therapeutic utilisation of endophytic fungal metabolites. This review highlights recent advances in the discovery and characterisation of novel compounds from endophytic fungi, while also addressing ongoing challenges in understanding endophyte biology and optimising metabolite production.

title: Sustainable Raw Material Manufacturing Processes
summary: The growth of the fashion industry, rising global clothing demand, and the shortened lifespan of textile products have increased textile waste, much of which ends up in landfills and waterways, contributing to environmental pollution. These
content: The growth of the fashion industry, rising global clothing demand, and the shortened lifespan of textile products have increased textile waste, much of which ends up in landfills and waterways, contributing to environmental pollution. These constitute significant social and environmental challenges. On the other hand, the various stages of textile and garment manufacturing consume large quantities of water, release hazardous chemicals into rivers, and emit greenhouse gases, all of which have detrimental effects on the environment and contribute to climate change. The environmental impact of end-of-life garments can be mitigated by reclaiming textile waste and transforming it into value-added products suitable for applications in the automotive, furnishing, and insulation sectors. However, a continuous and thorough investigation on some of the reclaiming processes needs to be monitored as they may release higher amount of CO 2 during the manufacturing process. The volume of water needed in garment manufacturing can be minimized using water management policies and salinized land, and it is possible with the participation of government (local, regional, national), private sector and communities. Biofriendly chemicals that are inexpensive and cleaner must be used instead of traditional toxic ones. They must be degraded without harming the environment and be recycled into novel products.

title: Pursuing a hierarchical taxonomy in a water-cooled data center room
summary: Despite the growing number of scientific investigations on developing taxonomies in various industries and categorizing energy end-use (EEU) processes, research on such frameworks in the data center (DC) sector remains limited, restricting
content: Despite the growing number of scientific investigations on developing taxonomies in various industries and categorizing energy end-use (EEU) processes, research on such frameworks in the data center (DC) sector remains limited, restricting systematic analysis of energy use, benchmarking, and identification of energy efficiency measures. This study seeks to achieve two key objectives: (1) to create a hierarchical taxonomy for categorizing EEU process, (2) and to identify the most relevant energy performance indicators (EnPIs). The methodology combines hierarchical classification of energy flows with quantitative analysis based on time-resolved operational data, allowing for detailed analysis of dynamic system behaviour and allocation of energy use across processes, applied to a DC room with a detached in-rack water cooling system in Sweden operated by Ericsson. The results of this paper present a novel hierarchical taxonomy for a water-cooled DC room with six defined EEU processes, of which four are related to data processing processes and two to support processes. Notably, over 99.9% of total EEU is connected to data processing processes which is a significantly higher figure compared to other production processes in other sectors. Moreover, the established EnPIs can facilitate benchmarking between DCs with similar infrastructures and for monitoring the energy use of various EEU processes. The proposed methodology is transferable to other DC environments with comparable system boundaries and data availability, and its reproducibility is supported by the structured and data-driven methodology, which enables replication of the analytical approach given comparable data availability.

title: Assessing the 2028–2034 CAP Reform: A Budget- and Payment-Driven Scenario Analysis Using the GLOBIOM Partial Equilibrium Model
summary: The European Commission's July 2025 Multiannual Financial Framework proposal introduces structural changes to the Common Agricultural Policy (CAP) for the 2028-2034 programming period, raising questions about its alignment with the environm
content: The European Commission's July 2025 Multiannual Financial Framework proposal introduces structural changes to the Common Agricultural Policy (CAP) for the 2028-2034 programming period, raising questions about its alignment with the environmental ambitions of the Green Deal.This paper uses the spatially explicit partial equilibrium model GLOBIOM to assess how the proposed policy shifts alter production incentives and land allocation across EU Member States.We operationalise the reform by linking regional budget envelopes with unit payment rates for the key interventions, including the degressive area-based income support corridor, the consolidated Agri-Environmental and Climate Action (AECA) framework, and expanded coupled income support.Testing Member State implementation strategies ranging from fiscal minimisation to high environmental ambition, we quantify impacts on agricultural production, prices, trade, and greenhouse gas emissions, explicitly capturing the quantity-rationing effects of binding budget constraints.Results show that the aggregate 15% budget cut translates into heterogeneous impacts across instruments and Member States, that payment rate equalisation is the reform's primary redistributive mechanism, and that without practice conditionality the environmental gains of even ambitious green implementation remain limited.

title: Removing Harmful Gases from Litter Used in a Broiler House by UV Lights
source: Yüzüncü Yıl Üniversitesi Tarım Bilimleri Dergisi
summary: Over the years, the growth in chicken production has brought with it certain problems. Pollutants from poultry farms cause environmental and health problems. Various measures must be taken to properly manage these issues and mitigate their
content: Over the years, the growth in chicken production has brought with it certain problems. Pollutants from poultry farms cause environmental and health problems. Various measures must be taken to properly manage these issues and mitigate their effects. Proper ventilation and litter management within the broiler house are the primary measures. Additionally, the treatment of pollutants in litter using UV rays is an alternative method. In this study, NH3 and CO2 gases originating from litter material obtained from a broiler farm operating in the Bursa region were treated using UV rays on a laboratory scale. Litter samples were exposed to UV-A and UV-C rays at different exposure times and distances, and their treatment efficiencies were determined. The data obtained as a result of the study show that UV rays are effective in reducing livestock-derived pollutant gases. When the treatment efficiencies of the parameters are evaluated independently, the highest CO2 treatment efficiencies in terms of exposure time were observed at the 120th minute (93.56% for UVA and 100% for UVC). For NH3 gas, the highest efficiencies over time were recorded at the 60th minute (90.50% for UV-A) and at the 90th minute (95.33% for UV-C). When the application distances were examined individually, it was determined that the highest purification performance for both gases and lamp types (UVA and UVC) was achieved at 40 cm. In this context, it has been determined that the UV-C lamp shows the highest treatment efficiency for CO2 gas, and the UV-A lamp for NH3 gas, at a distance of 40 cm for both gases.

title: Climate change, pharmaceuticals and prescribing patterns: a scoping review and proposal for the MAMS model for healthcare educators
summary: Background Healthcare contributes substantially to climate change, and pharmaceuticals account for a meaningful share of this footprint across manufacturing, distribution, prescribing, and disposal. However, climate-health education and pre
content: Background Healthcare contributes substantially to climate change, and pharmaceuticals account for a meaningful share of this footprint across manufacturing, distribution, prescribing, and disposal. However, climate-health education and prescribing practices are often addressed separately, leaving limited guidance for integrating climate change, pharmaceuticals, and prescribing patterns within a single framework. This scoping review synthesizes evidence on the intersection of these domains, with attention to how these concepts are incorporated into health professions education (HPE) and clinical practice. Methods A comprehensive literature search strategy of six databases (PubMed, Embase, CINAHL, ERIC, Health Source: Nursing Academic, and Web of Science) identified peer-reviewed studies published between January 1988 and December 2025 in English or Spanish. Eligible studies addressed climate change in relation to pharmaceutical use or prescribing patterns and included an educational or practice-based component; animal studies, studies without interventions, and non-prescribing studies were excluded. Searches were conducted in December 2023 and updated in April 2025. Data were extracted on study characteristics, clinical domain, educational approach, and directional relationships mapped to the MAMS model dyads (Climate ↔ pharmaceuticals; pharmaceuticals ↔ prescribing patterns; climate ↔ prescribing patterns). Results From 4,247 citations, 28 studies met inclusion criteria. Studies were conducted across multiple regions, most commonly the United States ( n = 6), United Kingdom ( n = 5), Australia ( n = 5), and Canada ( n = 4), with additional single country and multinational collaborations. Clinical domains varied, with the largest representation in anesthesia and perioperative care ( n = 8), followed by pharmacy and pharmacology ( n = 5), primary care ( n = 3), and fewer in other specialties. Studies used single and multi-educational domains, most commonly framework development ( n = 16), followed by curricular integration ( n = 6). Outcomes included reductions in anesthetic or inhaler related emissions, behavior change, knowledge or awareness, attitudes or satisfaction, and identification of barriers and facilitators. Although individual MAMS dyads were frequently examined, no study operationalized all three domains in an integrated bidirectional tri-dyadic manner. Conclusion Existing literature on climate-conscious prescribing education is expanding but remains clinically concentrated and largely conceptual, with limited evaluation of instructional strategies. No study operationalized a fully bidirectional, tri-dyadic approach linking climate change, pharmaceuticals, and prescribing patterns, underscoring the need for integrated, outcomes-oriented frameworks to guide HPE and practice change.

title: Controlled weakening of model ice: Replicating the mechanical response of summer-warmed sea ice in laboratories and test basins
summary: This study examines how the mechanical properties of model ice can be tuned to approximate the weakening of natural sea ice as it warms during summer. The work is motivated by satellite-derived observations and projections indicating that w
content: This study examines how the mechanical properties of model ice can be tuned to approximate the weakening of natural sea ice as it warms during summer. The work is motivated by satellite-derived observations and projections indicating that warm-ice conditions in the Arctic are increasing. The observed warming trend, coupled with the seasonal timing of Arctic shipping activities, challenges the traditional focus on winter conditions in model tests and suggests that incorporating weaker ice is increasingly relevant to ship–ice interaction and ship design. Laboratory tests for ship-performance optimization are often a crucial intermediate step toward implementation in the final maritime application. To provide a broader range of test conditions, we explore methods to adjust two key parameters – the elastic modulus and flexural strength – in model ice under laboratory conditions. The overarching goal is to establish a testing regime capable of representing selected summertime sea-ice properties. Experiments conducted at the Hamburg Ship Model Basin demonstrate that surface treatment of columnar model ice with saturated sodium chloride solution effectively reduces its flexural strength by 71 %. Furthermore, we investigate how variations in the amount of applied solution influence mechanical properties, highlighting differing sensitivities of elastic modulus and flexural strength to modifications of the ice surface layer.

title: Profit efficiency of smallholder dairy production systems: Empirical evidence from Northern Uganda
summary: This study examined the profit efficiency of smallholder dairy farmers operating under different dairy production systems in Gulu District and Gulu City. Specifically, the study assessed the determinants of profit efficiency among farmers p
content: This study examined the profit efficiency of smallholder dairy farmers operating under different dairy production systems in Gulu District and Gulu City. Specifically, the study assessed the determinants of profit efficiency among farmers practicing zero-grazing, tethering, and herding dairy production systems. A cross-sectional survey design was employed using quantitative primary data collected from 191 smallholder dairy households selected through a multistage sampling technique. The stochastic profit frontier model based on the Cobb-Douglas functional specification was used to estimate profit efficiency and identify factors influencing inefficiency across the dairy production systems. The findings revealed considerable variation in profit efficiency determinants across the three dairy production systems. For the overall dairy production system, equipment costs positively influenced profit efficiency (β = 0.069, p < 0.05), while feed costs negatively affected profitability (β = -0.145, p < 0.01). Under the zero-grazing system, herd size significantly improved profit efficiency (β = 0.700, p < 0.01), whereas feed costs reduced profitability (β = -0.553, p < 0.01). Within the tethering system, land size (β = 0.343, p < 0.05) and feed costs (β = 0.235, p < 0.01) positively influenced profit efficiency. In contrast, under the herding system, land size negatively affected profit efficiency (β = -0.482, p < 0.01), while equipment costs positively influenced profitability (β = 0.313, p < 0.05). The inefficiency model showed that education level, improved breed types, and market proximity significantly reduced inefficiency across the overall dairy production systems. The estimated gamma value (γ = 0.93454, p < 0.001) indicated that about 93.45% of the variation in dairy profit performance was attributed to inefficiency effects. The overall mean profit efficiency score was 0.6121, implying that farmers could improve profit efficiency by 26.14% if they operated at the level of the most efficient farmers. Among the production systems, the zero-grazing system recorded the highest mean profit efficiency score (0.9886), followed by the herding system (0.5163), while the tethering system had the lowest efficiency score (0.3572). The study concludes that improving feed management, strengthening extension services, promoting farmer education, and increasing investment in productive dairy assets are essential for improving profit efficiency among smallholder dairy farmers.

title: Mixed-integer production planning with two-echelon stockpile scheduling and contaminant-constrained feed control
summary: Long-term open-pit production scheduling in sulfide-bearing gold deposits requires the integrated coordination of extraction sequencing, material routing, and plant-feed quality control within a single-objective framework aimed at maximizin
content: Long-term open-pit production scheduling in sulfide-bearing gold deposits requires the integrated coordination of extraction sequencing, material routing, and plant-feed quality control within a single-objective framework aimed at maximizing discounted net present value (NPV). These decision variables and operational constraints create multidimensional trade-offs as ore grades decline over the mine’s life. Existing MILP formulations address this inadequately: stockpiles are either represented as attribute-free sinks or the financial penalty of capital tied up in intermediate storage is omitted entirely. The main contribution of this study is a long-term MILP formulation for sulfide-bearing open-pit gold mine scheduling that integrates a physically separated two-echelon stockpile network, explicit contained Au/S inventory conservation, bounded contained-flow grade-control constraints, and echelon-specific lag-cost penalization. The formulation enables plant-feed sulfur feasibility to be enforced over a multi-decade horizon while quantifying the economic cost of delayed processing and stockpile inventory accumulation. Applied to the Zarshuran gold mine, Iran, a 58-year instance with 92,104 decision variables, CPLEX achieved a 3.13% MIP gap in 9.4 hours. The grade-controlled model yields USD 750.148 million NPV, preserving 91.61% of the grade-relaxed benchmark. Independent recursive validation, assuming perfect-mixing, yields a maximum physical upper-envelope sulfur grade of 2.9528%, which corresponds to a minimum safety margin of 0.0472 percentage points below the plant limit of 3.0%. Per-stockpile sensitivity experiments characterize the operational responses observed across the tested lag-cost ranges for the two stockpile echelons; however, overlapping computational optimality intervals prevent interpreting the small differences in incumbent NPV as evidence of economically optimal lag-cost settings.

title: Dissolved oxygen thresholds drive adaptive functional trait remodeling in mesophytes via anatomical, physiological, and metabolic synergies
summary: Climate-exacerbated urban waterlogging imposes severe hypoxic stress on mesophytes. However, whether mesophytes possess dissolved oxygen (DO)-driven mechanisms for adaptive structural and physiological remodeling remains poorly understood.
content: Climate-exacerbated urban waterlogging imposes severe hypoxic stress on mesophytes. However, whether mesophytes possess dissolved oxygen (DO)-driven mechanisms for adaptive structural and physiological remodeling remains poorly understood. We conducted a hydroponic experiment with four representative mesophyte species ( Gardenia jasminoides , Murraya paniculata , Ixora chinensis , and Heptapleurum actinophyllum 'Variegata' ) across four DO gradients (0–2, 2–4, 4–6, and 6–8 mg/L). Plant growth, physiology, and root anatomy were measured, and structural equation modeling (SEM) was applied to disentangle the synergistic pathways underlying waterlogging tolerance. We identified a critical DO threshold: concentrations below 2 mg/L triggered irreversible root degeneration and substantial mortality (50% in I. chinensis), whereas 4–8 mg/L represented the optimal range for maintaining normal growth and 100% survival. Mechanistically, moderate-to-high DO (4–8 mg/L) induced a coordinated shift in functional traits. SEM revealed that DO directly promoted aerenchyma formation (β = 0.77), enhanced internal oxygen transport to mitigate ROS accumulation and significantly reduced membrane lipid peroxidation (MDA, β = –0.39). Concurrently, DO activated the antioxidant enzyme system (β = 0.73) and proline osmoregulation (β = 0.40) to scavenge residual ROS, while increased chlorophyll a content drove plant height (β = 0.90) and biomass accumulation. The four species exhibited distinct adaptive strategies: I. chinensis (structural adaptation), G. jasminoides (physiological compensation), M. paniculata (root reinforcement and osmoregulation), and H. actinophyllum 'Variegata' (synergistic aboveground–belowground growth). This study advances mechanistic understanding of mesophytic stress tolerance under oxygen fluctuations and identifies DO-driven structural–physiological pathways as a reference for plant waterlogging adaptation research.

title: How forest ecosystems regulate soil microbial diversity and function in the northeastern Tibetan Plateau?
summary: Climate shifts exert pronounced influence on the northeastern Tibetan Plateau, where forest ecosystems play a pivotal role in sustaining ecological equilibrium at both local and global scales. However, knowledge of how soil microbial commun
content: Climate shifts exert pronounced influence on the northeastern Tibetan Plateau, where forest ecosystems play a pivotal role in sustaining ecological equilibrium at both local and global scales.
