However, knowledge of how soil microbial communities are structured and function across the varied forest types in this region is still notably incomplete. This study investigated five contrasting forest types across the northeastern Tibetan Plateau to characterize the community structure, functional divergence, and environmental drivers shaping keystone bacterial and fungal lineages in the soil. The key findings are summarized below. (1) Soil physical properties significantly constrained the bacterial species diversity index, whereas they exerted no discernible effect on the fungal species diversity index. (2) Soil nutrient availability markedly enhanced the bacterial species diversity index and functional diversity index, yet exhibited minimal impact on those of fungi. (3) Conversely, soil enzyme activities suppressed the bacterial species diversity index and functional diversity index, but significantly promoted the functional diversity index of soil fungi. (4) Specific driver analysis revealed that soil water content (SWC), ammonium nitrogen ( NH 4 + -N), available phosphorus (AP), and soil urease (S-UE) interactively regulated the bacterial species diversity and functional diversity indices, whereas S-UE emerged as the singular key driver governing the fungal functional diversity index. This study advances our mechanistic understanding of how environmental factors drive the distinct diversity patterns and functional capacities of soil microbiota in high-altitude forest ecosystems.

title: The Road Freight Transport and Its Influence on Urban Mobility and on the Sustainability of Cities
summary: Urban road freight transport is an essential component of cities, ensuring the supply of goods to support economic activities and urban life. However, increasing interaction between freight and passenger transport has intensified traffic co
content: Urban road freight transport is an essential component of cities, ensuring the supply of goods to support economic activities and urban life. However, increasing interaction between freight and passenger transport has intensified traffic congestion, environmental degradation, operational inefficiencies, and pressure on urban infrastructure. Despite its strategic importance, urban freight transport has traditionally received limited attention in urban mobility policies and planning frameworks, particularly in developing countries. This chapter examines the influence of road freight transport on urban mobility and sustainability through the conceptual perspective of urban logistics. A structured methodological framework, integrating theoretical analysis and evidence-based assessment, is adopted to investigate challenges associated with urban freight distribution and their implications for sustainable and resilient urban transport systems. The analysis examines the relationship between urban freight transport, sustainable urban mobility, human mobility, and smart cities, highlighting the contribution of artificial intelligence, intelligent transport systems, and digital technologies to integrated urban transport planning. The contribution of this chapter is the development of urban logistics guidelines designed to improve the efficiency of urban goods distribution while strengthening sustainable urban mobility and integrated urban planning. The proposed guidelines promote coordination between public authorities and private stakeholders, encourage the incorporation of freight transport into municipal planning policies, and provide a framework for reducing congestion, improving logistics performance, mitigating environmental impacts, and enhancing urban quality of life. The chapter concludes that urban logistics should be recognised as a strategic component of sustainable urban development, supporting resilient transport systems and human mobility in future smart cities.

title: KARAYOLU ARAÇLARININ PERFORMANSINI ARTIRMAK VE EMİSYONLARINI AZALTMAK İÇİN AERODİNAMİK AKIŞ KONTROLÜ
summary: The aerodynamic drag of heavy road vehicles is a major contributor to transportation-related greenhouse gas emissions, since overcoming aerodynamic resistance requires additional energy expenditure, leading to increased fossil fuel consumpt
content: The aerodynamic drag of heavy road vehicles is a major contributor to transportation-related greenhouse gas emissions, since overcoming aerodynamic resistance requires additional energy expenditure, leading to increased fossil fuel consumption and associated carbon emissions. To address this challenge, the flow fields around a two-dimensional D-shaped cylinder, representing a generic bluff body, and a three-dimensional square-back Ahmed body, representing a simplified road vehicle geometry, were numerically investigated using passive flow control strategies involving rigid and flexible filaments/flaps. These approaches aim to mitigate flow separation and reduce aerodynamic drag, thereby contributing to lower fuel consumption and reduced greenhouse gas emissions. Prior to the implementation of the control methods, the baseline flow characteristics of both configurations were validated against available experimental data to ensure the accuracy and reliability of the numerical approach. In the first phase of the study, aimed at developing an understanding of passive flow-control mechanisms in a simplified two-dimensional bluff-body configuration, the flow around a D-shaped cylinder equipped with rigid and flexible filaments was investigated. The results showed that rigid filaments provided slightly greater drag reduction than flexible ones, although both configurations achieved substantial reductions, up to 35%. For the flexible filaments, a flow-synchronized lock-in phenomenon was observed between the filament oscillation frequency and the wake shedding frequency. Furthermore, increasing filament rigidity was found to improve flow-control effectiveness, as stiffer filaments remained more stable under flow-induced fluctuations and maintained a more favorable interaction with the wake dynamics. In the second phase of the study, the insights gained from the two-dimensional investigations were extended to a three-dimensional square-back Ahmed body representative of a road vehicle. Two different rigid flap configurations were examined, and it was found that flaps mounted along the side edges of the vehicle base provided substantially greater aerodynamic benefits than those positioned on the upper and lower edges. Through a systematic parametric investigation, the optimum configuration was identified as an inward-deflected flap with an angle of 30°, which achieved a drag reduction of approximately 26% relative to the baseline case. The results further demonstrated the potential of passive flow control to enhance vehicle aerodynamic efficiency, leading to reduced fuel consumption and lower greenhouse gas emissions.

title: Growth heterogeneity of Streptococcus suis in host-mimicking conditions is independent of clinical origin
summary: Abstract Background Streptococcus suis is an important swine and zoonotic pathogen whose virulence relies on complex, niche-specific metabolic adaptation within the host. However, the role of non-virulent S. suis strains in the host remains
content: Abstract Background Streptococcus suis is an important swine and zoonotic pathogen whose virulence relies on complex, niche-specific metabolic adaptation within the host. However, the role of non-virulent S. suis strains in the host remains poorly understood. In this study, using host-mimicking media and biological fluids, we compared the growth of S. suis strains from different anatomical origins, including clinical isolates from diseased piglets and upper respiratory tract and vaginal isolates from healthy animals. Results Strains were evaluated in Todd-Hewitt Broth supplemented with yeast extract (THY), Human Plasma-Like Medium (HPLM), Synthetic Nasal Medium (SNM), and SNM supplemented with mucin (SNM + M). Most isolates exhibited robust growth in THY, whereas proliferation was reduced in HPLM and SNM. Notably, five isolates (two systemic, one nasal and two vaginal) displayed comparatively enhanced growth in SNM compared to the rest of the strains, although this phenotype was not associated with the anatomical origin of the strains. Mucin supplementation consistently increased growth across all tested isolates, suggesting that mucin availability may support S. suis proliferation under nutrient-limiting conditions. Experiments using biological fluids revealed that while all strains grew consistently in saliva, vaginal isolates showed comparatively reduced growth in vaginal fluid, indicating limited adaptation to this environment. No evidence of growth inhibition of virulent strains was observed during co-cultivation, while interactions were predominantly positive and influenced by nutrient availability. Conclusion In summary, S. suis displays strain-specific variability in growth under different in vivo-like conditions independently of clinical origin. These findings suggest a role of metabolic adaptation in shaping bacterial fitness and highlight the importance of using host‑mimicking environments to uncover phenotypic differences and interactions masked under standard laboratory conditions.

title: Chronic disease vulnerability in Ukraine during armed conflict
summary: Abstract Armed conflicts, like the Russian invasion in Ukraine, devastated healthcare systems and amplified chronic disease burdens. This study aimed to unveil novel links between environmental and social factors and chronic illnesses durin
content: Abstract Armed conflicts, like the Russian invasion in Ukraine, devastated healthcare systems and amplified chronic disease burdens. This study aimed to unveil novel links between environmental and social factors and chronic illnesses during crises.This study uniquely combined individual-level data on chronic diseases, living conditions, and winter preparedness in Ukraine during crisis conditions. A multivariable logistic regression model, using age- and gender-adjusted analyses, revealed striking associations, while machine learning models employed rigorous feature selection and data balancing. Six algorithms predicted disease outcomes using validated metrics, ensuring robust and interpretable insights.Surveying 1,552 Ukrainians revealed high chronic disease rates, with hypertension (31.7%) and arthritis (13.9%) prominently linked to environmental and socioeconomic stressors. Poor air quality, crowding, and financial strain emerged as critical drivers. Machine learning pinpointed the top 10 key predictors, showcasing exceptional predictive accuracy. These novel findings underscore the profound health impacts of resource limitations and living conditions during crises.This study reveals unexpected links between environment, socioeconomic status, and healthcare access in chronic disease risks during crises. These insights demand urgently tailored interventions.

title: CRISPR-based point-of-care diagnostics for viral hepatitis: from molecular design to clinical implementation
summary: Timely etiological diagnosis of viral hepatitis is essential for surveillance, treatment initiation, linkage to care, and elimination efforts. In resource-limited settings, however, diagnostic pathways are frequently disrupted by centralize
content: Timely etiological diagnosis of viral hepatitis is essential for surveillance, treatment initiation, linkage to care, and elimination efforts. In resource-limited settings, however, diagnostic pathways are frequently disrupted by centralized nucleic acid testing, specimen-transport requirements, delayed reporting, and loss to follow-up. CRISPR-Cas-based point-of-care testing may help shorten these pathways, but its clinical value cannot be judged by analytical sensitivity alone. This review evaluates CRISPR-Cas strategies for detecting hepatitis A, B, C, D, and E viruses by linking molecular design to virus-specific clinical and public-health decisions. We compare target selection, Cas effectors, amplification strategies, readout formats, specimen processing, genotype coverage, clinical validation, and implementation feasibility. For each virus, the evidence is evaluated in relation to the principal diagnostic need, the potential contribution of CRISPR-Cas, the maturity of the available evidence, and the remaining requirements for deployment. Current evidence is most advanced for HBV and HCV, whereas HAV, HDV, and HEV applications remain less developed or more context dependent. Future platforms should prioritize clinically meaningful detection thresholds, closed-tube sample-to-answer workflows, internal controls, genotype-diverse validation, reagent stability, non-expert usability, and transparent pathway-level cost evaluation.

title: Metal Halide Perovskite‐Based Field‐Effect Transistors
summary: Perovskites have attracted significant attention in recent years owing to their outstanding optoelectronic properties, solution processability, and tunable band structures, which together have enabled strong progress in photovoltaics, light
content: Perovskites have attracted significant attention in recent years owing to their outstanding optoelectronic properties, solution processability, and tunable band structures, which together have enabled strong progress in photovoltaics, light-emitting devices, and photodetectors. Among these applications, perovskite field-effect transistors (PeFETs) have emerged as a key platform for probing charge transport and interfacial phenomena in perovskite materials, and have become a central focus of perovskite electronics research. This review summarizes recent advances in PeFETs, providing a systematic overview of material systems, device architectures, morphology control, interface engineering, and performance optimization. It also discusses the major challenges that currently limit PeFET development, including poor material stability, electrical instability arising from ion migration and trap states, and insufficient uniformity in large-area fabrication. Looking ahead, low-dimensional perovskite structures, A-site cation and organic ligand engineering, and multifunctional interface design are expected to play pivotal roles in enabling high-performance, stable, and environmentally sustainable PeFETs for practical applications.

title: Fatigue behavior of additively manufactured and conventionally manufactured 316L stainless steel under periodic overloading
source: Journal of Materials Research and Technology
summary: ABSTRACT This study explores the influence of periodic overloads on the low-cycle fatigue (LCF) behavior and microstructural evolution of 316L stainless steel fabricated by additive manufacturing (AM) and conventional manufacturing (CM). Tw
content: ABSTRACT This study explores the influence of periodic overloads on the low-cycle fatigue (LCF) behavior and microstructural evolution of 316L stainless steel fabricated by additive manufacturing (AM) and conventional manufacturing (CM). Two critical parameters—the number of consecutive overload cycles and the interval between overloads—were examined for their effects on fatigue life. The findings demonstrate that periodic overloads markedly reshape the LCF response of AM/CM-316L stainless steels, revealing pronounced differences in cyclic stress evolution and microstructural adaptability. Under conditions of low overload severity, AM-316L exhibits enhanced fatigue resistance; however, its fatigue life deteriorates sharply with increasing numbers of consecutive overload cycles. By contrast, CM-316L consistently undergoes sustained cyclic hardening across all overload scenarios. Microstructural analyses further show that variations in fatigue life are most strongly controlled by the evolution of geometrically necessary dislocation (GND) density and low-angle grain boundary (LAGB) content, both of which increase with overload severity, while exhibiting negligible dependence on grain size or texture. A striking distinction emerges in that mechanical twinning occurs extensively in AM-316L but is absent in CM specimens. This observation indicates that the microstructure and localized strain fields of AM-316L favor the activation of twinning, thereby modifying plasticity partitioning, cyclic hardening/softening behavior, and crack initiation pathways. Such mechanisms provide a fundamental explanation for the divergent fatigue responses of AM/CM-316L.

title: Enhancing Food Quality Through Radio Frequency Drying of In‐Shell Oil Crops: A Critical Review of Mechanisms, Advantages, and Challenges
source: Comprehensive Reviews in Food Science and Food Safety
summary: The postharvest drying of in-shell oil crops is severely constrained by their shell-kernel structure, which creates stubborn heat and mass transfer resistance, leading to prolonged processing times, high energy consumption, and rapid qualit
content: The postharvest drying of in-shell oil crops is severely constrained by their shell-kernel structure, which creates stubborn heat and mass transfer resistance, leading to prolonged processing times, high energy consumption, and rapid quality deterioration, including lipid oxidation and color loss. Radio frequency (RF) drying offers an inside-out volumetric heating strategy that bypasses shell resistance and directly heats the kernel, thus reducing drying time and preventing quality deterioration. This review aimed to systematically clarify the mechanism of RF selective heating induced by dielectric differences of the shell-kernel system, which is associated with the vapor pump effect (the phenomenon of internal pressure increase caused by the accumulation of water vapor in the shell) and enhanced moisture migration driven by internal pressure. The shell not only acted as a dual barrier of dielectric and physical properties but also led to enzyme inactivation under RF treatment. Beyond drying, RF treatment improved oil extractability and promoted the formation of desirable volatile compounds (e.g., pyrazines, aldehydes, and furans). However, previous studies focused on extremely few crop species, lacked dynamic dielectric data under realistic drying conditions, left subcellular mechanisms largely unexplored, and failed to monitor the real‑time microenvironment inside the shell. These limitations contributed to persistent industrial challenges, including nonuniform heating, thermal runaway, mechanical damage, and poor process control. Future studies should focus on multiphysics modeling, intelligent synergistic drying technologies (RF-vacuum and RF-hot air), smart sensing and adaptive control systems, and integrated processing approaches combining drying, disinfection, and mycotoxin degradation. Based on the theories of selective heating induced by shell-kernel dielectric differences and internal pressure‑driven moisture migration resulting from the steam pump effect, this review provides technical support for the process design and industrial scale‑up of RF drying for in‑shell oil crops.

title: Mechanistic Basis of Nanobubble Functionality in Food Systems: Linking Electrokinetic Stabilization, Transport Dynamics, and Functional Outcomes
source: Comprehensive Reviews in Food Science and Food Safety
summary: Recently, there has been a surge in shifting of scientific interest towards the adoption of nonthermal technologies in food processing applications. Nanobubble (NB) technology is one of the emerging green technologies that has gained increa
content: Recently, there has been a surge in shifting of scientific interest towards the adoption of nonthermal technologies in food processing applications. Nanobubble (NB) technology is one of the emerging green technologies that has gained increased attention over recent years. However, its functionality is often discussed separately from the gas identity, electrokinetic stabilization, transport behavior, and food matrix interactions. This review develops a framework based on mechanism-property-transport-function-outcome to explain how NB stability, interfacial charge, residence time, sustained transport, and matrix interactions govern food functionality and applications. This framework explains why similar NBs perform differently across food systems, emphasizing and classifying dominant mechanisms of NB action for food applications, along with gas properties as an underlying factor. This review bases electrokinetic and transport phenomena as mechanistic foundations of the stability and applicability of NBs in food systems, while highlighting gas-specific, property-tuned, and food-matrix-directed framework for selecting NBs for potential food applications. The outcome of electrokinetic and transport-based interactions with the food matrices has been discussed under residence time-governed transport, micro-convection effects, food matrix modulation, redox reactions, and bioactive delivery.

title: Effects of Green Electrolyte Characteristics on Environmental Response and Performance of Electrochemical Reinforcement Systems
summary: Objective: The study investigates how the physicochemical characteristics of biodegradable polymer-based green electrolytes influence electrochemical reinforcement efficiency, environmental responsiveness, and substrate stabilization. The g
content: Objective: The study investigates how the physicochemical characteristics of biodegradable polymer-based green electrolytes influence electrochemical reinforcement efficiency, environmental responsiveness, and substrate stabilization. The goal is to establish correlations between electrolyte properties and system performance across soil, concrete, and metallic substrates. Methods: Green electrolytes were synthesized using pectin, chitosan, and kappa-carrageenan matrices combined with ionic salts and plasticizers. Electrochemical reinforcement experiments were conducted in laboratory-scale cells under controlled temperature, humidity, and chemical exposure. Substrates were characterized before and after treatment, and electrochemical behavior was monitored via cyclic voltammetry, electrochemical impedance spectroscopy, chronoamperometry, and potential/current mapping. Ionic conductivity, viscosity, pH stability, and biodegradability of electrolytes were systematically measured. Results: High-conductivity electrolytes, such as Pectin-PVA with 30% glycerol, achieved uniform reinforcement fronts with peak current densities of 2.1 mA/cm2 and consistent potential distribution across substrates. Compressive strength of concrete samples increased by 25%, while soil bulk density improved by 18%. Corrosion current in metallic substrates decreased from 15 µA/cm2 to 5 µA/cm2. Environmental simulations showed stable performance under 10–50◦C temperature range and 30–95% relative humidity, with pH variations within ±0.1 units. Conclusion: Electrolyte properties, including conductivity, viscosity, polymer matrix structure, and plasticizer content, are critical determinants of electrochemical reinforcement efficiency and environmental resilience. Optimized green electrolytes provide uniform substrate stabilization, corrosion mitigation, and adaptability to environmental variations, offering a sustainable, efficient alternative to conventional electrolytes for structural reinforcement applications.

title: Long-Term Dispatch Method for Electro-Hydrogen Coupled Microgrids Considering a Tiered Carbon Trading Mechanism
summary: Electro-hydrogen coupled microgrids (EHCMs), in which water electrolyzers, hydrogen fuel cells, and power-electronic converters act as cascaded electromagnetic–electrochemical energy conversion interfaces, significantly enhance the renewabl
content: Electro-hydrogen coupled microgrids (EHCMs), in which water electrolyzers, hydrogen fuel cells, and power-electronic converters act as cascaded electromagnetic–electrochemical energy conversion interfaces, significantly enhance the renewable energy hosting capacity and flexible regulation capability of distributed energy systems through cross-temporal energy conversion and dynamic power regulation. However, few studies have addressed the medium-to-long-term operational optimization of EHCMs under carbon trading mechanisms. This paper proposes a medium-to-long-term low-carbon economic dispatch framework for EHCMs incorporating a tiered carbon trading mechanism. First, a tiered carbon trading model based on hierarchical pricing is established, in which differentiated carbon price brackets strengthen the low-carbon dispatch incentives of EHCMs and maximize their emission reduction potential. Second, a typical-day scenario generation method based on spectral joint clustering is introduced; exploiting eigen-decomposition of the normalized graph Laplacian—a spectral analysis technique sharing its mathematical foundation with modal decomposition methods widely used in computational electromagnetics—the method preserves the key statistical and temporal characteristics of multi-energy time series while significantly reducing the dimensionality of the long-term optimization problem. Subsequently, a medium-to-long-term operational optimization model of EHCMs is constructed, comprehensively considering electricity, heat, natural-gas, and hydrogen balance constraints. With the objective of minimizing the annual operating cost, the model reveals cross-seasonal hydrogen storage operation strategies for electro-hydrogen coupled micro-energy networks. Case studies of a large-scale microgrid in Shanxi, China, verify the effectiveness of the proposed method in enhancing system economics and reducing carbon emissions.

title: Optimal Configuration Strategy of Electricity–Hydrogen Coupled Rural Microgrid Considering Long-Term Hydrogen Storage Characteristics
summary: The limited flexibility of rural microgrids in accommodating long-term renewable energy fluctuations poses a major challenge to achieving low-carbon and cost-effective operation. To address this issue, an optimal configuration strategy for
content: The limited flexibility of rural microgrids in accommodating long-term renewable energy fluctuations poses a major challenge to achieving low-carbon and cost-effective operation. To address this issue, an optimal configuration strategy for an electricity–hydrogen coupled rural microgrid (EH-RM) system is developed, considering the long-term operational characteristics of hydrogen storage. Firstly, detailed models of key energy conversion and storage devices, including electrolyzers, fuel cells, combined heat and power (CHP) units, and hydrogen storage tanks, are established to capture multi-energy coupling relationships among electricity, heat, gas, and hydrogen. Then, a bilevel optimization framework is proposed, where the upper-level capacity configuration model minimizes the annualized total cost, and the lower-level scheduling model minimizes daily operating cost under multi-energy balance constraints. Subsequently, a Benders decomposition–based algorithm is employed to decouple capacity planning and operational scheduling, iteratively generating feasibility and optimality cuts to ensure convergence and computational efficiency. Finally, case study results show that the proposed bilevel configuration model effectively reduces the total system cost and carbon emissions in rural applications, demonstrating its economic efficiency and low-carbon advantages for rural integrated scenarios.

title: Genotypic and environmental effects on seed coat patterning and nutritional composition in common bean (Phaseolus vulgaris L.)
source: Journal of Agriculture and Food Research
summary: : Common bean ( Phaseolus vulgaris L.) is the leading grain legume consumed directly by humans and a primary source of nutrients in many communities. This study utilized common bean genotypes with diverse seed coat phenotypes to investigate
content: : Common bean ( Phaseolus vulgaris L.) is the leading grain legume consumed directly by humans and a primary source of nutrients in many communities. This study utilized common bean genotypes with diverse seed coat phenotypes to investigate genotypic and environmental effects on pigmented seed coat area and seed macronutrient (protein, starch, fat, ash, moisture), anti-nutrient (phytate), and mineral nutrient (iron, zinc, calcium, phosphorus, magnesium, potassium, sodium) profiles. Recombinant inbred lines (RILs) that comprise six phenotypic classes for seed coat patterning and nine commercial cultivars were field-evaluated for multiple years across inland, coastal, and intermountain environments in California. A custom near-infrared spectroscopy calibration had improved performance for macronutrients relative to a pre-existing calibration. Environmental effects on macronutrients in this data set were pronounced; the 2022 coastal growing environment was the most distinct, characterized by significantly higher starch and moisture content and significantly lower protein content in the RILs relative to any other environments. Across growing years in the RILs, greater consistency was observed at the inland site, where only protein was significantly different; all macronutrient traits significantly differed within the intermountain site. Certain commercial cultivars largely maintained their relative rank for protein content across environments, indicating consistency of genotypic performance, and Black Nightfall ranked among the highest for iron, zinc, phosphorus, and magnesium. Percent pigmented seed coat area was significantly negatively correlated with both calcium and magnesium concentrations. These results underscore the importance of continued multi-environment field trials to understand, and leverage in crop improvement, the genetic and environmental basis of seed coat patterning, seed nutritional composition, and their interplay within and among market classes of common bean.

title: Taguchi-optimized palmyra palm shell activated carbon for mitigating CO, HC, and NOx emissions in a fixed-bed motorcycle exhaust system
source: South African Journal of Chemical Engineering
summary: Air pollution from motor vehicle exhaust remains a critical environmental challenge in developing countries, including Indonesia, due to emissions of toxic gases such as CO, HC, and NOx. This study investigated the potential of activated ca
content: Air pollution from motor vehicle exhaust remains a critical environmental challenge in developing countries, including Indonesia, due to emissions of toxic gases such as CO, HC, and NOx. This study investigated the potential of activated carbon derived from palmyra (siwalan) shell waste as a renewable and low-cost adsorbent for mitigating motorcycle exhaust emissions. Activated carbon was synthesized via chemical activation using Na₂CO₃ (15–25%) and optimized using a Taguchi-based multi-response approach. Physicochemical characterization showed that the optimized PSAC had an iodine number of 762.5 mg g⁻¹, moisture and ash contents of 5.0% and 7.5%, respectively, and a BET specific surface area of 248.45 m² g⁻¹. The optimized PSAC was integrated into a fixed-bed reactor installed on a 100 cc motorcycle to evaluate its performance in removing CO, HC, and NOx. The adsorption system achieved maximum removal efficiencies of 56.9 ± 1.4% for CO, 79.5 ± 0.2% for HC, and 42.7 ± 1.0% for NOx. The pseudo-first-order model showed the highest overall correlation (R² > 0.95; k₁ = 0.0185–0.0279 min⁻¹), suggesting adsorption behavior dominated by physisorption and film-diffusion effects. The Yoon–Nelson model adequately described the breakthrough trend, whereas the Thomas model showed lower agreement under several conditions. SEM–EDX analysis indicated that the carbon structure remained stable after adsorption, while only minor changes were observed in the FTIR spectra, supporting limited surface chemical interactions. These findings demonstrate the potential of PSAC as a sustainable carbon-based material for reducing motorcycle exhaust emissions under the investigated conditions.

title: Do soft-skills courses pay for individuals? Evidence from German matched data
source: Empirical research in vocational education and training
summary: Abstract Soft skills are widely promoted as levers for productivity and as enablers for digital and green transitions. Linking soft-skills training courses with German employer–employee records for 2010–2020, we track 5,439 full-time worker
content: Abstract Soft skills are widely promoted as levers for productivity and as enablers for digital and green transitions. Linking soft-skills training courses with German employer–employee records for 2010–2020, we track 5,439 full-time workers, including 549 participants in non-formal soft-skills training typically financed by employers. A staggered event-study design finds no post-training changes in daily wages, span of control, leadership status, or job satisfaction for up to three years. In Germany’s compressed-wage setting, where firms hold considerable monopsony power, this pattern is consistent with two interpretations: either these courses produce relatively small productivity effects, or firms capture most of any productivity gains rather than sharing them through higher pay. We discuss how portable Individual Learning Accounts and targeted subsidies could, in principle, strengthen worker returns, while acknowledging that more evidence on productivity effects is needed before drawing firm policy conclusions. JEL codes: J24; J28; J31; M53; I26

title: The physical work environment in management research: a bibliometric analysis of knowledge structures, collaboration networks, and workplace transformations
summary: Abstract This article offers a comprehensive bibliometric analysis of research on physical work environments and maps its intellectual structure, thematic evolution, and collaborative dynamics over the past four decades from a business and
content: Abstract This article offers a comprehensive bibliometric analysis of research on physical work environments and maps its intellectual structure, thematic evolution, and collaborative dynamics over the past four decades from a business and management perspective. It reveals how previously fragmented streams of research on workplace design, employee well-being, and organizational performance are embedded in the broader management literature. The analysis provides insights into how the physical work environment has evolved from a peripheral topic to a topic of strategic concern in organizational research. Based on a dataset of 834 publications indexed in Scopus and Web of Science between 1978 and 2024, it captures the contributions of 1,906 authors publishing across 214 sources. Using advanced bibliometric techniques such as co-citation analysis, keyword co-occurrence, and strategic mapping, the study reveals a transition from early concerns with office layout and facility management to more recent emphases on employee well-being, workplace design, and the impacts of COVID-19. The thematic structure shows well-developed motor themes, such as office buildings and sustainability, alongside basic themes, such as workplace, productivity, and the physical work environment. Emerging topics include coworking spaces and workplace learning, while niche areas such as indoor air quality and workplace health highlight growing specialization. The results uncover the underlying knowledge structure of physical work environment research and highlight emerging research areas related to workplace transformation, hybrid work arrangements, and employee-centered workspace design. This study provides the conceptual foundation that enables researchers to better position future workplace research.

title: How Does Fintech Drive Corporate ESG Performance? Evidence from China
summary: With climate risk and sustainable development dominating global policy agendas, a key question for regulators and researchers alike is whether and under what conditions fintech development is associated with improved corporate ESG performan
content: With climate risk and sustainable development dominating global policy agendas, a key question for regulators and researchers alike is whether and under what conditions fintech development is associated with improved corporate ESG performance. Using A-share listed firms in China from 2011 to 2024, this paper builds a city-level fintech index from Baidu News advanced search records and links it to firm-level ESG and financial data. Our baseline estimates confirm that fintech development significantly improves corporate ESG performance. This core finding remains robust across lagged regressors, an ordered logit specification, additional industry fixed effects, the exclusion of the 2020 to 2022 pandemic window, and a spherical-distance-to-Hangzhou instrumental variable. Mechanism tests reveal two complementary channels: fintech eases financing frictions and stimulates green innovation. Further analyses are conducted to explore boundary conditions. Both management shareholding and spatial competition exert direct positive effects on ESG performance, yet their interactions with fintech are significantly negative, pointing to a substitution rather than complementary relationship. Heterogeneity analysis shows that the effect is more pronounced among state-owned enterprises, large firms, non-high-tech and labor-intensive industries, growth-stage firms, and firms in the eastern region. Our results offer differentiated policy implications for strengthening digital infrastructure, refining financing arrangements for growth-stage and SMEs, and calibrating region- and life-cycle-sensitive regulatory frameworks.

title: dfeen87/AILEE-Finance-Unified-Runtime: V18 UI/UX upgrade
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: AILEE Finance Unified Runtime — Version 18.0.0 Release Notes Overview Version 18.0.0 marks the formal transition of AILEE Finance Unified Runtime from prototype‑grade interface components to a fully hardened, institutional‑grade execution e
content: AILEE Finance Unified Runtime — Version 18.0.0 Release Notes Overview Version 18.0.0 marks the formal transition of AILEE Finance Unified Runtime from prototype‑grade interface components to a fully hardened, institutional‑grade execution environment. This release unifies the upgraded UI/UX architecture with the deterministic, multi‑layer governance system introduced in V17, delivering a stable, data‑dense, and operationally robust interface suitable for real‑time financial execution, cross‑asset evaluation, and stack integration at institutional scale. Institutional UI/UX Upgrade The dashboard under ailee_plugins/plugins/dashboard/ has been elevated into the authoritative institutional interface for AILEE. The UI now operates as a zero‑dependency HTML/CSS/JS system, optimized for deterministic rendering and ultra‑low‑latency environments. Key Enhancements High‑density Bloomberg‑style panel system Modular, compact, and information‑rich panels for governance state, execution pipeline status, deterministic state machine outputs, WNFS ingestion health, and fail‑closed indicators. Cross‑Asset Evaluation Grid Side‑by‑side comparison across Equities, FX, Crypto, Commodities, Derivatives, and Synthetic Instruments, with class‑specific filters and real‑time metric updates. Deterministic Visualizations Lightweight Canvas/SVG components delivering 60fps real‑time charts for latency distributions (p50/p99/p99.9), decision throughput, liquidity anomalies, reconciliation breaches, and governance transitions. Developer Integration & Runtime Lab A new sandbox module enabling engineers to inject state signals (sequence gaps, stress overrides, price shocks), trigger execution cycles, and inspect deterministic JSON traces and ABI structures. Governance & Determinism Alignment All UI components now adhere to the same deterministic principles as the core runtime: Unified naming conventions across modules Locked rendering paths for predictable behavior Zero dynamic heap allocation on hot visual paths Strict latency ceilings for institutional monitoring Hardened state indicators for STRESS_OVERRIDE and META_LOCKED This ensures the interface reflects the exact behavior of the 19‑layer governance architecture without drift or ambiguity. Institutional Aesthetic AILEE now presents a dark, high‑contrast institutional theme with: Monospace data rows Structured borders Neon state accents (cyan/green operational, amber advisory, crimson fail‑closed) Clear typography hierarchy for long‑duration monitoring The interface is designed to feel at home on a trading floor, risk desk, or execution environment. Versioning Update The entire codebase has been advanced to Version 18.0.0, marking the beginning of AILEE's institutional era. This release hardens the UI/UX layer, aligns it with the unified governance architecture, and establishes a stable foundation for future expansions in cross‑asset evaluation, deterministic visualization, and institutional integration.

title: Green finance–digital supply chain synergy and international logistics trade efficiency: evidence from China's Jing-Jin-Ji urban agglomeration
source: Journal of Applied Economics and Policy Studies
summary: This paper examines the impact of green finance–digital supply chain synergy on international logistics trade efficiency in the Jing-Jin-Ji region and explores the underlying mechanisms. Using panel data for 13 cities from 2013 to 2024, thi
content: This paper examines the impact of green finance–digital supply chain synergy on international logistics trade efficiency in the Jing-Jin-Ji region and explores the underlying mechanisms. Using panel data for 13 cities from 2013 to 2024, this study constructs green finance and digital supply chain indices based on the entropy weight method and measures their synergy using a coupling coordination degree model. International logistics trade efficiency is estimated through a super-efficiency DEA model, and a fixed-effects model is employed for empirical analysis. The results show that green finance, digital supply chains and their synergistic development exhibit an overall upward trend despite regional disparities. Green finance–digital supply chain synergy significantly improves international logistics trade efficiency, with stronger effects observed in regions with higher levels of development. Further analysis reveals that resource allocation efficiency and digital financial inclusion serve as important transmission channels. These findings provide new evidence on the role of financial and digital synergies in enhancing logistics performance and offer policy implications for promoting coordinated regional development and high-quality trade growth.

title: Ground family education explanation based on visibility graph of complex network by temporal community division
summary: Introduction Family education directly shapes adolescents’ positive behavioral habits, moral character, and cultural refinement, making it a critical component of their healthy development. With AI technology evolving at such a fast pace, s
content: Introduction Family education directly shapes adolescents’ positive behavioral habits, moral character, and cultural refinement, making it a critical component of their healthy development. With AI technology evolving at such a fast pace, search engines and social media platforms constantly generate vast amounts of data. Analyzing these data provides a quick understanding of the public’s attention to family education and how the characteristics of that attention have evolved over time, and this is critical for policy intervention and decision-making in family education. Methods The visibility graph (VG) has proven effective for nonlinear time series analysis in a range of real-world settings. Given the significant temporal fluctuations and nonlinear characteristics of public attention, this study utilized 1,882 daily observations of the comprehensive index for “family education” on Douyin, covering the period from January 1, 2021, to 25 February 2026, and mapped these data onto a natural visibility graph comprising 1,882 nodes and 3,738 edges, in order to examine its underlying complex network metrics. Subsequently, the greedy modularity optimization (Greedy Modularity Optimisation) algorithm was employed to resolve the internal community structure of the network. Finally, the evolutionary trend of public attention to family education over time was elucidated by combining the temporal features of each community with their cross-seasonal variation patterns. Meanwhile, to mitigate potential methodological limitation, the above descriptive findings were further subjected to formal statistical testing and robustness analyses: first, confirmatory maximum-likelihood analysis of the degree distribution was conducted; second, a null-model comparisons were performed; third, bootstrap confidence intervals were estimated and a modularity permutation test was carried out; fourth, sensitivity of community-detection algorithms and resolution-parameters was assessed; and fifth, a parallel analysis of the Search Index was performed. Results The family education composite network exhibits significant non-random structural properties: its degree distribution follows a heavy-tailed form (with a finite-size cutoff rather than a pure power law), alongside small-world clustering and a remarkably high modularity index (Q > 0.9066). These findings are robustly supported by confirmatory maximum likelihood estimation, Kolmogorov-Smirnov tests, and multiple sensitivity analyses. Notably, the network’s community dynamics display clear temporal rhythms, correlating not only with the academic year cycle, the phased implementation of the “Double Reduction” policy, and the enactment of the Preschool Education Law, but also with seasonal patterns (permutation test p = 0.0001; Cramér’s V = 0.591). This temporal structure is further corroborated by a parallel search index analysis, strengthening the credibility of our conclusions. Discussion These findings suggest that the visibil

title: The bright side of big data: the role of data literacy in mitigating negative effects on task performance
summary: Abstract While the proliferation of Big Data (BD) increasingly pressures task execution in the workplace, the underlying socio-cognitive pathways linking data demands to worker performance remain fragmented. The objective of this research i
content: Abstract While the proliferation of Big Data (BD) increasingly pressures task execution in the workplace, the underlying socio-cognitive pathways linking data demands to worker performance remain fragmented. The objective of this research is to analyze the effect of BD on Task Performance (TP), investigating the mediating roles of Cognitive Overload (CO), Avoidance Behavior (AB), and Data Literacy (DL), and the moderating role of DL in mitigating the negative effects of AB on TP. Grounded in the Situation-Organism-Behavior-Consequence (SOBC) and Job Demands-Resources (JD-R) models, this study surveyed 372 data workers in Brazil, analyzing empirical data using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). We discovered a dual-pathway mechanism influencing TP. The deterioration process operates as a negative loop where CO and AB deplete professional energy, whereas the motivational path triggers DL mobilization to enhance performance. Mediation indicates that DL and AB are significant intermediaries, while moderation indicates that DL buffers AB’s detrimental impact on TP. Specific triggers include Veracity as a cognitive anchor and Velocity as an engagement catalyst. Theoretically, this research highlights how data characteristics shape cognitive states and positions DL as a key resource for sociocognitive resilience. For practice, identifies DL as the strategic priority for organizational intervention to optimize performance. Socially, the study promotes well-being by identifying mechanisms that translate informational complexity into professional effectiveness. The study’s originality lies in explaining the critical tension surrounding the BD, showing that while its demands can lead to exhaustion (dark side), they also mobilize resources that catalyze resilience (bright side).

title: Quantifying audience perceptions of holographic displays in museums using neurophysiological measures (EEG)
summary: Abstract This study combined electroencephalography (EEG) and questionnaire measures to assess cognitive and emotional engagement with three museum display formats: holograms, photographs, and 3D-printed artefacts. Twenty-four adults (aged
content: Abstract This study combined electroencephalography (EEG) and questionnaire measures to assess cognitive and emotional engagement with three museum display formats: holograms, photographs, and 3D-printed artefacts. Twenty-four adults (aged 18–55 years) viewed the exhibits in a simulated museum environment while neural activity and self-reported immersion (IEQ-SF) were recorded. Holographic displays were associated with lower delta and alpha power and higher theta activity than the other display formats, indicating distinct patterns of EEG activity during viewing. Subjective immersion scores were significantly higher for holograms than for 3D-printed models and photographs, while 3D-printed models also scored higher than photographs. The EEG and questionnaire findings suggest that holographic presentation was associated with greater perceived immersion and attentional engagement, although the findings should not be interpreted as causal evidence. This study demonstrates a neurophysiological and self-report approach for evaluating audience responses to immersive display technologies in controlled museum settings.

title: Urbanization and Peri-Urban Household Food Security: Evidence from Faisalabad, Pakistan
source: Journal of Agricultural Policy and Transformation
summary: Unplanned urbanization is reshaping the rural–urban interface of Pakistani cities, converting agricultural land into housing and pressuring food systems. This study examines the association between urbanization and food security in peri-urb
content: Unplanned urbanization is reshaping the rural–urban interface of Pakistani cities, converting agricultural land into housing and pressuring food systems. This study examines the association between urbanization and food security in peri-urban Faisalabad, Pakistan’s textile hub. Using a random sample of 160 households from settlements located 2–14 km from city center, food security was assessed through a seven-day dietary recall against 2,350 kcal per adult equivalent per day. Binary logistic regression identified socioeconomic and locational correlates of food security, using migrant status and distance from city center as proxies for urbanization exposure. Results indicate that 26% of households were food insecure, with the highest prevalence in the settlement closest to city center. Both urbanization proxies were negatively associated with food security, although neither relationship was statistically significant. Headship age of 46 years and above was significantly and negatively associated with food security, while income, number of earners, and education of the household head were positively associated with food security. Household size showed a negative but partly significant relationship, whereas joint family structure showed a positive association that approached but did not reach significance. The study recommends agricultural zoning, land governance, and livelihood diversification to safeguard food security in peri-urban areas.

title: The Green Economy
summary: This chapter establishes the theoretical foundations of the green economy by treating it as an evolving policy paradigm rather than a fixed blueprint. It explains how shifting constraint framings—resource scarcity, ecological limits, financ
content: This chapter establishes the theoretical foundations of the green economy by treating it as an evolving policy paradigm rather than a fixed blueprint. It explains how shifting constraint framings—resource scarcity, ecological limits, financial instability, climate risk, and geopolitical competition—have repeatedly reordered policy priorities and instrument choices. Drawing on environmental economics, ecological economics, transition and innovation studies, governance theory, and mission-oriented industrial policy, this chapter distils four recurring design trade-offs: efficiency versus sufficiency; market correction versus system transformation; speed versus legitimacy; and credibility versus flexibility in standards, taxonomies, and transition finance. It then compares major models of green economy action and shows how each carries distinct mechanisms of change, evaluation criteria, and vulnerabilities, from rebound effects to greenwashing and uneven burden sharing. By linking market failures with systemic shortcomings and mapping alternative transition pathways across political economies, this chapter equips readers with a practical framework for diagnosing feasibility conditions, anticipating distributional conflict, and assessing whether strategies deliver absolute environmental improvement alongside durable social outcomes.

title: Institutional Fragility and the Conditional Transferability of Green Hydrogen Strategy Across the Middle East and North Africa (MENA): Heterogeneous Burdens, Shared Mechanism
summary: Green hydrogen strategies proliferate across developing economies, yet most assume the planning authority possesses the state capacity, regulatory autonomy, and investment conditions that conflict-affected and fragile economies lack. Whethe
content: Green hydrogen strategies proliferate across developing economies, yet most assume the planning authority possesses the state capacity, regulatory autonomy, and investment conditions that conflict-affected and fragile economies lack. Whether a strategy logic derived in one such context transfers to others with different institutional capacity remains untested. This study develops a Conflict-Affected Energy Transitions (CAET) framework and empirically examines its barrier gradient and conditional transferability propositions, analyzing at the country level a regional expert survey—data that prior single-case work, including the authors’ own, used only for binary external validation. A total of 137 energy experts across seventeen Arab states are grouped into three institutional clusters—conflict-affected/fragile, stable developing, and Gulf/high-capacity—and examined through cluster barrier and readiness profiles, a perceived-versus-predictive importance comparison, hierarchical clustering, and a Mode-A partial-least-squares path model with measurement invariance (MICOM) testing and permutation-based multi-group analysis. Energy justice and sovereignty are used as analytical and interpretive lenses, not as measured latent constructs in the structural model. Results show that barrier burdens follow a monotonic institutional fragility gradient: regulatory/institutional barriers rise from 3.02 (Gulf) through 3.52 (stable) to 4.06 (fragile), where they are the most severe constraint. Moreover, the perceived–predictive divergence—social barriers are rated least severe yet associate most strongly with sustainability—recurs across the region. In addition, the model satisfies compositional invariance across fragile and stable clusters while equality of regulatory means and variances fails as expected, and no structural path differs detectably between them at the current sample size. The adoption–governance–sustainability mechanism is therefore provisionally comparable rather than definitively invariant. We propose conditional transferability: the mechanism travels, provisionally, while priorities must be re-weighted by institutional context. Policy implications are differentiated—institutions-first, community-scale pathways for fragile states; finance and market formation for stable developing states; export-scale deployment for high-capacity states—and the CAET framework offers a generalizable alternative to techno-economic determinism for hydrogen strategy under constrained sovereignty. In practical terms, energy ministries in fragile states should sequence rule-making, permitting authority, and community-scale pilots before committing deployment capital; stable developing states should concentrate on de-risking finance and forming early offtake markets; and high-capacity states can proceed directly to export-scale projects and regional standard setting.

title: Human-centered security in practice: evidence from Y-FIT Ghana on privacy, trust, and youth engagement in health technology system HIV prevention
summary: Health technology systems (HTS) increasingly mediate health-related communication and decision-making, yet security is often conceptualized primarily as a technical property rather than as a socially situated user experience. This study exa
content: Health technology systems (HTS) increasingly mediate health-related communication and decision-making, yet security is often conceptualized primarily as a technical property rather than as a socially situated user experience. This study examined how adolescents and young adults in Ghana imagined, prioritized, and articulated requirements related to privacy, trust, and safe digital engagement in HIV prevention contexts. Data were drawn from the Open Call phase of the Y-FIT Ghana study, a national crowdsourcing initiative involving 103 youth aged 15–24 years. Of the submissions received, 72 that proposed digital or digitally mediated strategies for HIV prevention and care were included in the analysis. Using qualitative content analysis, we identified recurring patterns in participants' proposed strategies and design expectations. Participants consistently prioritized privacy and confidentiality as conditions they associated with anticipated willingness to engage, particularly because of stigma, social visibility, and fear of unintended disclosure. Trust was linked to peer influence, relatable communication, cultural resonance, transparency, and non-judgmental interaction rather than to institutional authority alone. Participants also favored systems that supported discreet access, simplified communication, anonymous questioning, and guided service navigation. Because the data comprised proposed strategies rather than observed system use, the findings should be interpreted as youth-generated perceptions and anticipated engagement rather than demonstrated behavior. The findings suggest that human-centered security in stigma-sensitive digital health settings should extend beyond technical safeguards to incorporate social exposure, relational trust, usability, and culturally responsive design.

title: Digital-Green Integration as a Catalyst for Urban Ecological Resilience: Evidence from Chinese Provinces
summary: China’s smart-city and green-transition policies have made digital-green integration an important pathway for improving urban ecological resilience. This study examines whether digital-green integration enhances urban ecological resilience,
content: China’s smart-city and green-transition policies have made digital-green integration an important pathway for improving urban ecological resilience. This study examines whether digital-green integration enhances urban ecological resilience, through which channels this effect occurs, and under what regional conditions it becomes more pronounced. The analysis uses a balanced panel of 510 observations for 30 Chinese provincial-level regions from 2005 to 2021, compiled from national and provincial statistical yearbooks. An indicator system encompassing resistance, recovery, and renewal is used to assess urban ecological resilience, and the composite index is calculated using the entropy-weighting method. Digital–green integration is captured by a coupling coordination index linking digital infrastructure with green finance. Its effect is estimated within a two-way fixed-effects framework, with additional tests used to assess the robustness of the findings and explore the underlying mechanisms, moderating conditions, and regional differences. The results show that: (1) digital–green integration significantly enhances urban ecological resilience, with its effect concentrated primarily in the recovery dimension; (2) industrial-structure upgrading and improvements in energy efficiency serve as important transmission channels, while better traffic infrastructure further strengthens this positive relationship; and (3) the effect is more pronounced in provinces with lower levels of urbanization and stronger environmental regulation. Governments should promote digital-green integration to support industrial-structure upgrading and energy-efficiency improvement, thereby strengthening cities’ capacity to recover from ecological shocks. Greater support should be directed to less urbanized regions, while areas with weaker environmental regulation should improve disclosure, verification, and enforcement. Future research could employ city-level data and spatial econometric models to examine the magnitude, geographic reach, and transmission mechanisms of cross-regional spillovers.

title: FROM SOFT GUIDANCE TO REAL EMISSION REDUCTION: IMPLEMENTATION STATUS AND EFFECT EVALUATION OF ENERGY SAVING INCENTIVE POLICIES FOR CHINESE ENTERPRISES
summary: Enterprises are the main energy users in China. Their saving behaviour decides whether national efficiency targets can be reached. Over the past four decades China has built an incentive system for enterprise energy saving. The system now c
content: Enterprises are the main energy users in China. Their saving behaviour decides whether national efficiency targets can be reached. Over the past four decades China has built an incentive system for enterprise energy saving. The system now contains fiscal subsidies, tax relief, green finance, market mechanisms and credit assessment. This paper reviews how the system evolved and how well it works in practice. A five layer analytical framework is proposed. The framework links policy input, delivery channel, firm response, outcome and feedback in one chain. A scoring system with fifteen indicators is designed for the macro level and the micro level. Policy texts, official statistics and published programme lists from 1980 to 2025 are compiled. The results show clear aggregate gains. National energy intensity fell by more than 26 percent against the 2015 level, and more than 3000 national green factories were certified. The results also show a structural gap. The take up rate of subsidy and green finance among small and micro firms stays below 35 percent. Marginal returns of the classic subsidy model are falling. Four optimisation paths are proposed for layered design, agency coordination, full cycle supervision and market based incentives.

title: Goodwill Bubbles in Emerging Markets: Can Clan Culture Serve as an Informal Circuit Breaker?
summary: This paper takes Chinese A-share listed companies from 2012 to 2024 as the research sample to examine the governance effect of clan culture, a local informal institution, on excess goodwill from mergers and acquisitions (M&As). The study fi
content: This paper takes Chinese A-share listed companies from 2012 to 2024 as the research sample to examine the governance effect of clan culture, a local informal institution, on excess goodwill from mergers and acquisitions (M&As). The study finds that enterprises located in regions with a stronger clan culture have a significantly lower level of excess goodwill generated in M&As. Mechanism tests reveal that clan culture operates through two channels: by easing financing constraints, it curbs managers’ incentive to signal growth via high-premium acquisitions, thereby reducing M&A premiums; and by attracting analyst coverage and improving information transparency, it mitigates managerial opportunism in M&A pricing. The moderating effect test shows that digital transformation amplifies the governance role of clan culture by improving the enforceability of reputation-based constraints, while family control weakens this effect by alienating clan networks and turning them into instruments for private benefit heterogeneity analysis reveals that the mitigating effect is more pronounced for non-state-owned enterprises, firms with lower audit quality, M&As with performance commitments, non-green M&A transactions, firms with limited M&A experience, firms in the decline stage of their life cycle, and firms located in southern China. Economic consequence tests demonstrate that by suppressing excess goodwill, clan culture significantly enhances firms’ long-term market value, improves future performance stability, reduces financial distress risk, and promotes stronger social responsibility performance.

title: Literacy Model of Pre-Retirement Financial Governance Based on Sundanese Social and Cultural Accounting for Teachers and Education Personnel
summary: Background. Financial readiness ahead of retirement is a strategic issue as changes in income, increasing health needs, and economic uncertainty can affect the well-being of individuals and families. In Indonesia, the financial literacy ind
content: Background. Financial readiness ahead of retirement is a strategic issue as changes in income, increasing health needs, and economic uncertainty can affect the well-being of individuals and families. In Indonesia, the financial literacy index has increased, but the gap between literacy and inclusion and low literacy in the pension sector indicate that access to financial services has not been fully followed by the ability to use them appropriately. Aims. This community service aims to develop and implement a pre-retirement financial governance literacy model that integrates financial literacy, social accounting, and Sundanese cultural values for teachers and education staff. Methods. The activity was held on June 22, 2026 at SMA Pasundan 2 Bandung City with the involvement of 30 participants, consisting of 24 teachers and 6 education staff. The approach used was participatory empowerment based on adult education through needs identification, material preparation, interactive workshops, case discussions, reflection, and descriptive evaluation. Result. The results showed that participants gained a more comprehensive understanding of pre-retirement financial planning, asset management, emergency funds, investments, and financial protection. The integration of social accounting expands the orientation of financial management from individual interests to family responsibility and social sustainability, while the values of mutual honing, mutual love, mutual nurture and Tri Tangtu provide a cultural context for the formation of financial behavior. The program's novelty lies in integrating these three dimensions in the Financial Literacy–Social Accounting–Sundanese Local Wisdom (FLSA) Model. Conclusion. This model has the potential to be replicated, but its long-term effectiveness still needs to be tested through longitudinal quantitative evaluation.

title: Rethinking urban agriculture futures in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania: evidence from a rapidly urbanizing city in the global south
summary: Urban agriculture (UA) remains an important but unevenly governed part of urban food systems in many rapidly urbanizing cities of the Global South. Existing research has documented its contribution to food access, livelihoods and urban resi
content: Urban agriculture (UA) remains an important but unevenly governed part of urban food systems in many rapidly urbanizing cities of the Global South. Existing research has documented its contribution to food access, livelihoods and urban resilience, but less attention has been given to locally grounded pathways for supporting UA in African cities. This paper examines the current landscape and possible future trajectories of UA in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania. Using an exploratory qualitative case-study and policy-analysis approach, the study draws on targeted literature and document review, a policy and regulatory scan, and 52 key informant interviews conducted between April and September 2025 with municipal actors, urban farmers and food-system practitioners. The findings show that UA is valued for household food supplementation, small-scale income generation and fresh-food provisioning, particularly through short-cycle vegetable production close to consumers. However, it remains shaped by tolerated informality, insecure land access, fragmented regulation, contamination risks, weak institutional coordination and pressure on peri-urban land. Based on the combined analysis, the paper proposes five evidence-informed trajectories: managed river-corridor cultivation; sacks, buckets and roofs for dense-ward micro-production; institutional land clusters; peri-urban foodshed belts with circular-resource hubs; and small-scale aquaculture and insect-based feed systems. These pathways are not presented as tested feasibility models, but as differentiated options requiring further technical, environmental, spatial and economic assessment. The paper argues that the future of UA in cities such as Dar es Salaam is unlikely to depend on a single large-scale model, but on risk-sensitive and institutionally grounded forms of support that align food access, livelihoods, public health and urban planning.

title: The Ontology of Transformational Risk
summary: This chapter develops an ontological reconstruction of climate and regulatory risk within the framework of green finance. It argues that transformational risk cannot be adequately understood through variance-based, mean-centred models domin
content: This chapter develops an ontological reconstruction of climate and regulatory risk within the framework of green finance. It argues that transformational risk cannot be adequately understood through variance-based, mean-centred models dominant in classical financial theory. Instead, climate-related and regulatory risks are conceptualised as endogenous, processual, and regime-dependent phenomena that alter the underlying structure of the financial system rather than merely affecting its parameters. This chapter distinguishes between parametric changes in risk and structural transformations of the data-generating process, emphasising non-stationarity, regime shifts, and the concentration of losses at transition points. Drawing on regime-switching theory, financial instability theory, and literature on tail risk, it demonstrates that transformational risk manifests not through gradual increases in volatility but through discontinuities in expectations, regulatory credibility, and technological trajectories. Time is treated not as a neutral analytical horizon but as a constitutive dimension of risk, shaping the sequencing and concentration of financial losses. The analysis further highlights the role of information, regulatory credibility, and supervisory institutions in structuring the perception and materialisation of risk. By embedding climate risk within institutional and regime-dependent dynamics, this chapter provides the conceptual foundation for the subsequent examination of financial decision-making under structural uncertainty.
